grammar.point: Accidental se: se me cayó, se me rompió, se me olvidó
grammar.explain: Se + me / te / le + verb says something happened to you by accident; the verb agrees with the thing, not the person.
grammar.trap: English says 'I dropped it'; Spanish says it 'fell on me', so the verb follows the thing: se me cayeron las llaves (plural).

grammar.point: se with things that break or stop
grammar.explain: Things that stop working or run out take se + the preterite: se descompuso, se fue la luz, se acabó el gas.

examples.es: Se acabó el agua del garrafón.
examples.en: The water jug has run out.

grammar.trap: descomponerse is for machines that stop working; romperse is for things that break or tear: se rompió el vaso, se descompuso la lavadora.

grammar.explain: ¿Me puede + infinitive? asks someone, politely, to do something for you.

examples.en: Can you send me a plumber?
Can you tell me how much it costs?

grammar.trap: Mexicans usually keep the a before a person, even an unspecified one: mandar a un plomero.

grammar.explain: Hay que + infinitive says what needs doing, without saying who.

examples.en: We need to call the gas company.

grammar.trap: hay que never changes: hay que pagar, not hay que pagamos; pronouns go on the end: hay que cambiarlo.

grammar.explain: To say something doesn't work, use no sirve (everyday) or no funciona.
grammar.trap: servir also means 'to serve' and 'to be useful': no sirve para nada = it's useless.

pronunciation: Regular past forms are stressed on the last syllable: se me ca-YÓ, se rom-PIÓ, se a-ca-BÓ; irregular ones are not: se des-com-PU-so, se FUE la luz.
Say bóiler the Spanish way, BÓI-ler, with a tapped r, and foco with two clear o's: FO-co.

common_errors.why: Accidents use se + me + verb.
The verb agrees with the thing that fell.
Machines that stop working se descomponen.
hay que takes the infinitive.

units.culture: Hot water usually comes from a gas boiler and gas from a delivered tank or cylinder, so 'no hot water' often means the gas has run out or the pilot light has gone out. Water is stored in a rooftop tinaco or a cistern, and tap water isn't for drinking. Repairs go through the casero or casera, who sends a plumber or electrician; electricity is billed by the CFE, usually every two months for homes.
recycles: a1-12: No hay agua caliente. / Mi casero vive abajo. / ¡Un garrafón, por favor!
a1-15: Se me olvidó la cartera.
units.evidence: The learner reports two faults with the right construction (se fue la luz, se descompuso …, no sirve …), says one thing happened by accident with se me + a preterite that agrees with the thing, asks for a repair with ¿me puede mandar a …?, and asks ¿para cuándo queda?
sources: PCIC Gram. B2 (accidental se: moved down); Tác. B2 (se me rompió); Func. B2 (¿para cuándo estará?)
PCIC NE B1–B2 (housing: descompuesto, prender / apagar, recibo de luz CFE, gas); NE C1 (se fue la luz, tinaco)
WP (se fue la luz, fuga, plomero, no sirve, descompuesto)
PCIC Saberes (gas trucks, tinaco, boiler de gas)
Books: none at A2 (gap)

units.title: Before and now
units.can_do: Say what things used to be like, what you used to do, and how your life has changed since you came.
situations: telling a neighbour how your life has changed
hearing how the colonia used to be

frames.es: Antes no hablaba español. Ahora hablo un poco.
frames.en: I didn't use to speak Spanish. Now I speak a little.

frames.es: Antes vivía en otro país; ahora vivo aquí.
frames.en: I used to live in another country; now I live here.

frames.es: Antes cenaba mucho; ahora como fuerte a las tres.
frames.en: I used to have a big dinner; now I have my main meal at three.
frames.note: comer fuerte = to have a big meal.

frames.es: Antes trabajaba mucho; ahora tengo más tiempo.
frames.en: I used to work a lot; now I have more time.

frames.es: Antes esta colonia era muy tranquila.
frames.en: This neighbourhood used to be very quiet.

frames.es: Aquí había un mercado.
frames.en: There used to be a market here.

frames.es: Cuando era niño, iba a la escuela caminando.
frames.en: When I was a child, I used to walk to school.
frames.note: A woman says: Cuando era niña…

frames.es: ¿Qué hacía antes de venir a México?
frames.en: What did you do before coming to Mexico?
frames.note: To a friend: ¿Qué hacías antes de venir?

model_exchanges.situation: A neighbour asks how your life has changed

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: ¿Y qué hacía usted antes de venir a México?
lines.en: And what did you do before coming to Mexico?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Trabajaba en una oficina. Trabajaba mucho y casi no tenía tiempo.
lines.en: I worked in an office. I worked a lot and hardly had any time.

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: ¿Y ahora?
lines.en: And now?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Ahora tengo más tiempo. Camino mucho y voy al mercado.
lines.en: Now I have more time. I walk a lot and go to the market.

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: ¿Y no extraña su país?
lines.en: And don't you miss your country?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: A veces, pero aquí estoy muy a gusto.
lines.en: Sometimes, but I'm very happy here.

model_exchanges.situation: Hearing how the colonia used to be

lines.speaker: doña Carmen
lines.es: Cuando yo era joven, esta colonia era muy tranquila.
lines.en: When I was young, this neighbourhood was very quiet.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿De veras? ¿Y cómo era?
lines.en: Really? And what was it like?

lines.speaker: doña Carmen
lines.es: No había tantos carros. Los niños jugaban en la calle.
lines.en: There weren't so many cars. The children used to play in the street.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y aquí qué había?
lines.en: And what was here?

lines.speaker: doña Carmen
lines.es: Aquí había un mercado. Todos los domingos veníamos con mi mamá.
lines.en: There used to be a market here. Every Sunday we came with my mother.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Qué bonito!
lines.en: How lovely!

model_exchanges.situation: A friend notices your habits have changed

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: ¿Ya te acostumbraste a comer tan tarde?
lines.en: Have you got used to eating so late?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí. Antes cenaba mucho a las siete. Ahora como fuerte a las tres y en la noche nomás me como un pan.
lines.en: Yes. I used to have a big dinner at seven. Now I have my main meal at three and at night I just have a piece of pan dulce.

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: ¿Y el picante?
lines.en: And spicy food?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Antes no comía nada de picante; ahora le pongo salsa a todo.
lines.en: I didn't use to eat anything spicy; now I put salsa on everything.

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: ¡Ya eres de aquí!
lines.en: You're one of us now!

grammar.explain: The imperfect describes how things used to be and what you used to do: -ar verbs take -aba, -er and -ir verbs take -ía.

examples.en: I used to live, eat, have
I used to work a lot.

grammar.trap: yo and él / ella / usted share one form (hablaba), so add the subject when it's unclear: yo vivía, ella vivía.

grammar.explain: Only three verbs are irregular in the imperfect: ser (era), ir (iba) and ver (veía).

examples.en: It used to be very quiet.
I used to walk to school.
I used to watch a lot of TV.

grammar.trap: Learn era, iba and veía as they are; 'seía' and 'iía' don't exist, and iría is a different tense (would go).

grammar.explain: Había means 'there was' or 'there were', with one form for singular and plural.

examples.en: There used to be a market here.
There were a lot of trees.

grammar.trap: Use había with plurals too: había muchos carros. You'll hear habían, but don't copy it.

grammar.explain: Contrast then and now with antes + imperfect and ahora + present.

examples.es: Antes no hablaba español; ahora hablo un poco.
examples.en: I didn't use to speak Spanish; now I speak a little.

examples.es: Antes vivía en una casa; ahora vivo en un departamento.
examples.en: I used to live in a house; now I live in a flat.

grammar.trap: English 'used to' has no separate word in Spanish; the imperfect ending does the job: antes fumaba = I used to smoke.

grammar.explain: After antes de and después de, use the infinitive.
grammar.trap: Don't conjugate after the preposition: antes de venir, not antes de vine.

pronunciation: -aba is stressed on the first a of the ending: tra-ba-JA-ba, and the nosotros form gets a written accent: ha-BLÁ-ba-mos.
-ía is two syllables with the stress on í: vi-VÍ-a, te-NÍ-a, never vi-VIA.

common_errors.wrong: Antes yo vivo en otro país.
common_errors.why: Past habits and situations take the imperfect.
After antes de, use the infinitive.
había doesn't change for plural.

common_errors.wrong: Cuando era niño, fui a la escuela caminando todos los días.
common_errors.right: Cuando era niño, iba a la escuela caminando todos los días.
common_errors.why: A repeated past habit takes the imperfect.

units.culture: Older neighbours love telling how the colonia used to be (Aquí había…, Antes esto era puro campo), and asking ¿Cómo era antes? is a warm way into a conversation. Many central neighbourhoods have changed fast, with new buildings and rising rents, and long-time residents feel it; listening first goes down well.
recycles: a1-03: Llevo dos semanas en México.
a2-02: routines in the present (normalmente como a las tres)
a1-13: Me gusta mucho la comida de aquí.
units.evidence: Asked about life before Mexico, the learner gives two or three before-and-now contrasts with antes + imperfect (regular verbs and era / iba) and ahora + present, follows a neighbour's description with era and había, and uses antes de + infinitive.
sources: EeM U10 (imperfect, antes); EeM immigrants before / now texts ("Antes no hablaba español")
PCIC Gram. A2 (imperfect); Gén. B1 (how someone has changed)
ELE: none

units.title: At the doctor
units.can_do: Explain symptoms and how long you've had them, understand questions and instructions, and know where to go.
situations: a doctor's office next to a pharmacy

frames.es: ¿Qué le pasa? / ¿Qué tiene?
frames.en: What's wrong?
frames.note: The doctor's opening question.

frames.es: Tengo tos desde hace tres días.
frames.en: I've had a cough for three days.

frames.es: ¿Desde cuándo se siente así?
frames.en: How long have you been feeling like this?

frames.es: Me duele aquí, del lado derecho.
frames.en: It hurts here, on the right side.

frames.es: Me caí y me torcí el tobillo.
frames.en: I fell and twisted my ankle.

frames.es: Soy alérgica a la penicilina.
frames.en: I'm allergic to penicillin.
frames.note: A man says alérgico.

frames.es: ¿Toma algún medicamento?
frames.en: Are you taking any medication?

frames.es: Tómese esto cada ocho horas y regrese en una semana.
frames.en: Take this every eight hours and come back in a week.

frames.es: ¡Que se mejore!
frames.en: Get well soon!
frames.note: To a friend: ¡Que te mejores!

model_exchanges.situation: At the doctor's office next to a pharmacy

lines.speaker: doctora
lines.es: Pase, siéntese. ¿Qué le pasa?
lines.en: Come in, sit down. What's wrong?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Tengo tos y me duele la garganta.
lines.en: I've got a cough and my throat hurts.

lines.speaker: doctora
lines.es: ¿Desde cuándo se siente así?
lines.en: How long have you been feeling like this?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Desde hace tres días. Y anoche tuve calentura.
lines.en: For three days. And last night I had a fever.

lines.speaker: doctora
lines.es: ¿Es alérgico a algún medicamento?
lines.en: Are you allergic to any medication?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí, soy alérgico a la penicilina.
lines.en: Yes, I'm allergic to penicillin.

lines.speaker: doctora
lines.es: Muy bien. Le voy a dar otra cosa. Tómese una pastilla cada ocho horas y regrese si no se siente mejor.
lines.en: Fine. I'll give you something else. Take one tablet every eight hours and come back if you don't feel better.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Gracias, doctora.
lines.en: Thank you, doctor.

model_exchanges.situation: A twisted ankle at urgent care

lines.speaker: enfermero
lines.es: ¿Qué le pasó?
lines.en: What happened to you?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Me caí en la banqueta y me torcí el tobillo.
lines.en: I fell on the pavement and twisted my ankle.

lines.speaker: enfermero
lines.es: ¿Le duele mucho?
lines.en: Does it hurt a lot?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí, mucho. No puedo caminar.
lines.en: Yes, a lot. I can't walk.

lines.speaker: enfermero
lines.es: Vamos a tomarle una radiografía. Siéntese aquí, ahorita viene el doctor.
lines.en: We're going to take an X-ray. Sit here, the doctor will be with you shortly.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Gracias.
lines.en: Thank you.

model_exchanges.situation: A friend asks how you are

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: ¿Cómo sigues?
lines.en: How are you feeling now?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Mejor, gracias. Ya no tengo calentura.
lines.en: Better, thanks. I don't have a fever any more.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: ¡Qué bueno! ¿Fuiste al doctor?
lines.en: Good! Did you go to the doctor?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí, me dio una receta.
lines.en: Yes, he gave me a prescription.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Bueno, cuídate mucho. ¡Que te mejores!
lines.en: Well, take good care of yourself. Get well soon!

grammar.point: desde hace + time, with the present
grammar.explain: To say how long something has been going on, use the present + desde hace + time, or hace + time + que + present.

examples.es: Tengo tos desde hace tres días.
examples.en: I've had a cough for three days.

examples.es: Hace una semana que me duele la espalda.
examples.en: My back has been hurting for a week.
How long has it been hurting?

grammar.trap: English uses 'have had'; Spanish keeps the present: tengo tos desde hace…, not he tenido tos por tres días.

grammar.explain: Many accidents use a reflexive verb in the preterite: me caí, me corté, me torcí, me quemé.

examples.en: I fell over in the street.

grammar.trap: Body parts take the article, not my: me corté el dedo, not mi dedo.

grammar.explain: Doler works like gustar: me duele + one thing, me duelen + several.
grammar.trap: The body part is the subject: me duelen las rodillas, with a plural verb.

grammar.explain: Doctors give instructions as usted commands, often with se on the end: tómese, acuéstese, regrese.

examples.es: Tómese una pastilla cada ocho horas.
examples.en: Take one tablet every eight hours.

grammar.trap: Recognise the -se ending as part of the instruction to you, not someone else.

grammar.point: ¡que se mejore! as a set phrase
grammar.explain: Wishes start with que + a special verb form (the subjunctive, taught at B1); learn these as whole phrases.
grammar.trap: ¡Mejórese! is a command, not a wish; use ¡que se mejore!

pronunciation: Accident verbs are stressed on the last syllable: me ca-Í, me tor-CÍ, me cor-TÉ; without that stress they sound like the present.
ll and y sound the same in Mexico: to-BI-yo (tobillo), ca-YÓ.

common_errors.right: Tengo tos desde hace tres días.
common_errors.why: Ongoing time uses desde hace + present.
Body parts take the article.
The verb agrees with the body parts.
alérgico takes a.

units.culture: For everyday illness most people go to the consultorio next to a pharmacy, where a doctor sees you for a small fee without an appointment. Public care is the IMSS for people with formal jobs (foreign residents can also join voluntarily), the ISSSTE for state workers and IMSS-Bienestar for people without social security; many residents use private doctors or insurance. Antibiotics need a prescription; in an emergency go to urgencias or call 911.
recycles: a1-14: Me duele … / Tengo gripa y un poco de calentura / ¿Necesito receta?
units.evidence: With a doctor, the learner says what's wrong and where it hurts, gives how long with desde hace + present, reports an accident with a reflexive preterite (me caí, me torcí …), mentions an allergy, and repeats back an instruction such as cada ocho horas.
sources: EeM U16 (doctor's visit, ¡que te mejores!), U10 (doler)
PCIC Gram. A2 (desde / desde hace); Gén. B1 (medical interview); NE A1–A2 (health)
PCIC Saberes (IMSS, ISSSTE, IMSS-Bienestar, private; pharmacy doctors)
WP (consultorio, urgencias, receta)

units.title: Feelings and reactions
units.can_do: Say how you feel, ask what's wrong, and react to news with the right Mexican expression.
functions: react with joy, surprise, sympathy, resignation
situations: hearing a neighbour's good or bad news
a friend in a bad mood

frames.es: ¡Qué padre!
frames.en: That's great!
frames.note: Informal; with an older person: ¡Qué bien! / ¡Qué gusto!

frames.es: ¡Híjole!
frames.en: Oh no! / Oh boy!
frames.note: For dismay, surprise or 'that's tricky'.

frames.es: ¡No me digas! / ¿En serio?
frames.en: No way! / Really?
frames.note: To usted: ¡No me diga!

frames.es: Ay, pobrecito.
frames.en: Oh, poor thing.
frames.note: pobrecita for a woman or girl.

frames.es: Ni modo.
frames.en: Oh well, nothing to be done.
frames.note: Also to cheer someone up about something that can't be changed.

frames.es: Me da pena hablar en español.
frames.en: I'm embarrassed to speak Spanish.
frames.note: pena in Mexico usually means embarrassment or awkwardness.

frames.es: ¿Qué te pasa? ¿Estás enojado?
frames.en: What's wrong? Are you angry?
frames.note: enojado / enojada = angry.

frames.es: ¡Calma, no pasa nada!
frames.en: Relax, it's fine!

model_exchanges.situation: A neighbour's good and bad news

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: ¿Sabe qué? Mi hija se va a casar en diciembre.
lines.en: Guess what? My daughter is getting married in December.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡No me diga! ¡Qué padre! ¡Felicidades!
lines.en: No way! That's great! Congratulations!

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: Gracias. Pero, híjole, mi esposo se cayó y se rompió el brazo.
lines.en: Thanks. But oh dear, my husband fell and broke his arm.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Ay, pobrecito. ¿Cómo está?
lines.en: Oh, poor thing. How is he?

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: Ahí va, poco a poco.
lines.en: Getting there, little by little.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Bueno, que se mejore pronto.
lines.en: Well, I hope he gets better soon.

model_exchanges.situation: Admitting you're shy about speaking

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Oye, ¿por qué no hablas en la reunión?
lines.en: Hey, why don't you talk at the meeting?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Es que me da pena hablar en español. Me equivoco mucho.
lines.en: It's just that I'm embarrassed to speak Spanish. I make a lot of mistakes.

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: ¡Calma, no pasa nada! Todos te entendemos.
lines.en: Relax, it's fine! We all understand you.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿En serio?
lines.en: Really?

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Sí, hablas muy bien. ¡Échale ganas!
lines.en: Yes, you speak really well. Go for it!

model_exchanges.situation: A friend in a bad mood

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Qué te pasa? ¿Estás enojada?
lines.en: What's wrong? Are you angry?

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: No, estoy cansada. Perdí el camión y llegué tarde al trabajo.
lines.en: No, I'm tired. I missed the bus and got to work late.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Híjole. ¿Y qué te dijo tu jefe?
lines.en: Oh no. And what did your boss say?

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Nada, pero me da coraje.
lines.en: Nothing, but it makes me cross.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Ni modo. Mañana sales más temprano.
lines.en: Oh well. Tomorrow you'll leave earlier.

grammar.explain: Feelings and moods use estar: estoy cansado, contento, enojado, preocupado, nervioso.
grammar.trap: ser changes the meaning: es aburrido = he's boring, está aburrido = he's bored.

grammar.explain: ¡Qué + adjective or noun! is the quickest way to react to news.
grammar.trap: No 'how' word: ¡qué bonito! (how pretty), not ¡cómo bonito!

grammar.point: me da pena, miedo, flojera, gusto
grammar.explain: Dar + a feeling noun, with me / te / le, says what something makes you feel.

examples.en: I can't be bothered to cook.

grammar.trap: A plural cause takes dan: me dan miedo las alturas.

grammar.explain: In Mexico pena usually means embarrassment or awkwardness; for sadness about something, people also say ¡qué lástima!

examples.en: I feel awkward asking him that.

grammar.trap: embarazada means pregnant, not embarrassed; say me da pena or qué vergüenza.

vocabulary.en: oh well, nothing to be done
go for it, give it your all

pronunciation: Exclamations start high and fall: ¡Qué PA-dre! A rising ¿En serio? asks; a falling one sounds doubtful.
Híjole is stressed on the first syllable, Í-jo-le, and the j is often just a breathy h in Mexico.

common_errors.why: Moods and states use estar.
embarazada means pregnant.
A plural cause takes dan.
enfadado sounds Spanish; Mexico says enojado.

units.culture: Mexicans react to news warmly and out loud: ¡qué padre!, ¡híjole!, ¡no me digas!, pobrecito. Ni modo is the national shrug for what can't be changed. Saying me da pena hablar en español usually earns encouragement (¡échale ganas!). Anger is rarely shown openly, so a quiet no, nada can still mean someone is upset.
recycles: a2-05: preterite news (se cayó, perdí el camión)
units.evidence: When a character shares news, the learner reacts with a fitting expression (¡qué padre!, ¡híjole!, ¡no me digas!, pobrecito, ni modo), says how they feel with estar + an agreeing adjective, uses me da pena / miedo / flojera correctly, and asks ¿qué te pasa? when someone seems upset.
sources: EeM U12 (ser / estar + adjective), U13 (chat reactions), U16 (moods with estar)
PCIC Func. B1 (me da pena); Func. B2 (¡no me digas!; ¡qué le vamos a hacer! → ni modo); Tác. C1–C2 (ni modo [México]: moved down)
7K (pobrecito)
WP (me da pena, me da flojera, enojado)

units.title: Comparing places and choosing
units.can_do: Compare neighbourhoods, shops and prices, say which is best, and ask for a recommendation.

frames.es: Esta colonia es más tranquila que el centro.
frames.en: This neighbourhood is quieter than the centre.

frames.es: Aquí la renta es más barata, pero está más lejos.
frames.en: The rent's cheaper here, but it's further away.

frames.es: Hay menos tráfico que en el centro.
frames.en: There's less traffic than in the centre.

frames.es: Es la mejor taquería de la colonia.
frames.en: It's the best taquería in the neighbourhood.

frames.es: No es tan caro como pensaba.
frames.en: It's not as expensive as I thought.

frames.es: ¿Cuál colonia te gusta más?
frames.en: Which neighbourhood do you like best?
frames.note: ¿Cuál + noun? is normal in Mexico; ¿qué colonia? also works.

frames.es: ¿Cuál me recomienda?
frames.en: Which one do you recommend?
frames.note: To a friend: ¿Cuál me recomiendas?

frames.es: Está carísimo.
frames.en: It's really expensive.

model_exchanges.situation: Choosing where to live

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: ¿Y dónde vas a rentar?
lines.en: So where are you going to rent?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: No sé. ¿Cuál colonia te gusta más, la Roma o Coyoacán?
lines.en: I don't know. Which neighbourhood do you like more, Roma or Coyoacán?

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Coyoacán es más tranquila, pero la Roma es más céntrica.
lines.en: Coyoacán is quieter, but Roma is more central.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y cuál es más barata?
lines.en: And which is cheaper?

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Pues las dos están carísimas, pero en Coyoacán la renta es un poco más barata.
lines.en: Well, both are really expensive, but in Coyoacán the rent is a bit cheaper.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Entonces Coyoacán. Me gusta más la tranquilidad.
lines.en: Then Coyoacán. I prefer peace and quiet.

model_exchanges.situation: Asking for a recommendation

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Disculpe, ¿cuál taquería me recomienda?
lines.en: Excuse me, which taquería do you recommend?

lines.speaker: señor
lines.es: La de la esquina es la mejor de la colonia. Los de pastor están buenísimos.
lines.en: The one on the corner is the best in the neighbourhood. The al pastor tacos are fantastic.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Es cara?
lines.en: Is it expensive?

lines.speaker: señor
lines.es: No, es más barata que las del centro.
lines.en: No, it's cheaper than the ones in the centre.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Gracias, hoy voy a ir.
lines.en: Thanks, I'll go today.

model_exchanges.situation: Comparing prices with a friend

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: ¿Cuánto te costó la bici?
lines.en: How much did the bike cost you?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Tres mil pesos. No es tan cara como pensaba.
lines.en: Three thousand pesos. It's not as expensive as I thought.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: En el tianguis está más barata.
lines.en: It's cheaper at the street market.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿En serio? Pero en la tienda dan garantía.
lines.en: Really? But in the shop they give a guarantee.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Bueno, sí, eso es mejor.
lines.en: Well, yes, that's better.

grammar.point: Comparatives: más / menos … que, más de + number
grammar.explain: Más or menos + adjective or noun + que compares two things; before a number use más de.

examples.es: Es más tranquila que el centro.

examples.en: It costs more than a thousand pesos.

grammar.trap: Before a number, 'than' is de: más de mil pesos, not más que mil.

grammar.point: Superlatives: el / la más … de; el / la mejor … de
grammar.explain: The article + más + adjective + de picks out the top one in a group; mejor and peor go before the noun.

examples.es: Es la colonia más tranquila de la ciudad.
examples.en: It's the quietest neighbourhood in the city.

examples.es: Es la mejor taquería de la colonia.
examples.en: It's the best taquería in the neighbourhood.

examples.es: Es la peor hora para salir.
examples.en: It's the worst time to go out.

grammar.trap: 'In the neighbourhood' after a superlative is de, not en: la mejor de la colonia.

grammar.explain: Tan + adjective + como means 'as … as'; tanto / tanta / tantos / tantas + noun + como means 'as much / many … as'.

examples.es: No es tan caro como pensaba.
examples.en: It's not as expensive as I thought.

examples.es: Aquí no hay tanto ruido como en el centro.
examples.en: There isn't as much noise here as in the centre.

examples.es: No hay tantos carros como antes.
examples.en: There aren't as many cars as before.

grammar.trap: Equal comparisons use como, not que: tan grande como.

grammar.explain: -ísimo means 'extremely', and works with adverbs too.
grammar.trap: Watch the spelling: rico > riquísimo, largo > larguísimo, lejos > lejísimos.

grammar.explain: Before a noun, Mexico uses both ¿qué colonia? and ¿cuál colonia? to choose; with ser, ¿cuál es…? asks which one and ¿qué es…? asks for a definition.

examples.en: Which neighbourhood do you like best?

grammar.trap: 'What's your number?' is ¿Cuál es tu número?, not ¿Qué es tu número?

pronunciation: -ísimo moves the stress to the í: ca-RÍ-si-mo, ba-ra-TÍ-si-mo, le-JÍ-si-mos.
más and tan link to a following vowel: más alto sounds like ma-SAL-to, tan alto como like ta-NAL-to-co-mo.

common_errors.wrong: Es más grande como el centro.
common_errors.right: Es más grande que el centro.
common_errors.why: más … que, not como.
más bueno becomes mejor.
Before a number, use de.

common_errors.wrong: La mejor taquería en la colonia.
common_errors.right: La mejor taquería de la colonia.
common_errors.why: Superlatives take de for the group.

units.culture: Mexicans love recommending places (the best taquería, the best market), and ¿cuál me recomienda? starts conversations easily. Choosing a colonia, people weigh safety, noise, distance and being near the metro or a market; rents in central Mexico City have risen sharply in recent years, a sensitive topic for locals.
recycles: a1-12: Rento un departamento en la colonia …
units.evidence: The learner compares two places or prices with más / menos … que and tan … como, names the best one with la mejor … de, uses an -ísimo form, and asks ¿cuál me recomienda? or ¿cuál + noun? to choose.
sources: EeM U9 (comparatives), U11 (qué / cuál: marks ¿cuál libro? wrong), U14 (tanto como, -ísimo)
ELE L7 (describing a town)
PCIC Gram. A2 (comparatives); Gram. B1 (-ísimo, el más … de; the ban on cuál + noun is rejected for Mexico); Gén. B1 sample (me gustaría tener un balcón …)

units.title: Experiences and time here
units.can_do: Say what you have and haven't done in Mexico, how long you've been here, and what you've just done.
functions: say what you haven't done yet
situations: a new friend asks what you've seen
being asked how long you've been here

frames.es: ¿Has ido a Oaxaca?
frames.en: Have you ever been to Oaxaca?
frames.note: To usted: ¿Ha ido a Oaxaca?

frames.es: Nunca he probado los chapulines.
frames.en: I've never tried grasshoppers.
frames.note: chapulines = toasted grasshoppers, a snack from Oaxaca.

frames.es: Sí, he estado varias veces.
frames.en: Yes, I've been several times.

frames.es: ¿Ya fuiste a las pirámides?
frames.en: Have you been to the pyramids yet?
frames.note: Mexicans use ya + preterite for 'have you … yet?'

frames.es: Todavía no conozco el norte.
frames.en: I haven't been to the north yet.
frames.note: todavía no + present = not yet; conocer a place = to have been there.

frames.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas en México?
frames.en: How long have you been in Mexico?
frames.note: To usted: ¿Cuánto tiempo lleva en México?

frames.es: Llevo seis meses aquí. / Tengo seis meses aquí.
frames.en: I've been here six months.

frames.es: Acabo de llegar.
frames.en: I've just arrived.

model_exchanges.situation: A new friend asks what you've seen

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas en México?
lines.en: How long have you been in Mexico?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Llevo seis meses.
lines.en: Six months.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: ¿Y ya fuiste a Oaxaca?
lines.en: And have you been to Oaxaca yet?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: No, todavía no. Pero quiero ir en noviembre.
lines.en: No, not yet. But I want to go in November.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: ¿Has probado el mole negro?
lines.en: Have you tried black mole?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí, lo he probado y me encanta. Pero nunca he probado los chapulines.
lines.en: Yes, I've tried it and I love it. But I've never tried grasshoppers.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: ¡Pues tienes que ir!
lines.en: Well, you have to go!

model_exchanges.situation: Talking about trips with a neighbour

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: ¿Ha ido a las pirámides de Teotihuacán?
lines.en: Have you been to the pyramids at Teotihuacán?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí, fui el mes pasado. ¿Usted ha subido a la Pirámide del Sol?
lines.en: Yes, I went last month. Have you climbed the Pyramid of the Sun?

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: Uy, muchas veces. Pero nunca he ido al norte.
lines.en: Oh, many times. But I've never been to the north.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Yo tampoco. Todavía no conozco Monterrey.
lines.en: Me neither. I haven't been to Monterrey yet.

model_exchanges.situation: Meeting a neighbour in the building

lines.speaker: señora
lines.es: ¿Usted es nuevo en el edificio?
lines.en: Are you new in the building?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí, acabo de llegar. Me mudé el sábado.
lines.en: Yes, I've just arrived. I moved in on Saturday.

lines.speaker: señora
lines.es: ¡Bienvenido! ¿Y cuánto tiempo va a estar?
lines.en: Welcome! And how long will you be here?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Un año, por lo menos.
lines.en: A year, at least.

lines.speaker: señora
lines.es: Qué bueno. Cualquier cosa, aquí estamos.
lines.en: Good. If you need anything, we're here.

grammar.point: The present perfect for life experience
grammar.explain: He / has / ha / hemos / han + participle asks about and tells life experience, often with alguna vez, nunca or varias veces.

examples.en: Have you ever been to Oaxaca?

examples.es: Hemos estado dos veces en Puebla.

grammar.trap: In Mexico, don't use it for things done today: hoy comí tacos, not hoy he comido tacos.

grammar.explain: Regular participles end in -ado or -ido; a handful of common verbs are irregular.

examples.es: ver > visto, hacer > hecho, decir > dicho
poner > puesto, escribir > escrito, volver > vuelto, abrir > abierto

grammar.trap: Never hacido or vido: hecho, visto.

grammar.explain: To ask 'have you … yet?', Mexicans use ya + preterite; 'not yet' is todavía no, often with the present.

examples.en: Have you been to the pyramids yet?
I haven't been to the north yet.

grammar.trap: Conocer a place means to have been there: no conozco Monterrey = I've never been to Monterrey.

grammar.point: llevar / tener + time; acabar de + infinitive
grammar.explain: Llevo or tengo + time + aquí says how long you've been somewhere; acabar de + infinitive says you've just done something.

examples.en: I've been in Mexico for six months.
I've been living here for a year.

grammar.trap: 'I've been here six months' doesn't use haber: llevo seis meses aquí, not he estado aquí por seis meses.

vocabulary.en: to know; to have been to (a place)

pronunciation: he and ha blend into the next vowel: ha ido sounds like a-I-do, he estado like e-es-TA-do; listen for the little he.
The h is silent in he, has, ha, hemos and hecho.

common_errors.why: Mexico uses the preterite for today.
hacer has an irregular participle.

common_errors.wrong: He estado aquí por seis meses.
common_errors.why: Time up to now uses llevar or tener.

common_errors.right: Nunca he ido. / No he ido nunca.
common_errors.why: nunca before the verb needs no other no.

units.culture: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas en México? and ¿Ya fuiste a …? are among the first questions newcomers hear, and people enjoy suggesting places and foods to try. Mexico has dozens of UNESCO World Heritage sites and many Pueblos Mágicos (towns with a special tourism designation), so saying where you'd like to go next always gets recommendations.
recycles: a1-03: Llevo dos semanas en México.
units.evidence: Asked about their time in Mexico, the learner says how long they've been here with llevo / tengo + time, asks and answers about experiences with the present perfect (¿has ido …?, nunca he …), uses ya + preterite and todavía no correctly, and says what they've just done with acabo de.
sources: EeM U12 (perfect: today, experiences, ya / todavía no; the "today" use is not taught), U13 (preterite vs perfect; the book says perfect-for-today is Peninsular), U18 (llevar: ¿cuánto tiempo llevas en México?)
PCIC Gram. A2 (perfect, acabar de); Func. A2 (¿has estado en …?, vivo aquí desde hace …); NG A2 (tengo dos meses aquí [México], todavía no pruebo)

units.title: Customs, rules and celebrations
units.can_do: Ask what's customary, understand what's allowed, wish people well on the big days, and join in birthdays and holidays.
functions: admit you don't know the custom
situations: Day of the Dead in the colonia

frames.es: ¿Aquí se acostumbra dejar propina?
frames.en: Is it usual to tip here?

frames.es: ¿Aquí se puede estacionar?
frames.en: Can you park here?

frames.es: Perdón, no sé cómo se hace aquí.
frames.en: Sorry, I don't know how it's done here.

frames.es: ¿Hay que llevar algo?
frames.en: Do we need to bring anything?

frames.es: ¡Feliz cumpleaños! / ¡Felicidades!
frames.en: Happy birthday! / Congratulations!
frames.note: ¡Felicidades! works for birthdays, weddings, babies, new jobs.

frames.es: Vamos a cantarle las mañanitas.
frames.en: Let's sing him the birthday song.
frames.note: Las Mañanitas is the traditional birthday song.

frames.es: ¡Que lo muerda!
frames.en: Bite the cake!
frames.note: Guests shout this so the birthday person takes a bite of the cake, and often get their face pushed into it.

frames.es: ¿Van a poner ofrenda este año?
frames.en: Are you putting up an altar this year?
frames.note: ofrenda = the Day of the Dead altar for family members who have died.

frames.es: ¿Y qué se hace en una posada?
frames.en: And what do you do at a posada?
frames.note: posadas = Christmas parties from 16 to 24 December.

model_exchanges.situation: A neighbour's birthday

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: Hoy es el cumpleaños de don Pepe. Vamos a cantarle las mañanitas.
lines.en: It's don Pepe's birthday today. We're going to sing him Las Mañanitas.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Qué bonito! ¿Y qué se hace después?
lines.en: How lovely! And what happens afterwards?

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: Se parte el pastel. Pero primero… ¡que lo muerda!
lines.en: We cut the cake. But first… bite it!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Que muerda el pastel?
lines.en: He bites the cake?

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: Sí, es tradición. Le da una mordida y alguien le empuja la cara. ¡Con cariño!
lines.en: Yes, it's tradition. He takes a bite and someone pushes his face in. Affectionately!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Feliz cumpleaños, don Pepe! ¡Felicidades!
lines.en: Happy birthday, don Pepe! Congratulations!

model_exchanges.situation: Day of the Dead in the colonia

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: ¿Van a poner ofrenda este año?
lines.en: Are you putting up an altar this year?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: No sé cómo se hace. ¿Qué se pone?
lines.en: I don't know how it's done. What do you put on it?

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: Se ponen fotos de los difuntos, flores de cempasúchil, velas, pan de muerto y la comida que les gustaba.
lines.en: You put photos of the people who've died, marigolds, candles, pan de muerto and the food they liked.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Qué bonito! ¿Puedo poner una foto de mi abuela?
lines.en: How lovely! Can I put a photo of my grandmother?

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: ¡Claro! Es para todos los que ya se fueron.
lines.en: Of course! It's for everyone who has passed away.

model_exchanges.situation: An invitation to the office posada

lines.speaker: compañera
lines.es: El viernes es la posada de la oficina. ¿Vienes?
lines.en: Friday is the office posada. Are you coming?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Sí! ¿Y qué se hace en una posada?
lines.en: Yes! And what do you do at a posada?

lines.speaker: compañera
lines.es: Se pide posada cantando, se rompe la piñata y se toma ponche.
lines.en: You sing asking for shelter, break the piñata and drink fruit punch.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Hay que llevar algo?
lines.en: Do I need to bring anything?

lines.speaker: compañera
lines.es: Nomás un regalito para el intercambio.
lines.en: Just a little present for the gift exchange.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Perfecto. ¡Ahí nos vemos!
lines.en: Perfect. See you there!

grammar.point: Impersonal se: se puede, se acostumbra, se hace
grammar.explain: Se + the él / ella form of a verb talks about what people in general do or may do.

examples.en: Is it usual to tip here?
How do you say … in Spanish?

grammar.trap: With a plural noun the verb goes plural: se ponen velas, se venden boletos.

grammar.point: hay que for customs and rules
grammar.explain: Hay que + infinitive gives general rules and advice.

examples.en: You have to bring a present.

grammar.trap: No hay que means 'you don't need to', not 'you mustn't'; for something forbidden, say no se puede.

grammar.explain: Cheers and wishes like ¡que lo muerda! and ¡que les vaya bien! use the subjunctive, taught at B1; learn them whole for now.

examples.en: All the best to you all!

grammar.trap: Reuse these as fixed phrases rather than building new ones yet.

grammar.point: le on the infinitive: cantarle, darle
grammar.explain: Le (to him, her, you) can go on the end of an infinitive or before the conjugated verb, but never in between.

examples.es: Le vamos a cantar las mañanitas.

examples.en: You have to give her a hug.

grammar.trap: Not vamos a le cantar: the pronoun goes on the infinitive or before vamos.

vocabulary.en: Day of the Dead sweet bread
to be in the habit of; se acostumbra = it's customary

pronunciation: cempasúchil comes from Nahuatl: cem-pa-SÚ-chil, stress on SÚ, ch as in English 'church'.
ñ is one sound, like the ny in canyon: ma-ña-NI-tas.

common_errors.why: With a plural noun, the verb is plural.

common_errors.wrong: No hay que estacionarse aquí. (meaning it's forbidden)
common_errors.why: no hay que means 'there's no need to'.

common_errors.right: Vamos a cantarle. / Le vamos a cantar.
common_errors.why: The pronoun can't go between the two verbs.
enhorabuena sounds Spanish; Mexico says felicidades.

units.culture: The big dates: Día de Muertos (1–2 November), when families set up an ofrenda with photos, cempasúchil and their dead relatives' favourite food; 12 December, the Virgin of Guadalupe; the posadas from 16 to 24 December, with piñatas, ponche and often a gift exchange; Reyes on 6 January with rosca; and Independence on the night of 15 September with the Grito. Birthdays get Las Mañanitas, and Mother's Day is always 10 May. Asking ¿aquí se acostumbra…? is welcomed: people like explaining their customs.
units.evidence: The learner asks about a custom or rule with ¿aquí se acostumbra …? or ¿se puede …?, admits not knowing with no sé cómo se hace aquí, congratulates with ¡felicidades! at the right moment, follows ¡que lo muerda! and ofrenda in context, and asks what to bring with ¿hay que llevar algo?
sources: EeM U8 (Mexican fiestas page), U12 (hay que, se puede), U15 (impersonal se)
PCIC Func. A1 (¡felicidades!); Func. A2 (good wishes; no conozco muy bien las costumbres del país); Intercult. (¿aquí se acostumbra …?, no sé cómo se hace aquí)
PCIC Saberes (Las Mañanitas, ¡que lo muerda!, Día de Muertos, posadas, Guadalupe); Ref. (Día de Muertos)
7K (holidays: 10 May, 30 Apr, Guadalupe–Reyes, posadas, the Grito, Day of the Dead)

units.title: Good wishes and hopes
units.can_do: Wish people well in the Mexican way, say what you hope for, and understand the everyday 'God willing' phrases.
situations: saying goodbye to a neighbour who's going away
a friend before a trip or an exam

frames.es: ¡Que te vaya bien! / ¡Que le vaya bien!
frames.en: Take care! / All the best! (tú / usted)
frames.note: Said at almost every goodbye, to friends and to shopkeepers. To several people: ¡Que les vaya bien!

frames.es: ¡Que te mejores pronto!
frames.en: Get well soon!
frames.note: To usted: ¡Que se mejore pronto!

frames.es: ¡Que te la pases muy bien!
frames.en: Have a great time!
frames.note: Mexican pasársela bien, with la. To usted: ¡Que se la pase muy bien!

frames.es: ¡Que descanses!
frames.en: Get some rest! / Sleep well!

frames.es: Ojalá que no llueva mañana.
frames.en: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.

frames.es: Espero que te guste.
frames.en: I hope you like it.

frames.es: Gracias, igualmente.
frames.en: Thanks, you too.

frames.es: Si Dios quiere, nos vemos el lunes.
frames.en: God willing, see you on Monday.

frames.es: Primero Dios, todo va a salir bien.
frames.en: God willing, it'll all work out.
frames.note: Heard constantly, from believers and non-believers alike. Reply with Primero Dios or ¡Ojalá!

model_exchanges.situation: A neighbour sees the newcomer off before a weekend trip

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: ¿Ya se va de viaje?
lines.en: Off on your trip, then?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí, mañana temprano salgo para Oaxaca.
lines.en: Yes, I'm leaving for Oaxaca early tomorrow.

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: ¡Qué bien! Que se la pase muy bien.
lines.en: How nice! Have a great time.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Gracias. Ojalá que no llueva.
lines.en: Thanks. I hope it doesn't rain.

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: Si Dios quiere, va a hacer buen tiempo. ¿Cuándo regresa?
lines.en: God willing, the weather will be good. When are you back?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: El lunes, si Dios quiere.
lines.en: On Monday, God willing.

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: Que le vaya muy bien. ¡Buen viaje!
lines.en: All the best. Have a good trip!

model_exchanges.situation: A friend calls in sick

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Oye, hoy no voy a poder ir. Tengo gripa.
lines.en: Listen, I won't be able to come today. I've got flu.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Ay, pobre! Que te mejores pronto. ¿Necesitas algo?
lines.en: Oh, poor you! Get well soon. Do you need anything?

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: No, gracias. Nada más quiero dormir.
lines.en: No, thanks. I just want to sleep.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Pues descansa. Espero que mañana te sientas mejor.
lines.en: Well, rest. I hope you feel better tomorrow.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Ojalá. Gracias por llamar.
lines.en: I hope so. Thanks for calling.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Que descanses! Te marco mañana.
lines.en: Get some rest! I'll call you tomorrow.

model_exchanges.situation: A small present before a friend's driving test

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Te traje un detallito. Espero que te guste.
lines.en: I brought you a little something. I hope you like it.

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: ¡Ay, qué amable! Muchas gracias.
lines.en: Oh, how kind! Thanks so much.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Mañana es tu examen de manejo?
lines.en: Is your driving test tomorrow?

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Sí, y estoy bien nervioso.
lines.en: Yes, and I'm really nervous.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Mucha suerte! Ojalá que te vaya muy bien.
lines.en: Good luck! I hope it goes really well.

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Primero Dios. Gracias.
lines.en: God willing. Thanks.

grammar.explain: Take the yo form of the present, drop the -o and swap the vowel: -ar verbs take e, -er and -ir verbs take a, so any irregular yo form carries over.

examples.es: descanso → descanses; como → comas; vivo → vivas
tengo → tenga; hago → haga; puedo → pueda
examples.en: have, do, be able (irregular yo forms carry over)

examples.es: ir → vaya; ser → sea; estar → esté; saber → sepa

grammar.trap: English has almost no subjunctive, so learners reach for the ordinary present: '¡que te va bien!' sounds wrong; it must be ¡que te vaya bien!

grammar.explain: A wish that starts with que is short for 'I hope that…', so its verb is subjunctive; the chunks you already know (que le vaya bien, que se mejore) work this way.
grammar.trap: Don't drop the que: '¡te vaya bien!' isn't Spanish. And the wish is for the other person, so use te or le, not me.

grammar.explain: Ojalá means 'I hope' or 'let's hope'; que after it is optional and the verb is always subjunctive.

examples.en: I hope you find a flat soon.
—Are you coming on Saturday? —I hope so!

grammar.trap: Ojalá never takes the indicative: 'ojalá no llueve' is wrong. On its own, ¡Ojalá! means 'I hope so!'

grammar.explain: When you hope something about someone else, use espero que + subjunctive; when it's about yourself, use espero + infinitive.

examples.en: I hope to get there on time.

grammar.trap: Same person, no que: 'espero que llego a tiempo' should be espero llegar a tiempo.

grammar.explain: Fixed phrases added to almost any plan, meaning 'God willing'; si Dios quiere uses the ordinary present because it's a si clause.

examples.es: Nos vemos el lunes, si Dios quiere.
examples.en: See you on Monday, God willing.

examples.es: Primero Dios, el mes que entra me cambio de depa.
examples.en: God willing, I'll move flats next month.

grammar.trap: Don't hear them as doubt or as strong religion: they are polite hedges, closer to 'fingers crossed'.

pronunciation: Ojalá is stressed on the last syllable (o-ja-LÁ), and its j is a soft, breathy h, never the English j.
In Mexico y and ll sound the same, so vaya (from ir) and valla (fence) are identical: say a clear y as in 'yes', not a j or an l.

common_errors.why: Espero que about someone or something else takes the subjunctive.
Ojalá always takes the subjunctive.
When the hope is about yourself, use the infinitive with no que.
Mexico says pasársela, with la; pasarlo bien is Spain.

units.culture: Mexicans hedge almost every plan with si Dios quiere or primero Dios, whether or not they're religious; it signals modesty, not doubt. Answer with the same phrase or ¡Ojalá!, and add a que + wish whenever anyone leaves: even a shopkeeper gets ¡Que le vaya bien!
recycles: a1-01: Hasta luego. Que le vaya bien.
a1-14: Tengo gripa y un poco de calentura.
units.evidence: Without being prompted, the learner closes a conversation with a que + subjunctive wish that fits the moment (que te mejores, que te la pases bien, que descanses), uses espero que + subjunctive about someone else and espero + infinitive about themselves, and answers si Dios quiere or primero Dios naturally instead of asking what it means.
sources: EeM U16 C (¡Que te mejores!, ¡Que descanses!, ¡Que tengas buen viaje!; espero que + subjunctive vs espero + infinitive)
PCIC Gram. B1 9.2 (present subjunctive; Ojalá que tengas suerte)
PCIC Func. B1 3.8, 3.22, 5.17 (que + subjunctive wishes, ojalá, espero que); Func. B2 5.17 (que te la pases bien)
7K ch. 4 (si Dios quiere as a hedge on plans); 7K section 3C (primero Dios)

units.title: Getting things done politely
units.can_do: Ask for favours and services politely, say what you need someone to do, reassure people, and hear a refusal hidden in a yes.
functions: say what you need someone to do
situations: asking a neighbour to take in a parcel
asking a friend to help you move
asking a repair shop to look at something today
asking to use the bathroom in a shop or café

frames.es: Quería pedirle un favor.
frames.en: I wanted to ask you a favour.
frames.note: The imperfect softens the request. With tú: Quería pedirte un favor.

frames.es: ¿Me hace el favor de recibirme un paquete?
frames.en: Would you be so kind as to take in a parcel for me?
frames.note: Very Mexican and very polite; also ¿Me hace favor de…? With tú: ¿Me haces el favor de…?

frames.es: Necesito que me ayudes con algo.
frames.en: I need you to help me with something.

frames.es: ¿Me echas la mano con la mudanza?
frames.en: Can you give me a hand with the move?

frames.es: Quiero que lo revisen hoy, si se puede.
frames.en: I'd like you to check it today, if possible.
frames.note: Quiero que is direct; si se puede or por favor softens it.

frames.es: ¿Se lo dejo aquí?
frames.en: Shall I leave it here for you?

frames.es: No se preocupe. / No te preocupes.
frames.en: Don't worry.

frames.es: ¿Me presta el baño?
frames.en: May I use your bathroom?
frames.note: Literally 'will you lend me the bathroom?': the normal way to ask in a shop, café or someone's home.

frames.es: Va a estar difícil, pero déjeme ver.
frames.en: That'll be tricky, but let me see.
frames.note: Often a polite no. So are a ver si se puede and ahorita lo checo.

model_exchanges.situation: Asking a neighbour to take in a parcel

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Buenas tardes, señora. Quería pedirle un favor.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I wanted to ask you a favour.

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: Sí, dígame.
lines.en: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Mañana llega un paquete y no voy a estar. ¿Me hace el favor de recibírmelo?
lines.en: A parcel's coming tomorrow and I won't be in. Would you be so kind as to take it in for me?

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: Claro que sí, no se preocupe.
lines.en: Of course, don't worry.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Muchas gracias. Es usted muy amable.
lines.en: Thank you so much. You're very kind.

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: Ya llegó su paquete. ¿Se lo dejo en la puerta?
lines.en: Your parcel's here. Shall I leave it at your door?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: No, mejor ahorita paso por él. ¡Mil gracias!
lines.en: No, I'll come and get it now. Thanks a million!

model_exchanges.situation: Asking a friend to help with a move

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Oye, necesito que me ayudes con algo. ¿Me echas la mano con la mudanza el sábado?
lines.en: Listen, I need you to help me with something. Can you give me a hand with the move on Saturday?

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Híjole, el sábado va a estar difícil… Tengo un compromiso, pero déjame ver.
lines.en: Oh dear, Saturday's going to be tricky… I've got something on, but let me see.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: No te preocupes. Ya contraté un flete; nada más necesito ayuda con las cajas.
lines.en: Don't worry. I've already hired a van; I just need help with the boxes.

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Bueno, a ver si llego en la tarde.
lines.en: OK, I'll see if I can make it in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sale, gracias. Si no puedes, no pasa nada.
lines.en: Great, thanks. If you can't, it's fine.

model_exchanges.situation: Leaving a phone at a repair shop

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Buenos días. Se me cayó el celular y ya no prende. Quiero que lo revisen hoy, si se puede.
lines.en: Good morning. I dropped my phone and it won't switch on. I'd like you to look at it today, if possible.

lines.speaker: técnico
lines.es: ¿Hoy? Va a estar difícil, tenemos mucho trabajo. Déjeme ver.
lines.en: Today? That'll be tricky, we've got a lot of work. Let me see.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Podría tenerlo para el viernes?
lines.en: Could you have it ready by Friday?

lines.speaker: técnico
lines.es: Para el viernes, sí. Déjemelo y le aviso.
lines.en: By Friday, yes. Leave it with me and I'll let you know.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Perfecto. Aquí le dejo mi número.
lines.en: Perfect. I'll leave you my number.

lines.speaker: técnico
lines.es: No se preocupe. Ahorita le doy su comprobante.
lines.en: Don't worry. I'll give you your receipt right now.

grammar.explain: When you want or need someone else to do something, the second verb goes in the subjunctive after que; if you're the one doing it, use the infinitive.

examples.en: I need you to help me.
I want you to check it today.
I need to go to the bank.

grammar.trap: English 'I want you to help' tempts 'quiero tú ayudar' or 'quiero que me ayudas': it's quiero que me ayudes.

grammar.explain: To tell someone not to do something, use no + the subjunctive form, with any pronouns in front of the verb.

examples.es: No lo toques, todavía está caliente.
examples.en: Don't touch it, it's still hot.

grammar.trap: The affirmative and negative look different: siéntate becomes no te sientes, and the pronoun moves in front of the verb.

grammar.point: le / les + lo / la becomes se lo / se la
grammar.explain: When 'to him, her, you (usted) or them' meets 'it' or 'them', le or les turns into se: se lo, se la, se los, se las.

examples.en: Shall I leave it here for you?

examples.es: Ya se lo di a la vecina.
examples.en: I've already given it to the neighbour.
Would you take it in for me?

grammar.trap: Never 'le lo'. And in Mexico you'll hear se los for 'it, to them' (ya se los dije = I've already told them): it's normal, just recognise it.

grammar.explain: The imperfect quería and the conditional podría soften a request, like English 'I wanted to…' and 'could you…?'.

examples.en: I wanted to ask you a favour.
Could you have it ready by Friday?
Could you lend me your drill?

grammar.trap: A bare command to a stranger (revíselo hoy) sounds rude in Mexico: ask with a question.

grammar.explain: ¿Me hace el favor de + infinitive? is the courteous Mexican 'would you be so kind as to…?', and prestar (lend) covers anything you use briefly, even a bathroom.

examples.es: ¿Me hace el favor de cerrar la puerta?
examples.en: Would you mind closing the door?

grammar.trap: Mexico says ¿me prestas…? where Spain says ¿me dejas…?; and don't build 'pedir prestado' when a simple ¿me presta…? will do.

vocabulary.en: to switch on; (of a device) to come on

pronunciation: Requests in Mexico sound gentle and fairly level, with a soft rise at the end; a big English-style pitch jump (¿me AYUDAS?) can sound annoyed or pushy.
A d between vowels stays soft but audible in Mexico, like the th in 'this': ayudes, mudanza, todo. Don't turn it into an English d or drop it.

common_errors.why: Quiero que about someone else takes the subjunctive.
Negative commands use the subjunctive form.
Le becomes se before lo, la, los, las.
Prestar means 'to lend', so you ask the owner ¿me prestas…? (¿Puedo usar su baño? is correct too, just less usual than ¿me presta el baño?).

units.culture: Mexicans rarely say a flat no to a request. Va a estar difícil, déjeme ver, a ver si se puede or ahorita lo checo usually mean no or probably not, so don't push with 'but you can do it!'. When you're the one refusing, do the same: soften it and give a reason with es que…
recycles: a2-06: Déjame ver. / A ver si puedo.
a2-09: Se me cayó el celular.
a2-08: ¿Me avisa dónde me bajo, por favor?
units.evidence: The learner asks for a favour with quería pedirle… or ¿me hace el favor de…? rather than a bare command, uses necesito / quiero que + subjunctive about someone else, gets se lo right when offering something, and, when a character answers va a estar difícil, recognises the refusal and backs off or offers an alternative instead of insisting.
sources: EeM U13 C (se lo / se la: ¿Le has dado las llaves a Mercedes? Sí, ya se las he dado)
EeM U16 A (negative imperative: no te pongas, no se ponga)
PCIC Gram. B1 7.1.5 (clitic combinations; Mexican se los), 9.2 (quiero que + subjunctive), 9.3 (negative imperative), 9.1 (imperfect and conditional of politeness)
PCIC Func. B1 4.2–4.4 (asking favours, objects and help), 4.24 (no te preocupes); Tác. B1 3.1.2 (polite imperfect and conditional)
PCIC Func. C1 (¿serías tan amable de…? → Mexican ¿me hace favor de…?)
7K ch. 8 ('it would be difficult' = no); 7K section 3C (producing soft refusals at B1)
WP 6.10 (mudarse; flete and mudanza as gap words)

units.title: Renting a place
units.can_do: Answer a rental ad, ask about rent, deposit and what's included, understand the guarantor requirement, and arrange a viewing.
situations: calling about a Se renta sign

frames.es: Vi que se renta un departamento. ¿Todavía está disponible?
frames.en: I saw there's a flat for rent. Is it still available?

frames.es: ¿Cuánto es la renta y qué incluye?
frames.en: How much is the rent and what does it include?

frames.es: ¿Está amueblado? ¿El mantenimiento va aparte?
frames.en: Is it furnished? Is the maintenance fee extra?
frames.note: Mantenimiento is the monthly building fee for cleaning, security and shared areas.

frames.es: Pedimos un mes de depósito, un mes por adelantado y aval.
frames.en: We ask for one month's deposit, one month in advance and a guarantor.
frames.note: An aval is a guarantor, usually someone who owns property in the same city.

frames.es: No tengo aval. ¿Aceptan póliza jurídica?
frames.en: I don't have a guarantor. Do you accept a legal guarantee policy?
frames.note: A póliza jurídica is a rental guarantee bought from a specialist firm: the usual option for newcomers.

frames.es: ¿Hay agua todo el día o hay tandeo?
frames.en: Is there water all day, or is it rationed?
frames.note: Tandeo: water supplied only on certain days or at certain hours.

frames.es: Quería preguntar si aceptan mascotas.
frames.en: I wanted to ask whether you accept pets.

frames.es: Si firmo hoy, ¿me lo deja en doce mil?
frames.en: If I sign today, would you let me have it for twelve thousand?

frames.es: ¿Cuándo lo puedo ver?
frames.en: When can I see it?

model_exchanges.situation: Calling about a Se renta sign

lines.speaker: casera

lines.speaker: casera

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Hay agua todo el día o hay tandeo?

lines.speaker: casera

lines.speaker: newcomer

model_exchanges.situation: Negotiating the terms

lines.speaker: newcomer

lines.en: I really like it. I wanted to ask whether you accept pets.

lines.speaker: casera

lines.en: Hmm, that'll be tricky… Let me think about it and I'll let you know tomorrow.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sale, quedo pendiente. Muchas gracias.
lines.en: OK, I'll wait to hear from you. Thanks very much.

grammar.point: se renta, se vende, se solicita
grammar.explain: Se + a third-person verb makes an impersonal or passive sentence, the way signs and ads talk; the verb agrees with the thing (se renta un cuarto, se rentan cuartos).
grammar.trap: Make the verb plural with plural things (se rentan cuartos), and say rentar, never Spain's alquilar.

grammar.explain: Quería + infinitive opens a question softly, like 'I was wondering…'; si introduces a yes/no question inside the sentence.

examples.en: I wanted to ask whether you accept pets.

examples.es: Quería saber si todavía está disponible.
examples.en: I wanted to know if it's still available.

grammar.trap: Si here means 'whether' and has no accent; sí with an accent means 'yes'.

grammar.explain: In a real condition, si takes the ordinary present, and the other half is present, ir a or a question.

examples.es: Si firmo hoy, ¿me lo deja en doce mil?
examples.en: If I sign today, will you let me have it for twelve thousand?

examples.es: Si no hay tandeo, me interesa.
examples.en: If there's no water rationing, I'm interested.
If I like it, I'll rent it.

grammar.trap: Never the future after si: 'si firmaré' is wrong.

grammar.explain: Va or van aparte means 'is or are extra'; está or están incluido means 'is or are included', and incluido agrees with the noun.

examples.es: La luz y el gas van aparte.

grammar.trap: Incluido agrees: la luz está incluida, los servicios están incluidos.

vocabulary.en: water rationing by days or hours

pronunciation: Depósito and póliza are stressed on the third syllable from the end (de-PÓ-si-to, PÓ-li-sa), and the z in póliza is an s. Amueblado keeps its final d softly: a-mue-BLA-do, never 'amueblao'.
Renta, rentar and recámara start with a trilled r, like every r at the start of a word: give it two or three quick taps.

common_errors.why: Alquilar and piso (flat) are Spain; in Mexico piso means floor.
The verb agrees with the thing being rented.
No future after si.
Terrateniente is a big landowner; a landlord is casero or dueño.

units.culture: To rent in Mexico you usually pay one month's deposit plus the first month in advance, and landlords often ask for an aval: a guarantor who owns property in the same city. A newcomer without one can usually offer a póliza jurídica instead. Before signing, ask about water: whether there's a cisterna and tinaco, and whether the area has tandeo.
recycles: a1-12: Rento un departamento… / Mi casero vive abajo.
a2-13: Aquí la renta es más barata, pero está más lejos.
b1-02: Va a estar difícil… / quería + infinitive
units.evidence: On a call or at a viewing the learner asks what the rent includes, whether maintenance and services are extra, and about water; understands depósito, por adelantado and aval when the landlord lists them; offers a póliza jurídica; and uses si + present to negotiate.
sources: EeM U13 A (renting at an agency: ¿Dónde le gustaría vivir?, me gustaría)
PCIC Gram. B1 7.1.4 (passive se: Se venden pisos → Se renta departamento)
PCIC Func. B1 1.4 (Quería saber si…); Gram. B1 15.3.6 (si + present)
PCIC NE B1 10 (casero, pagar la renta, ir a ver un depa); NG B2 4.3.5 (pagar el primer mes por adelantado); Gén. B2 (renting property)
PCIC Saberes 1.9, 1.14 rewritten for Mexico (deposit, first month, aval or póliza jurídica, Se renta signs, cisterna, tinaco, tandeo)
WP 6.7 (renta, casero; terrateniente flagged as an error)

units.title: Paperwork and offices
units.can_do: Get through a government office: say why you've come, ask what documents you need, follow instructions, and come back with what's missing.
situations: an appointment at the immigration office (INM)
a bank or office asking for ID
the copy shop next to the office

frames.es: Vengo por lo de mi tarjeta de residente.
frames.en: I've come about my residence card.
frames.note: Vengo por lo de… = I've come about…; it works for any procedure.

frames.es: ¿Qué documentos necesito?
frames.en: What documents do I need?

frames.es: ¿Tiene cita? — Sí, la hice en línea.
frames.en: Do you have an appointment? — Yes, I made it online.

frames.es: Tome un turno y espere a que lo llamen.
frames.en: Take a number and wait to be called.

frames.es: Traiga su pasaporte, dos copias y un comprobante de domicilio.
frames.en: Bring your passport, two copies and proof of address.
frames.note: A comprobante de domicilio is a recent bill (electricity, water, phone or internet) showing the address.

frames.es: Le falta una copia de la CURP.
frames.en: You're missing a copy of your CURP.
frames.note: CURP: Mexico's personal ID code; foreign residents get one with their residence card.

frames.es: Regrese mañana con todo completo.
frames.en: Come back tomorrow with everything.

frames.es: ¿Dónde puedo sacar copias por aquí?
frames.en: Where can I get copies made around here?

frames.es: ¿Me puede explicar qué tengo que llenar?
frames.en: Could you explain what I need to fill in?

lines.speaker: empleada
lines.es: Buenos días. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar?
lines.en: Good morning. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Buenos días. Vengo por lo de mi tarjeta de residente.

lines.es: Sí. ¿Le sirve mi tarjeta de residente?

grammar.explain: Officials give instructions with the usted command, which uses the subjunctive form (traiga, llene, firme, regrese, pase); pronouns attach to the end.

examples.en: Fill it in and sign it at the bottom.

grammar.trap: The stress doesn't move when a pronoun is added, so the written accent appears: llene → llénelo, firme → fírmelo.

grammar.explain: Faltar works like gustar: the missing thing is the subject, so the verb agrees with it, and the person who lacks it is me, te, le.
grammar.trap: Plural things need faltan: le faltan dos copias. And 'you're missing' is never 'usted falta'.

grammar.point: hace falta / es necesario que + subjunctive (understand)
grammar.explain: Hace falta + a noun or infinitive means 'you need'; with que and another person, the verb is subjunctive.

examples.es: Hace falta un comprobante de domicilio.

examples.en: You need to fill in this form.

examples.es: Es necesario que venga en persona.
examples.en: You have to come in person.

grammar.trap: Recognise the subjunctive in what officials say (que venga, que traiga); you can always check with ¿qué necesito?

grammar.explain: Vengo por + a noun (or por lo de…) says what you've come about or to collect; vengo a + infinitive says what you've come to do.

examples.es: Vengo por lo de mi CURP.

examples.en: I've come to collect my card.

grammar.trap: Don't use para here: 'vengo para mi tarjeta' sounds wrong.

vocabulary.en: personal ID code (Clave Única de Registro de Población)

pronunciation: Some acronyms are said as words and some are spelled out: CURP sounds like 'koorp' and INE like 'EE-neh', but INM is spelled out, i-ene-eme, and so is RFC, erre-efe-ce.
Ventanilla has a y sound for the ll (ven-ta-NI-ya), and identificación has six syllables, stressed on the last: i-den-ti-fi-ca-SIÓN.

common_errors.why: Faltar agrees with the missing things.
What you've come for or about takes por.
Mexico says llenar (rellenar sounds Spanish); offices usually call the paper a formato or forma, though formulario is understood.
The pronoun joins the command, and the written accent keeps the stress.

units.culture: Mexican offices want copies of everything, often two of each, plus a comprobante de domicilio no more than three months old; the papelerías near government offices make copies and print forms in minutes. Book INM appointments online, and if you came in on a residence visa, apply for the card within 30 calendar days of arriving.
recycles: b1-02: ¿me puede…? and other polite requests
a2-07: Quisiera hacer una cita para el jueves 15.
a1-02: ¿Me lo puede repetir, por favor?
a2-15: Perdón, no sé cómo se hace aquí.
b1-02: se lo (Ahorita se lo regreso.)
units.evidence: At a counter the learner says why they've come with vengo por (lo de)…, asks what documents are needed, follows usted instructions (traiga, llene, regrese) without asking for English, understands le falta / le faltan and comes back with the missing item, and asks where to get copies.
sources: PCIC Obj. B1 (residence and work permits); Gén. C1 (residence certificate)
PCIC Func. B1 2.17 (es obligatorio / necesario que…); Func. B2 4.1 (hace falta… dar los datos personales y entregar la ficha con tu firma)
PCIC NE B1 3.2 (burocracia, solicitar / renovar un documento); NE C1 3.1–3.2 (acta de nacimiento, RFC, tramitar)
PCIC Saberes 1.1, 2.1.4 rewritten for Mexico (INE, CURP, RFC, INM residence card, proof of address; online appointments, copies of everything, ventanilla)
WP 6.12 (trámite, forma, llenar, sacar copias, comprobante de domicilio, identificación)
consulmex.sre.gob.mx (INM: request the residence card within 30 calendar days of entry)

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Ahorita te la mando por WhatsApp.
lines.en: I'll send it to you on WhatsApp right now.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Listo, ya te transferí.
lines.en: Done, I've sent it.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Sí, ya me llegó. ¡Gracias!
lines.en: Yes, it's come through. Thanks!

model_exchanges.situation: Phoning the bank about a double charge

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Buenas tardes. Me cobraron dos veces la misma compra.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I've been charged twice for the same purchase.

lines.speaker: ejecutivo
lines.es: ¿Me da los últimos cuatro dígitos de su tarjeta?
lines.en: Could you give me the last four digits of your card?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí: siete, cuatro, cero, dos.
lines.en: Yes: seven, four, zero, two.

lines.speaker: ejecutivo
lines.es: Ya veo el cargo doble. Vamos a levantar una aclaración.
lines.en: I can see the double charge. We'll open a dispute.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y cuándo me regresan el dinero?
lines.en: And when do I get the money back?

lines.speaker: ejecutivo
lines.es: En unos días hábiles le llega a su cuenta.
lines.en: It'll reach your account within a few working days.

grammar.explain: Mexico uses the preterite for anything done and finished, even a minute ago, where English often says 'I've…'.

examples.en: I paid the electricity bill yesterday.

grammar.trap: Don't copy Spain's 'ya te he transferido': in Mexico the preterite is the normal way to say 'I've just…'.

grammar.explain: The third-person plural with no subject means 'they' in general, like English 'they charged me' for a bank or shop.

examples.en: How much did they charge you?

grammar.trap: Don't add ellos: 'ellos me cobraron' sounds as if you mean particular people.

grammar.point: estar a for prices and rates
grammar.explain: ¿A cómo está…? and está a… ask for and give a price or rate that changes from day to day.

examples.es: Hoy está más alto que ayer.

grammar.trap: Use estar, not ser: '¿a cuánto es el dólar?' sounds odd, and Mexico prefers a cómo to a cuánto.

grammar.point: si + present to ask about conditions
grammar.explain: Si + present, followed by a question in the present, checks what happens in a given case.

examples.es: Si pago con tarjeta, ¿me cobran comisión?
examples.en: If I pay by card, do you charge a fee?

examples.es: Si retiro en otro banco, ¿cuánto me cobran?
examples.en: If I withdraw at another bank, how much will they charge me?

grammar.trap: No future and no subjunctive after si: 'si pague' and 'si pagaré' are both wrong.

pronunciation: CLABE is said exactly like clave ('key'): b and v are the same sound in Spanish, and between vowels the lips barely touch.
Stress tells the tense: transfiero (I transfer, trans-FIE-ro) vs transferí (I transferred, trans-fe-RÍ), cobro vs cobró. Put the stress in the right place or the meaning changes.

common_errors.why: Mexico uses the preterite for something just finished.
Changing prices and rates take estar a; Mexico says a cómo.
Phone credit is saldo (crédito is a loan or credit line), and Mexicans use se me acabó for running out.
The cash machine is el cajero (automático).

units.culture: Mexicans pay each other by bank transfer all the time, using the 18-digit CLABE or a card number, and these SPEI transfers usually arrive within seconds; splitting a bill often ends with '¿me pasas tu CLABE?'. Corner shops and OXXO sell phone top-ups and take payments for many bills.
recycles: b1-04: comprobante de domicilio, tarjeta de residente
a1-15: Se me olvidó la cartera. (se me + verb)
units.evidence: The learner asks what's needed to open an account, asks for and gives a CLABE, reports a payment with the preterite (ya te transferí), tops up a phone without English, and explains a double charge (me cobraron dos veces) clearly enough for a clerk to act on it.
sources: PCIC Obj. A (bank transactions)
PCIC NE B1–B2 9, 11, 12 (abrir una cuenta, hacer una transferencia, quedarse sin saldo, pagar a plazos → meses sin intereses, factura); NE C1 (estado de cuenta)
PCIC Gram. B1 12 (estar a + a fluctuating price: El euro está a…)
PCIC Saberes 1.11 rewritten for Mexico (OXXO bill payments, meses sin intereses)
WP 6.3, 6.12 (cajero, comisión, tipo de cambio, recargar saldo, efectivo, datos)

units.title: Complaints
units.can_do: Point out a mistake, return a faulty product, complain about noise or a service, and say what you want done.
situations: a wrong bill in a restaurant

frames.es: Disculpe, creo que hay un error en la cuenta.
frames.en: Excuse me, I think there's a mistake on the bill.

frames.es: Lo compré la semana pasada y ya no sirve.
frames.en: I bought it last week and it's already stopped working.

frames.es: Quiero que me devuelvan mi dinero.
frames.en: I want my money back.

frames.es: ¿Puedo hablar con el encargado?
frames.en: Could I speak to the person in charge?

frames.es: Los vecinos ponen música hasta las tres de la mañana.
frames.en: The neighbours play music until three in the morning.

frames.es: Me molesta que no avisen.
frames.en: It bothers me that they don't let us know.

frames.es: Ya estoy harto de que se estacionen enfrente de mi cochera.
frames.en: I'm fed up with people parking in front of my garage.
frames.note: A woman says harta.

frames.es: Si no lo arreglan, voy a poner una queja en Profeco.
frames.en: If they don't fix it, I'll file a complaint with the consumer protection office.
frames.note: Profeco: the federal consumer protection office, for complaints against businesses.

frames.es: Tiene razón, una disculpa.
frames.en: You're right, our apologies.
frames.note: Una disculpa is the usual Mexican service apology.

model_exchanges.situation: A wrong bill in a restaurant

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Disculpe, creo que hay un error en la cuenta.
lines.en: Excuse me, I think there's a mistake on the bill.

lines.speaker: mesero
lines.es: ¿Ah, sí? ¿Qué pasó?
lines.en: Oh? What's wrong?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Nos cobraron tres cervezas, pero nada más pedimos dos.
lines.en: You've charged us for three beers, but we only ordered two.

lines.speaker: mesero
lines.es: Tiene razón, una disculpa. Ahorita se la corrijo.
lines.en: You're right, sorry. I'll correct it for you right away.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: No se preocupe. Gracias.
lines.en: Don't worry. Thanks.

model_exchanges.situation: Returning a faulty blender

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Buenas tardes. Compré esta licuadora la semana pasada y ya no sirve.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I bought this blender last week and it's already stopped working.

lines.speaker: vendedora
lines.es: ¿Trae su ticket?
lines.en: Have you got your receipt?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí, aquí está. Tiene garantía, ¿no?
lines.en: Yes, here it is. It has a guarantee, doesn't it?

lines.speaker: vendedora
lines.es: Sí. Se la podemos cambiar por otra.
lines.en: Yes. We can exchange it for another one.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: La verdad, prefiero que me devuelvan mi dinero.
lines.en: To be honest, I'd rather have my money back.

lines.speaker: vendedora
lines.es: Para un reembolso necesito autorización. Déjeme hablar con el encargado.
lines.en: For a refund I need authorisation. Let me talk to the manager.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Está bien, aquí espero.
lines.en: That's fine, I'll wait here.

model_exchanges.situation: Telling the building manager about noisy neighbours

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Buenas tardes. Quería comentarle algo de los vecinos del cuatro.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I wanted to mention something about the neighbours in number four.

lines.speaker: administrador
lines.es: Sí, dígame.
lines.en: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Ponen música hasta las tres de la mañana, y entre semana.
lines.en: They play music until three in the morning, even on weeknights.

lines.speaker: administrador
lines.es: Híjole, no es la primera queja.
lines.en: Oh dear, it's not the first complaint.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: No me molesta que hagan fiestas; me molesta que no avisen.
lines.en: I don't mind them having parties; what bothers me is that they don't warn us.

lines.speaker: administrador
lines.es: Tiene razón. Ahorita les mando un mensaje.
lines.en: You're right. I'll send them a message right away.

grammar.point: me molesta que / estoy harto de que + subjunctive
grammar.explain: After a verb of feeling, a que clause about what other people do takes the subjunctive.

examples.en: It bothers me that they don't let us know.

examples.es: Estoy harto de que se estacionen aquí.
examples.en: I'm fed up with people parking here.

grammar.trap: With a plain noun there's no que (me molesta el ruido); with something other people do, it's que + subjunctive, not the indicative.

grammar.explain: Say what you want the business or person to do with quiero que or prefiero que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Quiero que me devuelvan mi dinero.

grammar.trap: 'I want my money back' is not 'quiero mi dinero atrás': say quiero que me devuelvan mi dinero.

grammar.explain: Si + present, then ir a + infinitive, says what you'll do if something doesn't happen.

examples.es: Si no lo arreglan, voy a poner una queja.
examples.en: If they don't fix it, I'm going to complain.

examples.es: Si siguen con el ruido, voy a hablar con el administrador.
examples.en: If they carry on with the noise, I'll speak to the building manager.

grammar.trap: Keep the present after si: not 'si no lo arreglarán'.

grammar.explain: Ya no + verb says something has stopped happening or working.

examples.en: It won't switch on any more.
They don't make noise any more.

grammar.trap: English puts 'any more' at the end; ya no goes before the verb.

vocabulary.en: to work (of a machine); to be useful

pronunciation: Arreglar, error and reembolso all have a trilled r: in error the middle rr is trilled and the final r is a single tap (e-RROR).
Keep every vowel clear in disculpe and devuelvan (dis-KUL-pe, de-BUEL-ban); English speakers tend to swallow the unstressed e, and the word gets hard to catch.

common_errors.why: Feelings about what others do take que + subjunctive.

common_errors.right: Quiero que me devuelvan mi dinero.
common_errors.why: A word-for-word translation of 'back' doesn't work.
'Not any more' is ya no, before the verb.

common_errors.wrong: Estoy harto de los vecinos hacen ruido.
common_errors.right: Estoy harto de que los vecinos hagan ruido.
common_errors.why: Harto de que + subjunctive.

units.culture: Complain in Mexico calmly and in private: open with disculpe, describe the problem and say what you want, because raising your voice or embarrassing staff in front of others makes things harder. For a business that won't help, Profeco takes consumer complaints for free; with neighbours, go through the building's administrador, and expect some tolerance for weekend parties.
recycles: a2-09: Se descompuso el boiler. / ¿Para cuándo queda?
a2-04: ¿Lo puedo cambiar? Aquí está el ticket.
a2-03: Joven, ¿me trae la cuenta, por favor?
