frames.en: We agreed you'd deliver it on Monday.
frames.note: quedar en que + imperfect reports what was agreed.

frames.es: Me cobró de más y encima lo dejó peor.
frames.en: He overcharged me and on top of that left it worse.

frames.es: Si me hace un descuento, le encargo los dos.
frames.en: If you give me a discount, I'll order both.

model_exchanges.situation: Ordering a bookcase at a carpenter's workshop

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Buenas tardes. Quiero mandar hacer un librero de pino, de dos metros por uno.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I'd like to have a pine bookcase made, two metres by one.

lines.speaker: carpintero
lines.es: Con mucho gusto. ¿Lo quiere barnizado o al natural?
lines.en: Certainly. Do you want it varnished or natural?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Barnizado, por favor. ¿Me puede pasar una cotización?
lines.en: Varnished, please. Could you send me a quote?

lines.speaker: carpintero
lines.es: Le sale en cuatro mil quinientos, con todo y material. Le pido la mitad de anticipo.
lines.en: It comes to four thousand five hundred, materials included. I'll ask you for half as a deposit.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y para cuándo lo tendría listo?
lines.en: And when would you have it ready?

lines.speaker: carpintero
lines.es: Para el viernes de la otra semana ya lo habré terminado, si Dios quiere.
lines.en: I'll have finished it by Friday week, God willing.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Perfecto. Si me hace un descuento, le encargo también un buró.
lines.en: Great. If you give me a discount, I'll order a bedside table too.

lines.speaker: carpintero
lines.es: Ándele, le dejo los dos en seis mil.
lines.en: All right, I'll let you have both for six thousand.

model_exchanges.situation: Calling back the technician after a repair that went wrong

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Buenos días. Le hablo porque la lavadora sigue sin funcionar.
lines.en: Good morning. I'm calling because the washing machine still isn't working.

lines.speaker: técnico
lines.es: ¿Cómo? Si yo la dejé funcionando.
lines.en: What? But I left it working.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Pues no. Me cobró de más por la refacción y encima ahora tira agua.
lines.en: Well, it isn't. You overcharged me for the part, and on top of that it's leaking now.

lines.speaker: técnico
lines.es: Ha de ser la manguera. A lo mejor no quedó bien apretada.
lines.en: It must be the hose. Maybe it wasn't tightened properly.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Quedamos en que tenía garantía de tres meses, ¿verdad?
lines.en: We agreed it had a three-month guarantee, right?

lines.speaker: técnico
lines.es: Sí, cómo no. Paso mañana temprano y se la reviso sin costo.
lines.en: Yes, of course. I'll come by early tomorrow and check it at no charge.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Se lo agradezco. Y por favor tráigame una nota de lo que le pagué.
lines.en: Thank you. And please bring me a receipt for what I paid you.

grammar.explain: To say you had something done by someone else, Mexicans use mandar + infinitive, with the thing as the object.

examples.en: I'm going to get it fixed.
Where did you get the door painted?

grammar.trap: English 'I had it made' tempts you into 'lo tuve hecho', which doesn't mean that. And lo arreglé means you fixed it yourself.

grammar.point: the future perfect for 'by then' and for guesses; ha de haber
grammar.explain: habré + participle says something will be finished before a future point, and in conversation it often guesses about the past, like ha de haber + participle.

examples.es: Para el viernes ya lo habré terminado.
examples.en: I'll have finished it by Friday.
The materials will have arrived by now.

examples.es: Ha de haber salido a comer.
examples.en: He must have gone out for lunch.

grammar.trap: Ya habrá llegado is usually a guess about now, not a prediction. And a deadline takes para (para el viernes), not por.

grammar.point: encargar, cobrar de más, quedar en
grammar.explain: Three everyday verbs for jobs: encargar is to order something to be made or brought, cobrar de más is to overcharge, and quedar en is to agree on something.

examples.es: Le encargué dos sillas al carpintero.
examples.en: I ordered two chairs from the carpenter.

examples.es: Creo que me cobraron de más.

examples.en: We agreed to meet on Monday.

grammar.trap: Encargar isn't 'to charge': that's cobrar. And quedar en (agree to) is different from quedar alone (to be left, to fit).

vocabulary.en: to order (to be made or brought)
on top of that, what's more

pronunciation: The h is always silent, so habré, habrá and ha de haber start with a vowel. Ha de haber runs together as one word: a-de-a-BER.
With seseo, z and c before e or i sound like s: cotización is co-ti-sa-SIÓN. In refacción the two c's differ: the first is a k, the second an s (re-fak-SIÓN).

common_errors.why: Spanish doesn't use tener + participle for 'had it done'; Mexicans say mandar + infinitive.
Encargar means to order; to charge is cobrar.
A deadline takes para.

common_errors.wrong: Lo arreglé. (when a technician did it)
common_errors.why: Lo arreglé means you fixed it yourself.

units.culture: Small workshops still make and fix most things in Mexico: carpenters, ironworkers, upholsterers and seamstresses work to order. They usually ask for half the price as an anticipo, and deadlines tend to be optimistic, so agree a date (quedamos en…), ask for a written cotización or a nota, and check in politely before the day. Good tradespeople are found by recommendation: ¿Me recomiendas a alguien de confianza?
recycles: b2-04 (Le hablo para…; sigue sin funcionar)
units.evidence: Talking with a tradesperson or technician, the learner asks for a quote, a deadline and the deposit, uses mandar + infinitive for what they want done or had done, reports an agreement with quedamos en que…, and complains about poor work firmly but politely.
sources: PCIC Obj. C1 (repairs arranged by phone); Gram. B2 (future perfect of probability); Gram. C1 (future perfect: ¿No me habré olvidado de algo?); Mexican ha de haber (pcic-1 variety notes)
PCIC Nociones específicas C1 10.1 (arreglar una gotera), 10.4 (pieza de repuesto → refacción); Nociones generales C1 (anticipo, adelanto)
PCIC Saberes (hardware shops, gestores), rewritten for Mexico
Word Power 6.7, 6.10 (plomero, fuga; gaps: carpintero, albañil, cerrajero)
Seven Keys ch. 4 and 7 (si Dios quiere; flexible deadlines)

units.title: The health system in depth
units.can_do: Describe symptoms precisely, understand referrals, tests and hospital routines, and ask what's covered.
functions: offer help during a hospital stay

frames.es: Es un dolor punzante, aquí, del lado derecho.
frames.en: It's a stabbing pain, here, on the right side.
frames.note: Other kinds: sordo (dull), agudo (sharp), constante, que va y viene (comes and goes).

frames.es: Me empieza en la espalda y se me baja a la pierna.
frames.en: It starts in my back and goes down into my leg.

frames.es: Desde que empecé a tomar la medicina, me siento mareado.
frames.en: Since I started taking the medicine, I've been feeling dizzy.
frames.note: A woman says mareada. Desde que + preterite, then the present for what's still going on.

frames.es: ¿Me puede dar un pase al especialista?
frames.en: Could you give me a referral to the specialist?
frames.note: At IMSS your family doctor gives you the pase before you can see a specialist.

frames.es: Hay que venir en ayunas para los análisis.
frames.en: You have to come without eating for the blood tests.
frames.note: En ayunas: nothing to eat since the night before. Water is usually allowed; ask.

frames.es: En caso de que le suba la fiebre, váyase directo a urgencias.
frames.en: If your temperature goes up, go straight to the emergency room.

frames.es: ¿Qué tan grave es?
frames.en: How serious is it?
frames.note: Mexico says ¿qué tan + adjective? for 'how …?'.

frames.es: ¿Se puede hacer por el IMSS o tengo que ir con un médico particular?
frames.en: Can it be done through IMSS or do I have to see a private doctor?
frames.note: You go con a person and a a place: ir con el doctor, ir al hospital.

frames.es: ¿Cuánto cubre el seguro y de cuánto es el deducible?
frames.en: How much does the insurance cover, and how much is the deductible?
frames.note: You'll also hear coaseguro: the percentage you pay after the deductible.

frames.es: Lo van a internar unos días; hace falta que alguien se quede con él.
frames.en: They're going to admit him for a few days; someone needs to stay with him.

model_exchanges.situation: A specialist appointment

lines.speaker: doctora
lines.es: A ver, cuénteme. ¿Qué tipo de dolor es?
lines.en: Right, tell me about it. What kind of pain is it?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Es un dolor punzante, aquí, del lado derecho. Va y viene.
lines.en: It's a stabbing pain, here, on the right side. It comes and goes.

lines.speaker: doctora
lines.es: ¿Desde cuándo lo tiene?
lines.en: How long have you had it?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Desde hace dos semanas. Y desde que empecé a tomar la medicina, me siento mareado.
lines.en: For two weeks. And since I started taking the medicine, I've been feeling dizzy.

lines.speaker: doctora
lines.es: Le voy a mandar a hacer unos análisis y un ultrasonido. Hay que venir en ayunas.
lines.en: I'm going to send you for some blood tests and an ultrasound. You have to come without eating.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Qué tan grave puede ser?
lines.en: How serious could it be?

lines.speaker: doctora
lines.es: Seguramente no es nada grave, pero en caso de que el dolor aumente, váyase directo a urgencias.
lines.en: It's probably nothing serious, but if the pain gets worse, go straight to the emergency room.

model_exchanges.situation: At the insurance desk of a private hospital

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Buenas tardes. Tengo seguro de gastos médicos. ¿Me cubre la cirugía?
lines.en: Good afternoon. I have private medical insurance. Does it cover the operation?

lines.speaker: empleada
lines.es: Déjeme revisar su póliza… Sí, está cubierta, pero primero paga usted el deducible.
lines.en: Let me check your policy… Yes, it's covered, but first you pay the deductible.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y de cuánto es el deducible?
lines.en: And how much is the deductible?

lines.speaker: empleada
lines.es: Veinte mil pesos, y después usted cubre un diez por ciento de coaseguro.
lines.en: Twenty thousand pesos, and after that you pay ten per cent co-insurance.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Entiendo. ¿Y hace falta que la aseguradora lo autorice antes?
lines.en: I see. And does the insurer need to authorise it beforehand?

lines.speaker: empleada
lines.es: Sí. Como es una cirugía programada, necesitamos la autorización antes de internarlo.
lines.en: Yes. Since it's a planned operation, we need the authorisation before we admit you.

model_exchanges.situation: Visiting a neighbour's family at the hospital

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Cómo sigue don Arturo?
lines.en: How is Don Arturo doing?

lines.speaker: hija
lines.es: Mejor, gracias. Lo internaron el martes y ya le hicieron los estudios.
lines.en: Better, thanks. They admitted him on Tuesday and they've done the tests.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Les hace falta algo? Si quieren, me quedo con él una noche.
lines.en: Do you need anything? If you like, I'll stay with him one night.

lines.speaker: hija
lines.es: ¡Qué amable! Mi mamá se queda en las noches, pero si puede venir el sábado en la mañana, nos ayuda mucho.
lines.en: That's so kind! My mum stays at night, but if you can come on Saturday morning, it would help us a lot.

grammar.explain: Spanish describes pain with an adjective after dolor (punzante, sordo, agudo) and says where it goes with verbs like bajar and subir plus me.

examples.es: Tengo un dolor sordo en la espalda.
examples.en: I have a dull pain in my back.

examples.es: Es un dolor que va y viene.
examples.en: It's a pain that comes and goes.

examples.es: Me duele aquí y se me sube al cuello.
examples.en: It hurts here and goes up into my neck.

grammar.trap: Don't use 'my' with body parts: me duele la espalda, not mi espalda duele.

grammar.explain: Desde que + preterite marks when something started, and the main verb stays in the present if it's still true.

examples.en: Since I arrived, I've been sleeping badly.

examples.es: Desde que me operaron, ya no me duele.
examples.en: Since my operation, it hasn't hurt.

grammar.trap: English uses 'have been' here; Spanish uses the plain present: me siento mareado, not he estado sintiendo.

grammar.explain: En caso de que (in case, if) always takes the subjunctive; doctors and leaflets use it for instructions that depend on something happening.

examples.es: En caso de que tenga fiebre, tómese esta pastilla.
examples.en: If you get a temperature, take this tablet.

examples.es: En caso de que no pueda venir, avise un día antes.
examples.en: If you can't come, let us know a day before.

grammar.trap: After si the present indicative is right (si tiene fiebre); after en caso de que it never is: en caso de que tenga, not tiene.

grammar.explain: Hace falta que (it's necessary that) takes the subjunctive; hace falta + infinitive is for when nobody in particular is meant.

examples.es: Hace falta que venga en ayunas.
examples.en: You need to come without eating.
There's no need to bring copies.

grammar.trap: Hace falta que vengas, not hace falta que vienes: the second verb is subjunctive.

vocabulary.en: blood test, lab test (same in the plural)

pronunciation: Keep every vowel clear in long medical words: a-NÁ-li-sis, es-pe-sia-LIS-ta, ul-tra-so-NI-do. English swallows the middle vowels of 'specialist'; Spanish doesn't.
Mexicans say the acronyms as words: el IMSS is 'ims' and el ISSSTE is 'is-te'.

common_errors.why: Pain uses doler with me, and the body part takes la, not mi.

common_errors.wrong: En caso de que tiene fiebre…
common_errors.right: En caso de que tenga fiebre…
common_errors.why: En caso de que always takes the subjunctive.
With a named doctor Mexico says ir con (a person goes with con); ir al doctor is fine for 'going to the doctor's' in general, and a goes with places: ir al hospital.

common_errors.wrong: He estado mareado desde que he empezado la medicina.
common_errors.right: Me siento mareado desde que empecé a tomar la medicina.
common_errors.why: Mexico uses the preterite for the starting point and the present for what's still true.

units.culture: Mexico has public healthcare through IMSS (for formal employees; residents can also join voluntarily through its family health scheme), ISSSTE (for government workers) and IMSS-Bienestar (for people without social security), alongside private doctors and hospitals. At IMSS you see your family doctor first and need a pase to see a specialist. Many newcomers also buy seguro de gastos médicos mayores and should ask about the deducible, the coaseguro and any waiting periods. In hospital, relatives stay with the patient day and night, and friends offer to take a turn.
recycles: b1-10 (Me mandaron a hacer unos estudios. ¿Tienes IMSS o seguro de gastos médicos?)
units.evidence: At a doctor's or insurer's, the learner describes a pain by type, place and timing without prompting, asks for a pase or what the insurance covers, follows an en caso de que… instruction correctly, and uses the present after desde que + preterite.
sources: PCIC Obj. C1 (describing symptoms you can't see); Nociones específicas C1 13.3 (dolor sordo / agudo / punzante), 13.4 (análisis clínicos, médico de cabecera / particular); Gén. C1 (medical certificates)
PCIC Gram. C1 (en caso de que; hacer falta que + subjunctive)
PCIC Saberes 1.12 (health centres; relatives stay with patients), rewritten for Mexico: IMSS, ISSSTE, IMSS-Bienestar, private insurance
Word Power 6.8 (urgencias, seguro médico, análisis de sangre, mareado)

units.title: Taxes, banking and contracts
units.can_do: Deal with the tax office, invoices and contracts, and understand and negotiate their conditions.
functions: understand the conditions of a contract
situations: asking for an invoice in a shop or restaurant

frames.es: Necesito darme de alta en el SAT.
frames.en: I need to register with the tax office.
frames.note: The SAT is the tax authority; registering gives you an RFC, your tax ID.

frames.es: ¿Me puede hacer factura? Le paso mi constancia de situación fiscal.
frames.en: Could you give me an invoice? I'll send you my tax certificate.
frames.note: The constancia has what an invoice needs: RFC, full name, postcode and tax regime.

frames.es: ¿El precio ya incluye IVA, o es más IVA?
frames.en: Does the price include VAT, or is VAT on top?

frames.es: Firmo siempre y cuando el contrato incluya la opción de renovar.
frames.en: I'll sign as long as the contract includes the option to renew.

frames.es: Con tal de que me deje pagar por transferencia, no hay problema.
frames.en: As long as you let me pay by transfer, that's fine.

frames.es: En caso de que no pague a tiempo, se cobrará un recargo.
frames.en: If you don't pay on time, a surcharge will be charged.
frames.note: Contracts state rules with se + the future: se cobrará, se aplicará.

frames.es: A menos que avise con un mes de anticipación, pierde el depósito.
frames.en: Unless you give a month's notice, you lose the deposit.

frames.es: Tengo que presentar la declaración anual.
frames.en: I have to file my annual tax return.
frames.note: Individuals file in April.

frames.es: ¿Me recomiendas un contador?
frames.en: Can you recommend an accountant?

model_exchanges.situation: Asking for an invoice at a shop

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Me puede hacer factura, por favor?
lines.en: Could you give me an invoice, please?

lines.speaker: cajera
lines.es: Sí, claro. ¿Me da su RFC y su código postal?
lines.en: Yes, of course. Can you give me your RFC and your postcode?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Mejor le paso mi constancia de situación fiscal. ¿Se la mando por WhatsApp?
lines.en: I'd better send you my tax certificate. Shall I send it on WhatsApp?

lines.speaker: cajera
lines.es: Si gusta, también la puede sacar usted en la página, con el número del ticket.
lines.en: If you like, you can also get it yourself on the website, with the receipt number.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Ah, perfecto. ¿Hasta cuándo tengo?
lines.en: Oh, great. How long do I have?

lines.speaker: cajera
lines.es: Nada más dentro del mes de la compra.
lines.en: Only within the month of purchase.

model_exchanges.situation: Renewing a lease with the landlady

lines.speaker: casera
lines.es: Ya le mandé el contrato nuevo. La renta sube un cinco por ciento.
lines.en: I've sent you the new contract. The rent goes up five per cent.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Ya lo leí. Firmo siempre y cuando incluya la opción de renovar otro año.
lines.en: I've read it. I'll sign as long as it includes the option to renew for another year.

lines.speaker: casera
lines.es: Está bien, eso se puede agregar.
lines.en: All right, that can be added.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Y aquí dice que, a menos que avise con dos meses de anticipación, pierdo el depósito. ¿Lo podemos dejar en un mes?
lines.en: And here it says that unless I give two months' notice, I lose the deposit. Can we make it one month?

lines.speaker: casera
lines.es: Mmm… con tal de que me avise por escrito, sí.
lines.en: Hmm… as long as you tell me in writing, yes.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Trato hecho. En cuanto esté corregido, lo firmo.
lines.en: Deal. As soon as it's corrected, I'll sign it.

model_exchanges.situation: Asking a friend about an accountant

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Oye, ¿me recomiendas un contador? Tengo que presentar la declaración anual.
lines.en: Listen, can you recommend an accountant? I have to file my annual return.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Sí, el mío es muy bueno. ¿Ya tienes tu RFC?
lines.en: Yes, mine's very good. Do you have your RFC yet?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí, me di de alta cuando empecé a trabajar por mi cuenta.
lines.en: Yes, I registered when I started working freelance.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Entonces háblale ya, que en abril todo el mundo anda con prisa.
lines.en: Then call him now, because in April everyone's in a rush.

grammar.point: siempre y cuando, con tal de que, a menos que, en caso de que + subjunctive
grammar.explain: These conjunctions set a condition, and the verb after them is always in the subjunctive.

examples.es: Firmo siempre y cuando incluya la renovación.
examples.en: I'll sign provided it includes renewal.

examples.es: Te lo presto con tal de que me lo regreses.
examples.en: I'll lend it to you as long as you give it back.

examples.es: A menos que llueva, nos vemos ahí.
examples.en: Unless it rains, see you there.

grammar.trap: Si is the 'if' word that takes the present indicative; after siempre y cuando, con tal de que, a menos que and en caso de que, use the subjunctive.

grammar.point: the formal future in contracts (se cobrará)
grammar.explain: Contracts and notices state rules with se + the future: se cobrará, se aplicará, se devolverá.

examples.es: Se cobrará un recargo del diez por ciento.
examples.en: A ten per cent surcharge will be charged.

examples.es: El depósito se devolverá al término del contrato.
examples.en: The deposit will be returned at the end of the contract.

grammar.trap: In conversation Mexicans use ir a for the future, so se cobrará sounds like paperwork: understand it, but don't use it for your own plans.

grammar.explain: Contracts and tax forms use fixed words you rarely hear in conversation: el arrendador, el arrendatario, la cláusula, el plazo, presentar la declaración, darse de alta.

examples.es: El arrendatario se obliga a pagar la renta los primeros cinco días de cada mes.
examples.en: The tenant agrees to pay the rent within the first five days of each month.
What does the renewal clause say?

grammar.trap: In a contract the landlord is el arrendador and the tenant el arrendatario; in conversation they're el casero and el inquilino.

vocabulary.en: notice, advance (con un mes de anticipación)
to register (with an authority or service)

pronunciation: Acronyms: SAT and IVA are said as words ('sat', 'í-ba'); RFC and ISR are spelled out: erre-efe-ce, i-ese-erre.
The r at the start of a word is trilled like rr: renta, renovación, recargo. Practise it in the phrase el recargo de la renta.

common_errors.wrong: Firmo siempre y cuando incluye la renovación.
common_errors.right: Firmo siempre y cuando incluya la renovación.
common_errors.why: Siempre y cuando takes the subjunctive.

common_errors.wrong: ¿Me da la cuenta? (meaning a tax invoice)
common_errors.why: La cuenta is the bill in a restaurant; a tax invoice is la factura.
'File taxes' is presentar la declaración; llenar is for forms.

common_errors.wrong: Voy a aplicar para el RFC.
common_errors.why: Aplicar para is a common anglicism in Mexico; for paperwork, tramitar or solicitar is the standard verb.

units.culture: Anyone earning money in Mexico needs an RFC from the SAT, and residents can get one with their residence card. Businesses issue electronic invoices (CFDI) on request: you give your RFC, full name, postcode and tax regime, usually by sending your constancia de situación fiscal, and many shops only invoice within the month of purchase. Individuals file their annual return in April, and most people pay a contador rather than doing it alone.
recycles: b2-04 (Lea las letras chiquitas antes de firmar.)
units.evidence: In a conversation about a contract, invoice or tax, the learner asks for a factura with the right details, sets a condition with siempre y cuando or con tal de que + subjunctive, understands a contract rule read aloud with se + future or a menos que, and negotiates a change politely.
sources: PCIC Gram. C1 (en caso de que); Gram. B2 (siempre que, a no ser que); Gén. C1 (simple rental contracts, insurance, negotiations)
PCIC Nociones específicas B1–B2 (SAT, annual return); C1 15.1–15.2 (IVA, ISR, facturar, contribuyente)
PCIC Saberes 1.6 (taxes), rewritten for Mexico
Word Power 6.10, 1.x (contador, factura as CFDI)

units.title: Residency and bureaucracy in depth
units.can_do: Handle renewals and changes of status, follow official procedures, and get advice on them.
functions: pass on what you've heard, with a hedge
situations: changing from temporary to permanent residence
asking an agent or a friend for advice

frames.es: La tarjeta se me vence en marzo. ¿Cuándo puedo empezar la renovación?
frames.en: My card expires in March. When can I start the renewal?
frames.note: vencerse with accidental se: se me vence, se me venció. The INM takes renewals in the 30 days before the card expires.

frames.es: Quiero cambiar de residente temporal a permanente.
frames.en: I want to change from temporary to permanent resident.
frames.note: The official name is cambio de condición de estancia.

frames.es: ¿Cuánto tarda en salir la resolución?
frames.en: How long does the decision take?

frames.es: Le falta el comprobante del pago de derechos.
frames.en: You're missing the receipt for the fee.

frames.es: Hace falta que traiga la solicitud impresa y firmada.
frames.en: You need to bring the application printed and signed.

frames.es: Le sugiero que contrate a un gestor.
frames.en: I'd suggest you hire an agent.
frames.note: A gestor handles paperwork for a fee; immigration lawyers do the same for residency.

frames.es: Tengo entendido que la solicitud se llena en línea.
frames.en: I understand the application is filled in online.

frames.es: Que yo sepa, el acta tiene que estar apostillada.
frames.en: As far as I know, the certificate has to be apostilled.

frames.es: Se me pasó la fecha. ¿Qué hago?
frames.en: I missed the date. What do I do?
frames.note: pasársele a uno: another accidental se.

model_exchanges.situation: At the INM window, renewing a residence card

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Buenos días. Vengo a renovar mi tarjeta de residente temporal.
lines.en: Good morning. I've come to renew my temporary residence card.

lines.speaker: funcionaria
lines.es: ¿Trae su solicitud impresa y firmada?
lines.en: Have you brought your application printed and signed?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Sí, aquí está. Tengo entendido que también hay que pagar los derechos.
lines.en: Yes, here it is. I understand there's a fee to pay as well.

lines.speaker: funcionaria
lines.es: Así es, y le falta el comprobante del pago. Sin eso no se la puedo recibir.
lines.en: That's right, and you're missing the payment receipt. Without it I can't accept the application.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y dónde se paga?
lines.en: And where do I pay?

lines.speaker: funcionaria
lines.es: En el banco, o aquí en la terminal con tarjeta. En cuanto lo tenga, regrese a esta ventanilla.
lines.en: At the bank, or here at the terminal by card. As soon as you have it, come back to this window.

model_exchanges.situation: Asking a friend who has already changed status

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Ya llevo cuatro años como residente temporal. Quiero cambiar a permanente.
lines.en: I've been a temporary resident for four years now. I want to change to permanent.

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Yo lo hice el año pasado. Te sugiero que contrates a un gestor; te ahorra muchas vueltas.
lines.en: I did it last year. I'd suggest you hire an agent; it saves you a lot of trips.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Cuánto tarda en salir la resolución?
lines.en: How long does the decision take?

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: A mí me la dieron en como un mes, pero depende de la oficina.
lines.en: I got mine in about a month, but it depends on the office.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y me van a pedir el acta de nacimiento? Que yo sepa, tiene que estar apostillada.
lines.en: And will they ask for my birth certificate? As far as I know, it has to be apostilled.

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Para el cambio por cuatro años, que yo sepa, no. Pero si te piden un documento de fuera, que esté apostillado y, si no está en español, traducido por un perito.
lines.en: For the four-year change, not as far as I know. But if they ask for a document from abroad, it has to be apostilled and, if it isn't in Spanish, translated by a certified translator.

grammar.point: bureaucratic register: impersonal se and the passive
grammar.explain: Officials and forms describe procedures without saying who does them, with se + verb, or with ser + participle in writing.

examples.es: La solicitud se llena en línea y se entrega en ventanilla.
examples.en: The application is filled in online and handed in at the window.

grammar.trap: English instructions use 'you'; Spanish ones use se. Se entrega means 'it is handed in', not 'it hands itself in'.

grammar.point: tengo entendido que; que yo sepa
grammar.explain: Tengo entendido que (I understand that) and que yo sepa (as far as I know) state what you've heard while leaving room to be corrected.

examples.es: Tengo entendido que ya no piden carta del banco.
examples.en: I understand they no longer ask for a bank letter.

examples.es: Que yo sepa, no cierran a mediodía.
examples.en: As far as I know, they don't close at midday.

grammar.trap: Que yo sepa is a fixed form with the subjunctive sepa; 'que yo sé' is wrong.

grammar.point: sugerir que / hace falta que + subjunctive
grammar.explain: Advice and requirements put the other person's verb in the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hace falta que traiga dos fotos.
examples.en: You need to bring two photos.

grammar.trap: After sugerir que the verb is subjunctive: le sugiero que contrate, not que contrata.

grammar.point: vencerse and other accidental se verbs
grammar.explain: Documents and deadlines 'expire on you' or 'slip past you': se me vence, se me venció, se me pasó la fecha.
grammar.trap: Expirar exists but sounds odd for documents; Mexicans say vencerse.

vocabulary.en: birth certificate (el acta, but las actas)

vocabulary.form: se me vence, se me venció

vocabulary.en: to make repeated trips (to an office)

pronunciation: INM is spelled out: i-ene-eme. Mexicans say 'Migración' just as often: Tengo cita en Migración.
ll in apostilla and ventanilla sounds like the y in 'yes': a-pos-TI-ya, ven-ta-NI-ya.

common_errors.why: Documents vencen in Mexico, usually with accidental se.

common_errors.wrong: Le sugiero que contrata un gestor.
common_errors.right: Le sugiero que contrate a un gestor.
common_errors.why: Sugerir que takes the subjunctive, and a person as object takes a.

common_errors.wrong: Quiero aplicar para la residencia permanente.
common_errors.why: Aplicar para is a common anglicism; with officials, solicitar or tramitar is the standard verb.

common_errors.wrong: Que yo sé, no hace falta.
common_errors.right: Que yo sepa, no hace falta.
common_errors.why: The hedge is fixed with the subjunctive.

units.culture: Temporary residence covers stays of more than 180 days and up to four years. Renewals are requested at the INM in the 30 days before the card expires, and after four years as a temporary resident you can apply to change to permanent residence. The form is filled in online, then taken printed and signed to the INM office with proof of the fee (pago de derechos); missing the window means a regularisation process and a fine. Many residents pay a gestor or an immigration lawyer to save themselves the vueltas.
recycles: b1-04 (Vengo por lo de mi tarjeta de residente. Le falta una copia de la CURP.)
b2-11 (formal usted; Adjunto los documentos que me solicitó.)
units.evidence: Dealing with an official or asking a friend, the learner asks when and how to renew or change status, understands a requirement given with le falta or hace falta que, uses vencerse with accidental se, and passes on what they've heard with tengo entendido que or que yo sepa.
sources: PCIC Gén. C1 (residence certificates, face-to-face transactions); Nociones generales C1 4.3 (caducar → MX vencerse); Func. C1 1.4 (tengo entendido que); Tác. B2 (que yo sepa); Gram. C1 (hace falta que)
PCIC Saberes 1.1, 2.1.4 (ID documents, dealing with the administration), rewritten for Mexico: INM card, gestores
consulmex.sre.gob.mx (temporary residence: more than 180 days, up to four years; card applied for at INM within 30 calendar days of entry)
tramitaseguro.com, Renovación de residencia en México (renewal in the 30 days before expiry; permanent after four years; form online, filing in person)

units.title: Nuanced debate
units.can_do: Hold your own in a serious discussion: concede and qualify, emphasise what matters, and keep the floor.
situations: a residents' meeting about a city project

frames.es: Si bien es cierto que el turismo trae dinero, también encarece la vida.
frames.en: While it's true that tourism brings money, it also pushes up the cost of living.

frames.es: Lo que me preocupa no es el precio, sino la falta de agua.
frames.en: What worries me isn't the price but the lack of water.

frames.es: Fue el gobierno el que lo propuso, no los vecinos.
frames.en: It was the government that proposed it, not the residents.

frames.es: Por más que lo expliquen, no me convence.
frames.en: However much they explain it, I'm not convinced.

frames.es: Habría que ver de dónde salen esos datos.
frames.en: We'd need to see where that data comes from.

frames.es: Digan lo que digan, el metro sigue siendo lo más rápido.
frames.en: Whatever they say, the metro is still the fastest.

frames.es: No digo que no, pero…
frames.en: I'm not saying no, but…
frames.note: Concede first, then disagree: the Mexican way into a counter-argument.

frames.es: Déjame terminar, que a eso voy.
frames.en: Let me finish, I'm getting to that.
frames.note: que here means 'because': colloquial and very common.

frames.es: Con todo respeto, yo lo veo de otra manera.
frames.en: With all due respect, I see it differently.

model_exchanges.situation: A serious conversation at dinner about tourism and rents

lines.speaker: anfitrión
lines.es: Yo digo que tanto turismo es bueno para la colonia: hay más negocios, más trabajo.
lines.en: I say all this tourism is good for the neighbourhood: more businesses, more jobs.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Si bien es cierto que el turismo trae dinero, también encarece la vida. Las rentas subieron muchísimo.
lines.en: While it's true that tourism brings money, it also pushes up the cost of living. Rents have gone up enormously.

lines.speaker: anfitriona
lines.es: Bueno, pero eso pasa en todas las ciudades del mundo.
lines.en: Well, but that happens in every city in the world.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: No digo que no. Pero lo que me preocupa no es el precio, sino el agua.
lines.en: I'm not saying it doesn't. But what worries me isn't the price, it's the water.

lines.speaker: anfitrión
lines.es: ¿El agua? ¿Y eso qué tiene que ver?
lines.en: The water? What's that got to do with it?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Déjame terminar, que a eso voy: con tantos edificios nuevos, ya hay tandeo en varias colonias.
lines.en: Let me finish, I'm getting to that: with so many new buildings, several neighbourhoods already have water rationing.

lines.speaker: anfitriona
lines.es: Eso sí es cierto. Y fue la alcaldía la que dio los permisos, ¿no?
lines.en: That's true. And it was the borough that gave the permits, wasn't it?

model_exchanges.situation: A community forum about a new bus line

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: Según el estudio, el tráfico va a bajar un treinta por ciento.
lines.en: According to the study, traffic will drop by thirty per cent.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Habría que ver de dónde salen esos datos. ¿Quién hizo el estudio?
lines.en: We'd need to see where that data comes from. Who did the study?

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: La misma empresa que va a construir la línea.
lines.en: The same company that's going to build the line.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Pues por más que lo expliquen, a mí no me convence.
lines.en: Well, however much they explain it, I'm not convinced.

lines.speaker: vecina
lines.es: Perdón, pero digan lo que digan, el transporte público sigue siendo lo más rápido.
lines.en: Sorry, but whatever they say, public transport is still the fastest.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Con todo respeto, no es que esté en contra, sino que quiero ver los números.
lines.en: With all due respect, it's not that I'm against it; I want to see the figures.

grammar.point: clefts: lo que … es / no es … sino; fue … el que
grammar.explain: To put one idea in focus, Spanish wraps it in lo que … es (or no es … sino), or puts it between ser and el que / la que / los que.

examples.es: Lo que me molesta es el ruido.
examples.en: What bothers me is the noise.

examples.es: Fue la alcaldía la que dio el permiso.
examples.en: It was the borough that gave the permit.

examples.es: Son los vecinos los que pagan.

grammar.trap: Spanish needs the article: fue el gobierno el que, not fue el gobierno que. And it agrees with the noun: fue la alcaldía la que.

grammar.explain: Si bien concedes a point before you qualify it, and it takes the indicative.

examples.es: Si bien es cierto que hay más trabajo, los sueldos no subieron.
examples.en: While it's true there's more work, wages haven't gone up.

examples.es: Si bien la idea es buena, el plan tiene problemas.
examples.en: Although the idea is good, the plan has problems.

grammar.trap: Si bien isn't 'if well' and has nothing to do with conditions: it means 'although'.

grammar.explain: Por más que (however much) takes the subjunctive for 'whatever happens' and the indicative for something that did happen.

examples.es: Por más que insistas, no voy a ir.
examples.en: However much you insist, I'm not going.

examples.es: Por más que lo intenté, no pude.
examples.en: Hard as I tried, I couldn't.

grammar.trap: 'No importa cuánto' is understood, but por más que is what you hear in a real argument.

grammar.explain: A verb repeated in the subjunctive around lo que, como or donde means 'whatever', 'however' or 'wherever'.

examples.es: Digan lo que digan, yo voy a votar.
examples.en: Whatever they say, I'm going to vote.

examples.es: Sea como sea, hay que decidir hoy.
examples.en: Be that as it may, we have to decide today.

examples.es: Pase lo que pase, te aviso.
examples.en: Whatever happens, I'll let you know.

grammar.trap: Both verbs are subjunctive and identical: digan lo que digan, not dicen lo que digan.

grammar.explain: Habría que (we'd have to, someone should) proposes an action without pointing at anyone.

examples.es: Habría que preguntarles a los vecinos.

grammar.trap: Hay que is a plain 'you have to'; habría que softens it into a suggestion, which suits Mexican indirectness.

vocabulary.form: no es que esté en contra

pronunciation: In a cleft the stress falls on what's in focus: FUE el GOBIERNO el que lo propuso; lo que me preocupa es el AGUA. Mexicans add emphasis with word order and sí, not with a higher pitch, which can sound angry.
Holding the floor is partly melody: keep the end of the phrase level (suspended) to show you haven't finished: lo que me preocupa →, déjame terminar.

common_errors.wrong: Fue el gobierno que lo propuso.
common_errors.right: Fue el gobierno el que lo propuso.
common_errors.why: Spanish clefts need the article before que.

common_errors.wrong: Dicen lo que digan, no me importa.
common_errors.right: Digan lo que digan, no me importa.
common_errors.why: Both verbs are subjunctive.

common_errors.wrong: Si bien es cierto que el turismo traiga dinero…
common_errors.right: Si bien es cierto que el turismo trae dinero…
common_errors.why: Si bien and es cierto que both state a fact, so the verb is indicative.

common_errors.right: Con todo respeto, yo lo veo de otra manera.
common_errors.why: Flat contradiction sounds aggressive in Mexico; concede or soften first.

units.culture: Mexicans enjoy talking about politics and city issues, but disagreement is softened: concede a point first (si bien es cierto que…, no digo que no…), criticise institutions rather than the person in front of you, and don't tell someone they're wrong in front of others. Criticism of Mexico from a foreigner lands harder than the same words from a Mexican, so ask questions and present your view as your own.
recycles: b2-06 (Por un lado… por otro; No es que no me guste, sino que…; Lo que pasa es que…)
units.evidence: In a real disagreement, the learner concedes before contradicting (si bien, no digo que no), puts the key point in focus with a cleft, uses digan lo que digan or por más que correctly, and keeps or takes back the floor politely.
sources: PCIC Gram. C1 (digan lo que digan; si bien; cuyo, el cual, lo cual); Gram. B2 (por más que, a pesar de que); Func. C1 2.10–2.12 (no me convence, yo no digo que…, pero; counter-arguments)

PCIC Gén. C1 (negotiations; argumentative text: si bien es cierto que…, no olvidemos que…); Obj. C1 (holding the floor); Tác. C1 (ahora bien; dialogic softening: no, yo no digo que eso esté mal, pero…)
Seven Keys ch. 3 and 4 (discutir = argue; harmony; criticise in private)

units.title: Humour, irony and wordplay
units.can_do: Get the jokes, sarcasm and teasing, and join in with light humour.
functions: take teasing well and tease back
situations: friends teasing each other at a carne asada
a calaverita at the office for Día de Muertos

frames.es: ¡Ay, sí, cómo no!
frames.en: Oh yeah, sure! (sarcastic)
frames.note: Drawn out with a falling tone it's sarcasm; quick and bright, sí, cómo no is a real 'of course'.

frames.es: ¡Qué esperanza!
frames.en: Not a chance!
frames.note: Mexican and a little old-fashioned.

frames.es: Es broma, no te creas.
frames.en: Just kidding, don't take it seriously.

frames.es: ¡Me la creí!
frames.en: I fell for it!

frames.es: ¿Es en serio o me estás vacilando?
frames.en: Are you serious or are you pulling my leg?
frames.note: vacilar in Mexico = to tease, to joke with someone.

frames.es: Le echaste mucha crema a tus tacos.
frames.en: You're showing off a bit there. (lit. you put a lot of cream on your tacos)

frames.es: Será muy listo, pero no sabe ni freír un huevo.
frames.en: He may be clever, but he can't even fry an egg.
frames.note: The future here grants a point only to knock it down.

frames.es: Al que le quede el saco, que se lo ponga.
frames.en: If the cap fits, wear it.

frames.es: Te lo digo, Juan, para que lo entiendas, Pedro.
frames.en: I'm saying it to one person so that another will get it.

model_exchanges.situation: Friends teasing each other at a carne asada

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Oye, ¿es cierto que ya te invitaron a cantar con el mariachi?
lines.en: Hey, is it true they've asked you to sing with the mariachi?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Neta? ¿Es en serio o me estás vacilando?
lines.en: Really? Are you serious or are you pulling my leg?

lines.speaker: amigo
lines.es: Es broma, no te creas.
lines.en: Just kidding, don't believe it.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Me la creí! Ya me veía con el sombrero.
lines.en: I fell for it! I could already see myself in the sombrero.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Bueno, cantar no cantas, pero ¿bailar? ¡Qué esperanza!
lines.en: Well, you can't sing, but dance? Not a chance!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Serás muy buena para criticar, pero en la fiesta de Lupe tú tampoco bailaste.
lines.en: You may be great at criticising, but you didn't dance at Lupe's party either.

model_exchanges.situation: A calaverita at the office for Día de Muertos

lines.speaker: compañera
lines.es: Te tocó a ti en las calaveritas de la oficina. ¿Quieres oírla?
lines.en: You got picked for the office calaveritas. Want to hear yours?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: A ver, ¿qué me escribieron?
lines.en: Go on, what did you write about me?

lines.speaker: compañera
lines.es: «La Flaca llegó a la oficina / con ganas de trabajar, / pero vio tu escritorio / y mejor se fue a almorzar.»
lines.en: 'Death came to the office / ready to do her job, / but she saw your desk / and went off for a snack instead.'

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Ja! Pero mi escritorio no está tan mal, ¿o sí?
lines.en: Ha! But my desk isn't that bad, is it?

lines.speaker: compañera
lines.es: No, ¿cómo crees? Está impecable. Pero al que le quede el saco, que se lo ponga.
lines.en: No, of course not. It's spotless. But if the cap fits, wear it.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Ay, sí, cómo no! Ya entendí la indirecta.
lines.en: Oh yeah, sure! I get the hint.

grammar.explain: Positive words mean the opposite when they're drawn out with a falling tone, and a diminutive can sound sarcastic rather than affectionate.

examples.en: Oh yeah, sure. (= I don't believe you)
How kind of the gentleman! (about someone rude)
Poor thing, he works three hours a day!

grammar.trap: English speakers miss the irony because the words are positive; listen to the tone and the situation, not the words.

grammar.point: the future of objection (será muy listo, pero …)
grammar.explain: Será muy + adjective, pero … grants a point only to knock it down: 'he may be …, but …'.

examples.es: Será muy bonito, pero es carísimo.
examples.en: It may be very nice, but it's really expensive.

examples.es: Tendrá mucho dinero, pero no tiene educación.
examples.en: He may have a lot of money, but he has no manners.

grammar.trap: It has nothing to do with the future: será here means 'he may well be'. And educación here means manners, not schooling.

grammar.point: calaveritas literarias: rhyming Day of the Dead verses
grammar.explain: For Día de Muertos people write short rhyming verses in which Death comes for friends, colleagues or politicians; it's affectionate mockery, and the target is expected to laugh.

examples.es: La Flaca llegó a la oficina / con ganas de trabajar,
examples.en: Death came to the office / ready to do her job,

examples.es: pero vio tanto papeleo / que mejor se fue a almorzar.
examples.en: but she saw so much paperwork / she went off for a snack instead.

grammar.trap: A calaverita about you isn't a death wish or an insult. Death has nicknames: la Flaca, la Calaca, la Catrina, la Huesuda.

grammar.point: albures: recognise that they exist; don't attempt them
grammar.explain: Albures are fast double-meaning wordplay, mostly sexual, traded as a contest of wit; a newcomer should know they exist, laugh along and not try them.

examples.en: Is that a double meaning aimed at me?

grammar.trap: Innocent words can set one off. If everyone laughs at something you said, that's probably why: laugh along and move on.

vocabulary.en: Day of the Dead verse; sugar skull
Death (nickname; also la Calaca, la Catrina)
annoying, too much (of a person or joke)

pronunciation: Sarcasm is in the melody: ¡Ay, sííí, cómo nooo! is stretched and falls at the end; a genuine 'of course' is short and bright.
Mexican teasing is often deadpan, said flat with a straight face; a serious face doesn't mean it's serious.

common_errors.why: The expression is fixed with la.

common_errors.wrong: Es un chiste, no te crees.
common_errors.why: A negative command takes the subjunctive, and a joke made in the moment is una broma.

common_errors.wrong: ¡Gracias! (in reply to a sarcastic ¡Ay, sí, cómo no!)
common_errors.why: It was sarcasm: the speaker doesn't believe you.

common_errors.wrong: Joking about Mexico, someone's mother or the Virgin
common_errors.right: Joking about yourself or the situation
common_errors.why: Only Mexicans get to mock Mexico, and mothers and the Virgin of Guadalupe are off limits.

units.culture: Mexicans tease the people they like (echar carrilla), and taking it well, or teasing back, is how you show you belong. Dark humour about death is normal, above all in the calaveritas of Día de Muertos. Two lines a foreigner shouldn't cross: jokes about Mexico itself, and jokes about someone's mother or the Virgin of Guadalupe.
recycles: b2-07 (sí, cómo no as a soft no; never joke about someone's mother)
units.evidence: The learner reacts to sarcasm or teasing as such (not literally), says they were joking with es broma, no te creas, admits being fooled with me la creí, and at least once teases back gently, for example with the future of objection.
sources: Seven Keys ch. 4 (B2: echarle crema a los tacos, al que le quede el saco, calaveritas, crisis jokes; C1: te digo Juan para que entiendas Pedro; humour taboos)

PCIC Tác. C1–C2 (¡qué esperanza! [México]; irony 1.8.2; ironic diminutives); Gram. C1 (future of objection: será muy listo pero…); Obj. C1 (understanding humour and implicit meaning); Pron. C (ironic intonation)
PCIC Nociones generales C1 6.9 (doble sentido)

units.title: Storytelling with flair
units.can_do: Tell a story the way Mexicans do among friends: vivid, in the present, with voices and asides.
functions: keep a story going as a listener
situations: a story about a run-in with bureaucracy

frames.es: No te lo vas a creer.
frames.en: You won't believe it.

frames.es: Pues nada, que llego a la oficina y me dicen que ya cerraron.
frames.en: So anyway, I get to the office and they tell me they've closed.
frames.note: The historical present makes the action vivid.

frames.es: Y yo así de: «¿Cómo que ya cerraron?»
frames.en: And I'm like: 'What do you mean, closed?'

frames.es: Y que me dice: «Regrese mañana».
frames.en: And he goes: 'Come back tomorrow.'
frames.note: y que me dice: a very Mexican way to bring in a quote.

frames.es: Total que acabé esperando tres horas.
frames.en: So in the end I waited three hours.

frames.es: Ni te cuento lo que pasó después.
frames.en: Don't even ask what happened next.

frames.es: ¡Y yo qué sabía!
frames.en: How was I supposed to know!

frames.es: Iba a decirle que no, pero…
frames.en: I was going to say no, but…

model_exchanges.situation: After dinner: a run-in at the bank

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: No te lo vas a creer. Ayer fui al banco a abrir la cuenta.
lines.en: You won't believe it. Yesterday I went to the bank to open the account.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: ¿Y? ¿Qué pasó?
lines.en: And? What happened?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Pues nada, que llego, hago la fila una hora, y cuando por fin me toca, el señor me dice que no hay sistema.
lines.en: So anyway, I get there, queue for an hour, and when it's finally my turn, the man tells me the system is down.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: ¡No inventes!
lines.en: No way!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Y yo así de: «¿Cómo que no hay sistema?» Y que me dice: «Regrese mañana».
lines.en: And I'm like: 'What do you mean, the system's down?' And he goes: 'Come back tomorrow.'

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: ¿Y no te enojaste?
lines.en: And didn't you get angry?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Iba a decirle algo, pero me aguanté. Total que hoy regresé y en cinco minutos me la abrieron.
lines.en: I was going to say something, but I held back. So in the end I went back today and they opened it in five minutes.

model_exchanges.situation: Telling a neighbour about a mistake at the market

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Ni te cuento lo que me pasó en el tianguis.
lines.en: You won't believe what happened to me at the street market.

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: A ver, cuéntame.
lines.en: Go on, tell me.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Le pido a la señora un kilo de chiles habaneros, y ella así de: «¿Un kilo? ¿Seguro?»
lines.en: I ask the lady for a kilo of habaneros, and she's like: 'A kilo? Are you sure?'

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: ¡Un kilo de habaneros! ¿Para qué querías tantos?
lines.en: A kilo of habaneros! What did you want so many for?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Y yo qué sabía! Yo pensaba que no picaban tanto.
lines.en: How was I supposed to know! I thought they weren't that hot.

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: ¿Y luego? ¿Cuántos te llevaste?
lines.en: And then? How many did you take?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Tres. Y con uno lloré toda la comida.
lines.en: Three. And one of them had me in tears all through lunch.

grammar.explain: In a lively story Mexicans switch from the past to the present for the main action, as if it were happening now.

examples.es: Ayer voy al banco y ¿qué crees? Está cerrado.
examples.en: Yesterday I go to the bank and guess what? It's closed.

examples.es: Llego, me siento, y en eso se va la luz.
examples.en: I arrive, I sit down, and just then the power goes out.

grammar.trap: Set the scene in the past first (ayer fui…), then switch; jumping back and forth in every sentence makes the story hard to follow.

grammar.point: the imperfect of excuse (¡y yo qué sabía!)
grammar.explain: The imperfect of saber, pensar or creer explains what you didn't know at the time: it's how you excuse yourself.

examples.en: How was I supposed to know!

examples.es: Nadie me dijo que había que hacer cita.
examples.en: Nobody told me you had to book.

grammar.trap: The preterite changes the meaning: supe means 'I found out', so 'y yo qué supe' doesn't work.

grammar.explain: Iba a + infinitive is what you were going to do, usually before something stopped you.

examples.es: Iba a llamarte, pero se me acabó la pila.
examples.en: I was going to call you, but my battery died.

examples.es: Íbamos a salir cuando empezó a llover.
examples.en: We were about to go out when it started to rain.

grammar.trap: Don't drop the a: iba a decirle, not iba decirle.

grammar.point: quoted speech: y yo así de…, y que me dice…, ¿cómo que…?
grammar.explain: In stories Mexicans act out the dialogue: y yo así de or y que me dice brings in a quote, and ¿cómo que…? repeats someone's words in disbelief.

examples.es: Y que me dice: «Aquí no se puede».
examples.en: And he goes: 'You can't do that here.'
What do you mean, the system's down?

grammar.trap: Don't translate 'I was like' as 'yo estaba como': in Mexico it's y yo así de.

grammar.point: story markers: pues nada, total que, o sea, y así
grammar.explain: Small words structure a story: pues nada starts the action, total que jumps to the outcome, o sea clarifies, and y así or y no sé qué skips the boring part.

examples.es: Pues nada, que llego y no hay nadie.
examples.en: So anyway, I arrive and there's nobody there.

examples.es: Total que me regresé a mi casa.
examples.en: So in the end I went back home.

examples.es: Me pidieron copias, fotos y no sé qué.
examples.en: They asked me for copies, photos and whatnot.

grammar.trap: Pues nada doesn't mean 'well, nothing': it's a way to get into the story.

vocabulary.en: to hold back, put up with it
don't even ask, you won't believe
and then? (to keep a story going)

pronunciation: When you quote someone, change your voice and pause before the quote: y yo así de… «¿Cómo que no hay sistema?» The pause does the work of English 'like'.
In fast highland speech pues often shrinks to p's: p's nada, p's sí. Recognise it; you don't need to copy it.

common_errors.why: 'Was like' is a calque; Mexicans say así de.
ir a + infinitive keeps its a.
The excuse uses the imperfect.
A reported request takes the subjunctive (past after dijo).

units.culture: Among friends a story is a performance: the teller switches to the present for the action, acts out everyone's voice, and the listeners keep it going with ¿Y luego?, ¡No inventes! or ¡No te creo! A story told flatly, or a listener who stays silent, feels cold. Stories about your own mistakes in Spanish go down especially well.
recycles: b1-07 (¿A que no sabes qué me pasó? Fíjate que… Total que llegué dos horas tarde. ¡No te creo!)
units.evidence: Telling something that happened, the learner sets the scene in the past, switches to the present for the action, quotes people with y yo así de or y que me dice, uses at least one excuse or iba a…, and rounds off with total que; as a listener they keep the story going with ¿Y luego?
sources: PCIC Gén. A2 → C1 (beach anecdote ladder; C1 narrative: no te lo vas a creer, pues nada, total que, y tal y cual, ¿a que no sabes…?); Tác. C1 1.5 (direct speech brought in by intonation; Mexican y yo así de / y que…)
PCIC Gram. C1 (historical present; imperfect of excuse: ¡y yo qué sabía!); Func. C1 1.3.1 (¡¿Cómo que…?!); Gram. B2 (iba a)
PCIC Func. C1 6.11 (Spain's va y… / coge y… → Mexican y que me dice, y luego luego)

units.title: History and identity
units.can_do: Talk about Mexican history and how it shapes the present, ask informed questions, and handle sensitive topics with care.
functions: say what you know, with a hedge

frames.es: Muchas palabras vienen del náhuatl: chocolate, aguacate, tomate.
frames.en: Many words come from Nahuatl: chocolate, avocado, tomato.

frames.es: Quienes vivieron el temblor del 85 todavía hablan de él.
frames.en: People who lived through the 1985 earthquake still talk about it.

frames.es: ¡2 de octubre no se olvida!
frames.en: We won't forget 2 October!
frames.note: Chanted every year at the march for the students killed at Tlatelolco in 1968.

frames.es: ¿Qué opinas de cómo se cuenta la Revolución en las escuelas?
frames.en: What do you think of how the Revolution is taught in schools?

frames.es: Mucha gente aquí tiene familia del otro lado.
frames.en: Lots of people here have family in the US.
frames.note: el otro lado = the United States.

frames.es: ¿Me recomiendas un libro para entender el 68?
frames.en: Can you recommend a book to help me understand 1968?

frames.es: Hasta donde sé, el 19 de septiembre ha temblado fuerte tres veces: en 1985, en 2017 y en 2022.
frames.en: As far as I know, there have been three strong earthquakes on 19 September: in 1985, 2017 and 2022.
frames.note: That's why the national earthquake drill is held around that date.

frames.es: Benito Juárez, cuyo natalicio es día feriado, era zapoteco.
frames.en: Benito Juárez, whose birthday is a public holiday, was Zapotec.

frames.es: A quien prefiere todo lo extranjero le dicen malinchista.
frames.en: Someone who prefers everything foreign gets called a malinchista.
frames.note: From La Malinche, Cortés's interpreter: a disputed figure, so use the word carefully.

model_exchanges.situation: At the National Museum of Anthropology with a Mexican friend

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: No sabía que tantas palabras venían del náhuatl.
lines.en: I didn't know so many words came from Nahuatl.

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Uy, un montón: chocolate, aguacate, chile… y aquí decimos jitomate, que también es náhuatl.
lines.en: Oh, loads: chocolate, avocado, chilli… and here we say jitomate, which is Nahuatl too.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y todavía se habla mucho?
lines.en: And is it still widely spoken?

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Sí, lo hablan más de un millón y medio de personas, sobre todo en Puebla, Veracruz e Hidalgo.
lines.en: Yes, more than a million and a half people speak it, mainly in Puebla, Veracruz and Hidalgo.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y en tu familia?
lines.en: And in your family?

lines.speaker: amiga
lines.es: Mi abuela lo hablaba; mi mamá lo entiende, pero ya no lo habla. Es una lástima.
lines.en: My grandmother spoke it; my mum understands it but doesn't speak it any more. It's a shame.

model_exchanges.situation: The earthquake drill at the office on 19 September

lines.speaker: compañero
lines.es: Hoy es el simulacro. Cuando suene la alerta, todos al punto de reunión.
lines.en: Today's the drill. When the alarm goes off, everyone to the assembly point.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Hasta donde sé, el 19 de septiembre ha temblado fuerte tres veces.
lines.en: As far as I know, there have been three strong earthquakes on 19 September.

lines.speaker: compañero
lines.es: Sí. Quienes vivieron el del 85 no lo olvidan. Mi papá ayudó a sacar gente de los edificios.
lines.en: Yes. People who lived through the one in 85 don't forget it. My dad helped pull people out of the buildings.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y en 2017 dónde estabas?
lines.en: And where were you in 2017?

lines.speaker: compañero
lines.es: Aquí mismo. Dos horas antes habíamos hecho el simulacro, y luego tembló de verdad.
lines.en: Right here. Two hours earlier we'd done the drill, and then there was a real one.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡Qué impresión! Con razón todos se lo toman tan en serio.
lines.en: How shocking! No wonder everyone takes it so seriously.

model_exchanges.situation: Asking a neighbour carefully about migration

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Si no es indiscreción, ¿tiene familia del otro lado?
lines.en: If you don't mind my asking, do you have family in the US?

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: Sí, dos hermanos en Chicago. Se fueron hace veinte años.
lines.en: Yes, two brothers in Chicago. They left twenty years ago.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y los ve seguido?
lines.en: And do you see them often?

lines.speaker: vecino
lines.es: Vienen en diciembre, cuando pueden. Lo que mandaban ayudó mucho a mi mamá.
lines.en: They come in December when they can. What they sent home helped my mum a lot.

grammar.explain: History is told in the preterite, and when the doer doesn't matter, with se or ser + participle.

examples.es: Tenochtitlan fue fundada sobre un lago.
examples.en: Tenochtitlan was founded on a lake.

examples.es: Después del 85 se cambiaron las normas de construcción.
examples.en: After 1985 the building codes were changed.

grammar.trap: A single historical event takes the preterite: la Revolución empezó en 1910, not empezaba.

grammar.explain: Quienes means 'those who' for people; cuyo (whose) agrees with the thing owned; el cual / la cual is a formal 'which', mostly after prepositions.

examples.es: Quienes vivieron el 68 lo recuerdan bien.
examples.en: Those who lived through 1968 remember it well.

examples.es: Juárez, cuyas leyes separaron la Iglesia del Estado, …
examples.en: Juárez, whose laws separated Church and State, …

examples.es: la plaza en la cual murieron los estudiantes
examples.en: the square in which the students died

grammar.trap: Cuyo agrees with what's owned, not with the owner: Juárez, cuyas leyes…, not cuyo leyes.

grammar.explain: Hasta donde sé (as far as I know) hedges your own knowledge; según + a source attributes a claim to someone else.

examples.en: As far as I know, it was in 1968.

examples.es: Según mi suegro, antes aquí había un río.
examples.en: According to my father-in-law, there used to be a river here.

grammar.trap: Según takes subject pronouns: según tú, según ella; según yo is common and colloquial in Mexico. Never según ti.

vocabulary.en: to shake; for an earthquake to happen

pronunciation: Words ending in tl, like náhuatl, end in one sound: the tongue is in the l position and the air escapes at the sides. Say NÁ-watl, not ná-wa-tel.
Mexicans name events by the last two digits of the year: el 68 (sesenta y ocho), el 85 (ochenta y cinco), el temblor del 17 (diecisiete).

common_errors.wrong: Hablaban náhuatl antes de los españoles llegaron.
common_errors.right: Hablaban náhuatl antes de que llegaran los españoles.
common_errors.why: antes de que takes the subjunctive.
Cuyo agrees with the thing owned.
Single events in history take the preterite.

common_errors.wrong: (to someone you've just met) ¿Por qué tanta gente se va a Estados Unidos?
common_errors.right: Si no es indiscreción, ¿tiene familia del otro lado?
common_errors.why: Migration is personal for many families; ask gently and about their story.

units.culture: History is part of daily life in Mexico: streets are named after dates (5 de Mayo, 16 de Septiembre, 20 de Noviembre), 19 September brings the national earthquake drill and memories of 1985 and 2017, and every 2 October there's a march for the students killed in 1968. Knowing the basics earns real respect, and newcomers from the US especially should know about the war of 1846–48 and the Niños Héroes. Ask questions and let Mexicans lead any criticism of their own history.
recycles: b2-10 (El Grito se da la noche del 15 de septiembre. La ciudad fue fundada por los mexicas. Según cuentan…)
b2-13 (¿Ya supiste lo del temblor de anoche?)
units.evidence: In a conversation about the past or a commemoration, the learner tells events in the preterite and passive, uses a relative such as quienes or cuyo correctly, hedges with hasta donde sé or según, and raises a sensitive subject (migration, 1968, the earthquakes) with care.
sources: PCIC Referentes culturales (Olmecs, Maya, Mexica; Moctezuma, Zapata, the Revolution, 1968, Paz; missing and added here: 19 September, La Malinche, Juárez, migration); Nociones específicas B1–B2 (remesas, inmigrante)
PCIC Saberes 1.10 (civil protection: 19 September drills), rewritten for Mexico
PCIC Gram. C1 (quienes, cuyo, el cual)
Seven Keys ch. 3 and 7 (history lives in the present; Niños Héroes; learn history to earn respect)
EFE and Uno TV reports on the three 19 September earthquakes (1985, 2017, 2022)

units.title: Regional varieties and indigenous languages
units.can_do: Recognise how Spanish varies across Mexico and the Spanish-speaking world, and pronounce Nahuatl and Maya place names.
functions: ask about local words and languages
situations: meeting people from Spain or Argentina
a market where indigenous languages are spoken

frames.es: ¿Cómo se pronuncia «Xochimilco»?
frames.en: How do you pronounce 'Xochimilco'?

frames.es: Muchos nombres de lugares vienen del náhuatl: Tlalpan, Coyoacán, Mixcoac.
frames.en: Many place names come from Nahuatl: Tlalpan, Coyoacán, Mixcoac.

frames.es: En el norte hablan más golpeado.
frames.en: In the north they speak more bluntly.
frames.note: golpeado: loud, clipped and direct; normal there, not rude.

frames.es: En Yucatán se usan muchas palabras del maya.
frames.en: In Yucatán they use lots of Maya words.

frames.es: ¿Vosotros sois de aquí?
frames.en: Are you from here? (Spain's plural 'you')
frames.note: Recognise only. In Mexico: ¿Ustedes son de aquí?

frames.es: ¿Vos sos de acá?
frames.en: Are you from here? (Argentina, Central America)
frames.note: vos replaces tú, with its own verb forms.

frames.es: En Chiapas mucha gente usa el vos.
frames.en: In Chiapas a lot of people use vos.

frames.es: ¿Así se dice aquí o nada más en la capital?
frames.en: Is that how you say it here, or only in the capital?

frames.es: ¿Qué lengua se habla en esta región?
frames.en: What language is spoken in this region?

model_exchanges.situation: Asking a taxi driver about place names in Mexico City

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Disculpe, ¿cómo se pronuncia «Xola»? ¿Con equis?
lines.en: Excuse me, how do you pronounce 'Xola'? With an x sound?

lines.speaker: taxista
lines.es: Se dice «Shola», como sh. Pero Xochimilco se dice con s.
lines.en: It's 'Shola', like sh. But Xochimilco is said with an s.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y por qué cambia?
lines.en: And why does it change?

lines.speaker: taxista
lines.es: Son nombres del náhuatl. Los españoles los escribieron como pudieron.
lines.en: They're Nahuatl names. The Spanish wrote them down as best they could.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y «Tlalpan»? Me cuesta la tl.
lines.en: And 'Tlalpan'? I find the tl hard.

lines.speaker: taxista
lines.es: Dígalo junto, sin meterle vocal: Tlal-pan.
lines.en: Say it together, without putting a vowel in: Tlal-pan.

model_exchanges.situation: Meeting a couple from Spain in a café

lines.speaker: española
lines.es: ¿Vosotros sois de aquí?
lines.en: Are you two from here?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Yo no, yo vivo aquí desde hace un tiempo. Ella sí es de aquí.
lines.en: Not me, I've been living here for a while. She is from here.

lines.speaker: mexicana
lines.es: Sí, soy de Puebla. ¿Y ustedes de dónde son?
lines.en: Yes, I'm from Puebla. And where are you from?

lines.speaker: español
lines.es: De Madrid. Oye, ¿aquí cómo llamáis al autobús?
lines.en: From Madrid. Hey, what do you call the bus here?

lines.speaker: mexicana
lines.es: Le decimos camión. Y aquí todo el mundo es ustedes, nada de vosotros.
lines.en: We call it camión. And here it's ustedes for everyone, no vosotros.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Al principio se me hacía raro el vosotros, pero ya les entiendo todo.
lines.en: At first vosotros sounded strange to me, but now I understand everything you say.

model_exchanges.situation: At a market in Oaxaca where Zapotec is spoken

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Qué lengua están hablando las señoras?
lines.en: What language are the ladies speaking?

lines.speaker: vendedor
lines.es: Zapoteco. Aquí en el valle mucha gente lo habla en su casa.
lines.en: Zapotec. Here in the valley lots of people speak it at home.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¿Y cómo se dice «gracias» en zapoteco?
lines.en: And how do you say 'thank you' in Zapotec?

lines.speaker: vendedor
lines.es: Depende del pueblo; cada uno tiene su variante. Pregúntele a doña Rosa, ella le enseña.
lines.en: It depends on the village; each one has its own variant. Ask Doña Rosa, she'll teach you.

grammar.point: recognising vosotros forms (sois, tenéis, habláis) and voseo (vos sos, tenés)
grammar.explain: Spain uses vosotros for 'you all' among friends, and Argentina and much of Central America use vos for 'you'; both have their own verb forms.

examples.en: = tú eres / tienes / hablas (Argentina, Central America, Chiapas)
What would you all like to drink? (Spain)

grammar.trap: Recognise them, don't adopt them: in Mexico vosotros sounds Spanish and theatrical, and vos is regional. Keep ustedes and tú.

grammar.point: x in Mexican names: /x/ (México), /s/ (Xochimilco), /ʃ/ (Xola); tl and tz
grammar.explain: In names from Nahuatl and Maya, x can sound like Spanish j, like s, or like English sh, so each name has to be learned; tl and tz are single sounds.

examples.en: x like Spanish j: MÉ-ji-co, wa-JA-ka, ja-LA-pa
x like English sh: SHO-la; Maya names starting X- begin ish-: ish-ka-RET
tl and tz as single sounds

grammar.trap: México with x is the official, historical spelling; it's never 'Mek-si-co' in Spanish.

grammar.point: regional accents: northern, coastal (aspirated s), Yucatec
grammar.explain: Mexico City and the highlands keep a strong s and can weaken unstressed vowels; the Gulf and Pacific coasts aspirate or drop s at the end of a syllable; the north sounds louder and more clipped; Yucatán has sharp stops and breaks from Maya.

examples.en: coastal: final s becomes a breath or disappears

grammar.trap: An aspirated s isn't sloppy speech; it's the local norm. Keep your own clear s, but don't correct anyone else's.

grammar.explain: The official catalogue (drawn up by INALI in 2008) lists 68 indigenous languages with 364 variants, all national languages by law; the most spoken are Nahuatl, Maya, Tseltal, Tsotsil, Mixtec and Zapotec.

examples.es: En la sierra se habla zapoteco.
examples.en: Zapotec is spoken in the mountains.
How do you say 'thank you' in Maya?

grammar.trap: Don't call these languages dialectos, and never say indio: say indígena, or name the people and the language (una señora mixteca, un hablante de náhuatl).

vocabulary.en: Tsotsil (language of Chiapas); also spelled tzotzil

pronunciation: x in Mexican names: like j in México, Oaxaca and Xalapa; like s in Xochimilco and Taxco; like English sh in Xola and in Maya names such as Xcaret.
tl is one consonant, at the start of a word or at the end: Tlal-pan, Ná-watl, Po-po-ca-TÉ-petl. Don't slip a vowel in (te-lal-pan).

common_errors.why: The x of México is a Spanish j.
Mexico uses only ustedes for plural 'you'.

common_errors.right: Hablan zapoteco. / Hablan una lengua indígena.
common_errors.why: Calling indigenous languages dialectos is dismissive; they are languages.
Indio is offensive in Mexico.

units.culture: Mexico recognises 68 indigenous languages as national languages, and more than seven million people speak one; in markets in Oaxaca, Chiapas, Yucatán or Puebla you'll hear them every day. Mexicans are proud of regional differences and tease each other about them (chilangos, norteños, costeños), and they're happy to explain a local word if you ask. Calling an indigenous language a dialecto is a common and hurtful slip.
recycles: b2-12 (cuate; fast highland speech: p's, nec'sito)
a1-11 (Nahuatl place names on the metro)
units.evidence: The learner pronounces common Nahuatl place names with the right x and tl, understands a Spanish or Argentinian speaker using vosotros or vos without switching to those forms, and asks about local words or languages respectfully, without dialecto or indio.
sources: PCIC Pron. C (Nahuatl x; aspirated j in most of Mexico); Pron. B (tense s in the highlands, aspirated on the coasts; weak unstressed vowels in the highlands); Referentes (indigenous languages largely missing; lacandones)
PCIC pcic-1 variety notes (voseo in Chiapas; ustedes only)
Seven Keys ch. 1 (Nahuatl and Maya place names; regional accents: Mexico City, the North, Veracruz, Yucatán)
ELE (x in México)
INALI catalogue (68 language groups, 364 variants); INEGI census 2020 (speakers of indigenous languages)

units.title: Formal occasions
units.can_do: Give a short speech or toast, thank people formally, and offer condolences with the right words.
functions: offer help to a grieving family

frames.es: Quisiera decir unas palabras.
frames.en: I'd like to say a few words.

frames.es: Quiero agradecerles a todos por estar aquí.
frames.en: I want to thank you all for being here.

frames.es: ¡Brindemos por los novios! ¡Salud!
frames.en: Let's drink to the bride and groom! Cheers!

frames.es: Es un honor para mí estar aquí.
frames.en: It's an honour for me to be here.

frames.es: Les agradezco de todo corazón.
frames.en: I thank you from the bottom of my heart.

frames.es: Mi más sentido pésame.
frames.en: My deepest condolences.
frames.note: Said quietly with a handshake or a hug; nothing more is needed.

frames.es: Lo acompaño en su dolor.
frames.en: I share your grief.
frames.note: To a woman: la acompaño. To a family: los acompaño.

frames.es: Que en paz descanse.
frames.en: May he rest in peace.

frames.es: Aquí estamos para lo que se les ofrezca.
frames.en: We're here for whatever you need.
frames.note: ofrecérsele a alguien: Mexican for 'to need'; also ¿qué se le ofrece? in shops.

model_exchanges.situation: A toast at a friend's wedding

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Perdón, ¿me permiten? Quisiera decir unas palabras.
lines.en: Excuse me, may I? I'd like to say a few words.

lines.speaker: invitados
lines.es: ¡Que hable, que hable!
lines.en: Speech, speech!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Es un honor para mí estar aquí. Cuando llegué a México, Ana y Luis me recibieron como de la familia.
lines.en: It's an honour for me to be here. When I arrived in Mexico, Ana and Luis welcomed me like family.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Quiero agradecerles a los dos su amistad, y a sus papás, que me abrieron las puertas de su casa.
lines.en: I want to thank you both for your friendship, and your parents, who opened their home to me.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Les deseo toda la felicidad del mundo. ¡Brindemos por los novios!
lines.en: I wish you all the happiness in the world. Let's drink to the bride and groom!

lines.speaker: invitados
lines.es: ¡Salud! ¡Que vivan los novios!
lines.en: Cheers! Long live the bride and groom!

model_exchanges.situation: At a wake (velorio) for a neighbour

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Señora, mi más sentido pésame. La acompaño en su dolor.
lines.en: Señora, my deepest condolences. I share your grief.

lines.speaker: viuda
lines.es: Gracias por venir. Él hablaba mucho de usted.
lines.en: Thank you for coming. He talked about you a lot.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Era un gran hombre. Que en paz descanse.
lines.en: He was a great man. May he rest in peace.

lines.speaker: viuda
lines.es: Gracias. Vamos a rezar el rosario los nueve días, si gusta acompañarnos.
lines.en: Thank you. We'll be saying the rosary for nine days, if you'd like to join us.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Ahí estaré. Y para lo que se le ofrezca, aquí estamos.
lines.en: I'll be there. And whatever you need, we're here.

model_exchanges.situation: A leaving party at work

lines.speaker: jefa
lines.es: Antes de que se vaya, queremos darle este recuerdo de parte de todos.
lines.en: Before you go, we'd like to give you this keepsake from all of us.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: ¡No se hubieran molestado! Les agradezco de todo corazón.
lines.en: You shouldn't have! I thank you from the bottom of my heart.

lines.speaker: compañero
lines.es: ¡Que hable, que hable!
lines.en: Speech, speech!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.es: Solo quiero decirles que aprendí muchísimo con ustedes. Esto no es un adiós, es un hasta luego.
lines.en: I just want to tell you that I learned so much from you. This isn't goodbye, it's see you soon.

grammar.explain: The nosotros form of the present subjunctive works as 'let's': brindemos, celebremos, recordemos.

examples.en: Let's drink to the bride and groom.

examples.es: Recordemos a don Arturo con cariño.

grammar.trap: In everyday speech Mexicans say vamos a + infinitive for 'let's'; brindemos belongs to toasts and speeches. With reflexive verbs the s drops: pongámonos, not pongámosnos.

grammar.explain: Ustedes is the only plural 'you' in Mexico, for friends and strangers alike; in a speech it goes with les and su.

examples.es: Gracias por acompañarnos en este día.
examples.en: Thank you for joining us on this day.

grammar.trap: Su presencia here means 'your presence', not 'his' or 'her'; context decides.

grammar.explain: Agradecer takes the person as indirect object (le, les, a…) and the reason either as a direct object or, very commonly in Mexico, with por.

examples.es: Quiero agradecerles a todos por venir.
examples.en: I want to thank you all for coming.

grammar.trap: It's por venir, not para venir; and the pronoun is usually doubled: agradecerles a ustedes.

grammar.explain: Condolences are fixed phrases said briefly and quietly; adding your own words is optional.
grammar.trap: 'Siento mucho su pérdida' is understood but sounds translated; mi más sentido pésame is what people say.

vocabulary.en: godparent; sponsor at a wedding or XV años
nine days of prayers after a death
to accompany; to be with (in grief)

pronunciation: In a speech, slow down and pause between groups of words: Quiero agradecerles // a todos // por estar aquí. Formal Mexican speech keeps every syllable.
n before p, b or m sounds like m: que en paz descanse is ke-em-PAS; un brindis is um-BRIN-dis.

common_errors.wrong: Vamos a brindar a los novios.
common_errors.why: You drink to someone with brindar por.
The reason takes por.
The formula sounds natural; the translation from English doesn't.
The Mexican formula for 'You shouldn't have' uses the pluperfect subjunctive.

units.culture: Formal occasions in Mexico follow a script. At weddings, XV años and christenings, padrinos pay for parts of the celebration and are thanked publicly, and any guest may be called on to say a few words (¡que hable, que hable!). At a velorio people come and go through the night, give the pésame in a phrase and a hug, and are offered coffee and pan dulce; prayers (the rosario or novenario) follow for nine days. Short, warm and formal is the rule.
recycles: b1-12 (Mi más sentido pésame. Bueno, ya me voy. Muchas gracias por todo.)
units.evidence: Given an occasion, the learner gives a short toast or thanks with ustedes, agradecerles por… and a brindemos, and at a wake or funeral uses the condolence formulas briefly and correctly, adding an offer of help.
