example.en: When I got there, the bus had already left.

points.point: the present perfect for change up to now (la colonia ha cambiado mucho)
points.explain: For a process that continues into the present, Mexicans use the perfect.
points.trap: Using the preterite here closes the change off as finished.

example.es: La colonia ha cambiado mucho en los últimos años.
example.en: The neighbourhood has changed a lot in recent years.

groups.name: Future: ir a + infinitive, the synthetic future (guesses), haber de, future perfect

points.point: va a llover as a chunk
points.explain: Va a + infinitive says what's about to happen.
points.trap: Learners leave out a: *va llover.

example.es: Parece que va a llover, ¿verdad?
example.en: Looks like it's going to rain, doesn't it?

points.point: ir a + infinitive: the everyday future in Mexico
points.explain: Plans and predictions in speech use ir a + infinitive.
points.trap: Don't drop the a: voy a ir, not *voy ir; the -é future sounds formal for plans.

example.es: ¿Qué vas a hacer el sábado? — Voy a ir al tianguis.
example.en: What are you doing on Saturday? — I'm going to the street market.

points.point: the synthetic future mainly for guesses (¿qué hora será? ¿dónde estarán mis llaves?)
points.explain: In Mexico the -é / -á future mostly means 'I wonder' or 'probably'.
points.trap: ¿Qué hora será? isn't about the future; it means 'I wonder what time it is'.

example.es: ¿Dónde estarán mis llaves? Estarán en la cocina.
example.en: Where can my keys be? They're probably in the kitchen.

points.point: future endings on the infinitive and irregular stems (tendr-, podr-, saldr-, pondr-, vendr-, sabr-, har-, dir-, querr-, habr-)
points.explain: Add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án to the infinitive; a few common verbs shorten the stem.
points.trap: *teneré, *haceré.

example.es: A esta hora habrá mucho tráfico; no podremos llegar a las seis.
example.en: There'll be a lot of traffic at this time; we won't make it by six.

points.point: haber de + infinitive for 'must be / probably' (ha de estar en el tráfico)
points.explain: Ha de + infinitive is a very Mexican way to make a guess.
points.trap: It isn't obligation: ha de estar means 'he's probably', not 'he has to be'.

example.es: No contesta; ha de estar manejando.
example.en: She's not answering; she must be driving.

points.point: the synthetic future for promises and formal announcements (mañana habrá corte de agua)
points.explain: Notices and promises often use the -é future.
points.trap: Learners avoid it entirely and miss notices.

example.es: Mañana habrá corte de agua en toda la colonia.
example.en: There'll be no water in the whole neighbourhood tomorrow.

points.point: the future perfect (para el viernes ya lo habré terminado) and for guesses about the past (ya habrá llegado; ha de haber llegado)
points.explain: Habré + participle is 'will have done', and also 'must have done'.
points.trap: English 'he must have arrived' tempts *debe tener llegado.

example.es: Para el viernes ya lo habré terminado. ¿Y tu hermano? Ha de haber llegado ya.
example.en: I'll have finished it by Friday. And your brother? He must have arrived by now.

points.point: the future in contracts and rules (se cobrará un recargo)
points.explain: Contracts state obligations and penalties in the future, often with se.
points.trap: It's not a prediction; it's a binding rule.

example.es: En caso de pago tardío, se cobrará un recargo del 10 %.
example.en: If payment is late, a 10% surcharge will be charged.

points.point: the future of objection (será muy bonito, pero…)
points.explain: Será + adjective, pero… concedes a point before objecting.
points.trap: Será here means 'it may well be', not 'it will be'.

example.es: Será muy bonito, pero está carísimo.
example.en: It may be lovely, but it costs a fortune.

points.point: me encantaría / me gustaría + infinitive as chunks
points.explain: Me encantaría and me gustaría are the polite way to accept or decline.
points.trap: Learners use quiero, which sounds blunt when declining.

example.es: Me encantaría, pero no puedo. Es que tengo que trabajar.
example.en: I'd love to, but I can't. I have to work.

points.point: quisiera as a polite 'I'd like'
points.explain: Quisiera is the politest way to ask for something on the phone or at a counter.
points.trap: Quiero sounds demanding; quisiera is a fixed chunk here.

example.es: Quisiera hacer una cita para el jueves 15.
example.en: I'd like to make an appointment for Thursday the 15th.

points.point: the conditional for polite requests (¿podría…? ¿me haría el favor de…?)
points.explain: Podría and haría turn a request into a polite question.
points.trap: Puede is fine, but podría is softer with landlords and officials.

example.es: ¿Podría revisar la llave del baño, por favor?
example.en: Could you check the bathroom tap, please?

points.point: conditional forms: -ía on the infinitive; irregular stems as in the future (tendría, podría, haría, diría)
points.explain: The conditional adds -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían to the infinitive.
points.trap: *tenería, *hacería.

example.es: Yo no haría eso; tendrías que ir al doctor.
example.en: I wouldn't do that; you'd have to go to the doctor.

points.point: the conditional for advice (deberías, yo que tú iría)
points.explain: Deberías and yo que tú + conditional give advice gently.
points.trap: Debes sounds like an order; 'you should' is deberías.

example.es: Yo que tú, iría a urgencias.
example.en: If I were you, I'd go to the ER.

points.point: the conditional for guesses about the past (serían como las diez)
points.explain: The conditional estimates something in the past: serían = it must have been.
points.trap: Learners say *eran tal vez las diez.

example.es: Serían como las diez cuando me asaltaron.
example.en: It must have been about ten when I was mugged.

points.point: habría que + infinitive (one ought to)
points.explain: Habría que suggests what should be done, without blaming anyone.
points.trap: Hay que is firmer; habría que is diplomatic.

example.es: Habría que ver de dónde salen esos datos.
example.en: We'd have to see where those figures come from.

points.point: deme / dígame as usted command chunks
points.explain: Deme is the usted command 'give me', common at market stalls.
points.trap: Deme is fine with por favor; with strangers prefer usted, not dame.

example.es: Deme medio kilo, por favor.
example.en: Give me half a kilo, please.

points.point: usted commands in directions: siga, dé vuelta, cruce, tome
points.explain: Directions are given with usted commands built from the present subjunctive.
points.trap: Dé (turn / give) has an accent to tell it from de.

example.es: Siga derecho, cruce la avenida y dé vuelta a la derecha.
example.en: Go straight on, cross the avenue and turn right.

points.point: usted and ustedes commands in emergencies and at the pharmacy (tómese, llamen, salgan)
points.explain: Instructions to you or to a group use the usted or ustedes command.
points.trap: Ustedes commands end in -n; there is no vosotros form in Mexico.

example.es: ¡Llamen al 911! Tómese una pastilla cada ocho horas.
example.en: Call 911! Take one pill every eight hours.

points.point: affirmative tú and usted commands: regular (cruza / cruce) and irregular (ve, ven, sal, haz, pon, di / vaya, venga, salga, haga)
points.explain: Tú commands look like the él form of the present; usted commands switch the vowel (cruce, coma).
points.trap: Mixing the two: *cruce la calle, güey, or *ven usted.

example.es: Cruza la calle y sigue derecho dos cuadras.
example.en: Cross the street and go straight on for two blocks.

points.point: pronouns attached to affirmative commands, with a written accent (avíseme, dígame, súbase)
points.explain: Object and reflexive pronouns go on the end of an affirmative command.
points.trap: Forgetting the accent changes the stress: avíseme, not *aviseme.

example.es: ¿Me avisa dónde me bajo? — Sí, yo le aviso. Súbase.
example.en: Will you tell me where to get off? — Yes, I'll tell you. Get on.

points.point: ustedes commands: the usted form + n (pasen, siéntense)
points.explain: For a group, add -n to the usted command.
points.trap: Spain's pasad, sentaos aren't used.

example.es: Pasen, por favor, siéntense.
example.en: Come in, please, have a seat.

points.point: infinitives on signs (no estacionarse, prohibido fumar)
points.explain: Signs and rules often use the infinitive or prohibido + infinitive.
points.trap: It isn't rude or childish; it's the impersonal sign style.

example.es: No estacionarse. Prohibido tirar basura.
example.en: No parking. No dumping rubbish.

points.point: negative commands use the subjunctive (no te preocupes, no se preocupe, no lo toques)
points.explain: No + subjunctive is the negative command, with pronouns before the verb.
points.trap: *No preocúpate; *no tocas.

example.es: No se preocupe, ahorita lo arreglamos.
example.en: Don't worry, we'll fix it right away.

points.point: usted commands in office instructions: traiga, llene, firme, regrese, pase
points.explain: Officials give instructions in usted commands.
points.trap: Learners mistake them for questions or for the present.

example.es: Llene este formato y regrese con dos copias.
example.en: Fill in this form and come back with two copies.

points.point: ¡a + infinitive! and ¡vámonos! (¡a comer!)
points.explain: A + infinitive calls everyone to do something now.
points.trap: Learners translate 'let's eat' as *comamos, which sounds stiff.

example.es: ¡A comer, que se enfría!
example.en: Come and eat, it's getting cold!

points.point: the let's-form for toasts and formal occasions (brindemos, celebremos)
points.explain: The nosotros subjunctive works as 'let's' in formal speech.
points.trap: In everyday speech Mexicans prefer vamos a + infinitive.

example.es: ¡Brindemos por los novios!
example.en: Let's toast the bride and groom!

points.point: que le vaya bien as a fixed goodbye
points.explain: This goodbye is a wish; it's learned whole long before the subjunctive.
points.trap: *que le va bien.

example.es: Hasta luego, que le vaya bien.
example.en: Bye, have a good day.

points.point: no sé si pueda as a fixed soft refusal
points.explain: No sé si pueda ('I don't know if I can') usually means no.
points.trap: Learners hear it as 'maybe' and wait for the person.

example.es: No sé si pueda, pero hago la lucha.
example.en: I don't know if I can make it, but I'll try.

points.point: ¡que se mejore! as a chunk
points.explain: Que + subjunctive wishes someone well.
points.trap: Learners answer with gracias only; it's enough.

example.es: Tómese esto cada ocho horas. ¡Que se mejore!
example.en: Take this every eight hours. Get well soon!

points.point: ¡que + subjunctive! in celebrations (¡que lo muerda!)
points.explain: At birthdays the crowd chants ¡que lo muerda! for the bite of the cake.
points.trap: It's a chant, not an order to you.

example.es: ¡Que lo muerda! ¡Que lo muerda!
example.en: Bite it! Bite it!

points.point: present subjunctive forms: -ar → -e, -er / -ir → -a; irregulars vaya, sea, tenga, haga, pueda, esté, sepa
points.explain: Take the yo form, drop -o and add the 'opposite' vowel endings.
points.trap: Irregular yo forms carry over: tengo → tenga, hago → haga.

example.es: Espero que tengas un buen viaje.
example.en: I hope you have a good trip.

points.point: que + subjunctive for wishes (que te vaya bien, que descanses)
points.explain: Que + subjunctive on its own is a wish for someone.
points.trap: *que descansas.

example.es: ¡Que te mejores pronto! ¡Que descanses!
example.en: Get well soon! Sleep well!

points.point: ojalá (que) + subjunctive
points.explain: Ojalá always takes the subjunctive.
points.trap: *Ojalá que no llueve.

example.es: Ojalá que no llueva mañana.
example.en: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.

points.point: espero que + subjunctive (different subject) vs espero + infinitive (same subject)
points.explain: With two people, espero que + subjunctive; about yourself, espero + infinitive.
points.trap: *Espero que llego a tiempo.

example.es: Espero que te guste. Espero llegar a tiempo.
example.en: I hope you like it. I hope to get there on time.

points.point: quiero / necesito que + subjunctive (different subject)
points.explain: Wanting someone else to do something takes que + subjunctive.
points.trap: English 'I want you to help' tempts *quiero tú ayudar.

example.es: Necesito que me ayudes con algo.
example.en: I need you to help me with something.

points.point: es necesario que / hace falta que + subjunctive
points.explain: Necessity with a different subject takes the subjunctive.
points.trap: Officials say hace falta que traiga…: it means 'you need to bring'.

example.es: Hace falta que traiga el original.
example.en: You need to bring the original.

points.point: emotion + que + subjunctive (me molesta que, estoy harto de que)
points.explain: Feelings about someone else's action take the subjunctive.
points.trap: *Me molesta que no avisan.

example.es: Me molesta que no avisen cuando cortan el agua.
example.en: It annoys me that they don't warn us when they cut the water.

points.point: creo que + indicative / no creo que + subjunctive
points.explain: Positive belief takes the indicative; doubt or denial takes the subjunctive.
points.trap: *Creo que sea caro.

example.es: Creo que tienes razón, pero no creo que sea tan peligroso.
example.en: I think you're right, but I don't think it's that dangerous.

points.point: a lo mejor + indicative; tal vez / quizás + subjunctive or indicative
points.explain: A lo mejor, Mexico's everyday 'maybe', takes the indicative.
points.trap: *A lo mejor llueva.

example.es: A lo mejor llueve; tal vez lleguen tarde.
example.en: Maybe it'll rain; perhaps they'll be late.

points.point: se solicita persona que + subjunctive (someone not yet known)
points.explain: Job ads describe the person they want in the subjunctive.
points.trap: Learners read hable as a typo for habla.

example.es: Se solicita persona que hable inglés.
example.en: Wanted: English speaker.

points.point: es mejor que / te recomiendo que + subjunctive
points.explain: Advice about someone else's action takes the subjunctive.
points.trap: *Es mejor que no tomas.

example.es: Es mejor que no tomes antibióticos sin receta.
example.en: Better not to take antibiotics without a prescription.

points.point: para que + subjunctive (so that someone…)
points.explain: Purpose with a different subject is para que + subjunctive.
points.trap: *para que me marcas; with the same subject use para + infinitive.

example.es: Te dejo mi número para que me marques.
example.en: I'll leave you my number so you can call me.

points.point: cuando / en cuanto + subjunctive for the future (cuando llegues, avísame)
points.explain: Time clauses about the future use the subjunctive.
points.trap: *Cuando llegarás and *cuando llegas avísame.

example.es: En cuanto sepa algo, te aviso. Cuando llegues, avísame.
example.en: As soon as I hear anything I'll let you know. Let me know when you get there.

points.point: qué bueno que / me da gusto que + subjunctive
points.explain: Being glad about someone else's situation takes the subjunctive.
points.trap: *Qué bueno que estás aquí is common for facts, but the subjunctive is the polite norm.

example.es: ¡Qué bueno que estés aquí! Me da gusto que hayan venido.
example.en: So good you're here! I'm glad you came.

points.point: the present perfect subjunctive haya + participle (qué bueno que hayan venido)
points.explain: After an emotion or wish about something already done, use haya / hayas / hayan + participle.
points.trap: *Qué bueno que vinieron is common, but after que + feeling the subjunctive is the norm: hayan venido.

example.es: ¡Qué bueno que hayan venido! Espero que te haya gustado la comida.
example.en: So glad you came! I hope you enjoyed the food.

points.point: imperfect subjunctive -ra forms from the ellos preterite (tuvieron → tuviera)
points.explain: Take the ellos preterite, drop -ron and add -ra; -se forms are for reading only.
points.trap: Irregular preterites carry over: dijeron → dijera, fueron → fuera.

example.es: Si tuviera más tiempo, tomaría clases de cocina.
example.en: If I had more time, I'd take cooking classes.

points.point: me gustaría que / quería que + imperfect subjunctive
points.explain: After a conditional or past wish, the subjunctive moves to the -ra form.
points.trap: *Me gustaría que vengas.

example.es: Me gustaría que vinieras a la posada.
example.en: I'd like you to come to the posada.

points.point: ojalá + imperfect subjunctive for unlikely wishes
points.explain: Ojalá + -ra form wishes for something unlikely or impossible.
points.trap: Ojalá + present is for things that may well happen.

example.es: Ojalá pudiera quedarme más tiempo.
example.en: I wish I could stay longer.

points.point: como si + imperfect subjunctive
points.explain: Como si ('as if') always takes the imperfect subjunctive.
points.trap: *como si es de aquí.

example.es: Habla como si fuera de aquí.
example.en: She talks as if she were from here.

points.point: subjunctive after an unknown or non-existent antecedent (busco un depa que tenga…; no hay nadie que sepa)
points.explain: If the thing or person may not exist, the description is in the subjunctive.
points.trap: A known thing takes the indicative: el depa que tiene terraza.

example.es: Busco un depa que tenga luz natural y que acepte mascotas.
example.en: I'm looking for a flat with natural light that allows pets.

points.point: no pensé que + imperfect subjunctive
points.explain: Past disbelief takes the -ra form.
points.trap: *No pensé que era tan difícil is common, but fuera is the standard.

example.es: No pensé que fuera tan difícil.
example.en: I didn't think it would be so hard.

points.point: le agradecería que + imperfect subjunctive
points.explain: A formal request: 'I'd be grateful if you…'.
points.trap: *Le agradecería que me manda.

example.es: Le agradecería que me mandara la información por correo.
example.en: I'd be grateful if you could email me the information.

points.point: propongo que / sugiero que + subjunctive
points.explain: Proposals about what others should do take the subjunctive.
points.trap: *Propongo que subimos la cuota.

example.es: Propongo que subamos la cuota de mantenimiento.
example.en: I propose we raise the maintenance fee.

points.point: aunque + subjunctive (even if / no matter) vs indicative (a known fact)
points.explain: Aunque + indicative states a fact; + subjunctive concedes a possibility or a known point.
points.trap: Learners always use the indicative.

example.es: Aunque no estemos de acuerdo, hay que decidir hoy.
example.en: Even if we don't agree, we have to decide today.

points.point: antes de que (always subjunctive), hasta que and mientras + subjunctive for the future
points.explain: These time links take the subjunctive when the event hasn't happened yet.
points.trap: *antes de que se descompone.

example.es: Hay que arreglar el elevador antes de que se descomponga más.
example.en: We need to fix the lift before it gets worse.

points.point: no es que + subjunctive, sino que + indicative
points.explain: No es que denies a reason; sino que gives the real one.
points.trap: *No es que no me gusta.

example.es: No es que no me guste, sino que es demasiado caro.
example.en: It's not that I don't like it, it's that it's too expensive.

points.point: es cierto que + indicative / no está claro que + subjunctive; puede que + subjunctive
points.explain: Certainty takes the indicative, doubt and possibility the subjunctive.
points.trap: *Puede que tienes razón.

example.es: Es cierto que hay más seguridad, pero puede que no dure.
example.en: It's true there's more security, but it may not last.

points.point: esperaba que + imperfect subjunctive
points.explain: A past expectation takes the -ra form.
points.trap: *Esperaba que termina diferente.

example.es: No me gustó el final; esperaba que terminara diferente.
example.en: I didn't like the ending; I expected it to end differently.

points.point: en caso de que + subjunctive; hace falta que + subjunctive
points.explain: En caso de que ('in case') always takes the subjunctive.
points.trap: *en caso de que le duele.

example.es: En caso de que le duela más, venga a urgencias.
example.en: If it hurts more, come to the ER.

points.point: siempre y cuando, a menos que, con tal de que + subjunctive
points.explain: Conditions and exceptions in contracts take the subjunctive.
points.trap: *siempre y cuando incluye.

example.es: Firmo siempre y cuando incluya la renovación.
example.en: I'll sign as long as it includes renewal.

points.point: que yo sepa (as far as I know)
points.explain: A fixed subjunctive hedge.
points.trap: *que yo sé.

example.es: Que yo sepa, no hace falta traducir el acta.
example.en: As far as I know, the certificate doesn't need translating.

points.point: por más que + subjunctive (however much)
points.explain: Por más que concedes effort that doesn't change the result.
points.trap: *por más que lo explican.

example.es: Por más que lo expliquen, no me convence.
example.en: However much they explain it, I'm not convinced.

points.point: repeated subjunctive for 'whatever / no matter' (digan lo que digan, sea como sea)
points.explain: Verb + lo que + same verb in the subjunctive means 'no matter what'.
points.trap: Learners translate 'whatever they say' word for word.

example.es: Digan lo que digan, el metro sigue siendo lo más rápido.
example.en: Whatever they say, the metro is still the quickest.

points.point: si + present for real conditions (si firmo hoy, ¿me dan las llaves?)
points.explain: A real possibility uses si + present, then present, future or command.
points.trap: Never future after si: *si firmaré.

example.es: Si firmo hoy, ¿me dan las llaves el lunes?
example.en: If I sign today, will you give me the keys on Monday?

points.point: si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional for unlikely or unreal situations
points.explain: Imagining uses si + -ra form, then the conditional.
points.trap: *Si tendría tiempo; the conditional never goes after si.

example.es: Si yo fuera tú, no firmaría todavía.
example.en: If I were you, I wouldn't sign yet.

points.point: si hubiera … hubiera: the everyday Mexican unreal past (habría recognised)
points.explain: Mexicans use hubiera + participle in both halves for regrets about the past.
points.trap: Textbooks teach habría avisado; it's correct but sounds written in Mexico.

example.es: Si hubiera sabido, te hubiera avisado.
example.en: If I'd known, I'd have told you.

points.point: de + infinitive as a condition (de haberlo sabido…)
points.explain: De + infinitive replaces a si-clause in careful speech.
points.trap: It looks like a preposition phrase but means 'if'.

example.es: De haberlo sabido, no hubiera venido.
example.en: Had I known, I wouldn't have come.

groups.name: Se: accidental, impersonal, passive; passive with ser

points.point: se me olvidó as a chunk
points.explain: Se me olvidó ('it slipped my mind') is how Mexicans admit forgetting.
points.trap: Olvidé is correct but sounds blunter.

example.es: ¡Ay, se me olvidó la cartera!
example.en: Oh no, I forgot my wallet!

points.point: accidental se: se me cayó, se me rompió, se me perdió (the thing is the subject)
points.explain: Accidents are told as things happening to you: the thing is the subject and me marks you.
points.trap: English 'I dropped my phone' tempts *caí el celular; and plural things need se me cayeron.

example.es: Se me cayó el celular y se me rompió un vaso.
example.en: I dropped my phone and broke a glass.

points.point: se with things that break down or run out (se descompuso el boiler, se fue la luz, se acabó el gas)
points.explain: When something stops working by itself, the verb takes se.
points.trap: *El boiler descompuso.

example.es: Se descompuso el boiler y se acabó el gas.
example.en: The water heater broke and the gas ran out.

points.point: impersonal se: se puede, se acostumbra, se hace
points.explain: Se + third person says what people in general do or may do.
points.trap: English uses 'you' or 'people'; tú puedes can sound personal.

example.es: ¿Aquí se puede estacionar? ¿Se acostumbra dejar propina?
example.en: Can you park here? Is it usual to tip?

points.point: passive se on signs and ads, agreeing with the noun (se renta depa, se rentan cuartos)
points.explain: Se + verb agrees with the thing: se vende casa, se venden casas.
points.trap: *Se renta cuartos is very common on signs but standard is se rentan.

example.es: Vi que se renta un departamento en este edificio.
example.en: I saw there's a flat for rent in this building.

points.point: the passive with ser (fue detenido) in news and reports
points.explain: Ser + participle (agreeing) is the formal passive.
points.trap: In conversation Mexicans prefer lo detuvieron.

example.es: El ladrón fue detenido a dos cuadras.
example.en: The thief was arrested two blocks away.

points.point: vencerse with accidental se for expiry (se me venció la visa)
points.explain: Documents expire 'on you': se me venció, se le vence.
points.trap: *Mi visa expiró is understood but sounds translated.

example.es: Se me venció la tarjeta de residente y tengo que renovarla.
example.en: My residence card has expired and I need to renew it.

points.point: bureaucratic impersonal se le (se le notificará, se le informa)
points.explain: Offices write se le + verb: 'you will be notified'.
points.trap: Le refers to you (usted), not to a third person.

example.es: Se le notificará la resolución por correo electrónico.
example.en: You'll be notified of the decision by email.

groups.name: Verb phrases and modals (ir a, tener que, hay que, acabar de, andar + gerund…)

points.point: poder + infinitive in polite questions (¿me lo puede repetir?)
points.explain: ¿Puede + infinitive? asks a stranger to do something.
points.trap: With strangers use puede (usted), not puedes.

example.es: ¿Me lo puede repetir, por favor?
example.en: Could you repeat that, please?

points.point: llevo / tengo + time + aquí (tengo dos semanas aquí)
points.explain: Llevar or tener + time says how long you've been somewhere; tener is the everyday Mexican form.
points.trap: English 'I've been here two weeks' tempts *he estado aquí por dos semanas.

example.es: Tengo dos semanas aquí. / Llevo dos semanas en México.
example.en: I've been here two weeks. / I've been in Mexico for two weeks.

points.point: hay que + infinitive (one must)
points.explain: Hay que + infinitive says what needs doing, without saying who.
points.trap: It never changes: *hay que salimos.

example.es: Está sonando la alerta sísmica: hay que salir.
example.en: The earthquake alert is sounding: we need to get out.

points.point: ir + gerund for gradual change (me voy acostumbrando)
points.explain: Ir + -ando / -iendo describes something happening little by little.
points.trap: It doesn't mean literally going anywhere.

example.es: Poco a poco me voy acostumbrando.
example.en: Little by little I'm getting used to it.

points.point: tener que + infinitive (I have to)
points.explain: Tener que is personal obligation.
points.trap: *Tengo trabajar: the que is needed.

example.es: Es que tengo que trabajar el sábado.
example.en: The thing is, I have to work on Saturday.

points.point: quedar de + infinitive (Mexico) to arrange to do something
points.explain: Quedamos de vernos = we agreed to meet.
points.trap: Spain-based books teach quedar con / quedar en.

example.es: Quedamos de vernos a las seis en la esquina.
example.en: We agreed to meet at six on the corner.

points.point: ir por + noun (go and get: vamos por unos tacos)
points.explain: Ir por means to go and fetch or go and have something.
points.trap: *ir para unos tacos.

example.es: ¿Quieres ir por unos tacos el viernes?
example.en: Do you want to go for tacos on Friday?

points.point: estar + gerund for what's happening right now (estoy manejando)
points.explain: Estar + -ando / -iendo is for actions in progress.
points.trap: Don't use it for the future like English: 'I'm leaving tomorrow' is me voy mañana.

example.es: Ahorita estoy manejando; te marco al rato.
example.en: I'm driving right now; I'll call you in a bit.

points.point: hay que vs tener que: general vs personal obligation
points.explain: Hay que is general; tener que says who has to.
points.trap: Hay que never takes a subject: *yo hay que.

example.es: Hay que cambiar el foco, pero yo no tengo que hacerlo.
example.en: The bulb needs changing, but I don't have to do it.

points.point: volver a + infinitive (again)
points.explain: Volver a + infinitive means doing something again.
points.trap: Learners add otra vez to everything; volver a is shorter.

example.es: Se volvió a ir la luz.
example.en: The power went off again.

points.point: acabar de + infinitive (have just done)
points.explain: Acabo de + infinitive means 'I've just…'.
points.trap: English 'I've just' tempts *he justo llegado.

example.es: Acabo de llegar a México.
example.en: I've just arrived in Mexico.

points.point: llevar + time + gerund (llevo seis meses viviendo aquí)
points.explain: Llevar + time + gerund says how long you've been doing something.
points.trap: *He vivido aquí seis meses is understood but less natural.

example.es: Llevo seis meses viviendo aquí.
example.en: I've been living here for six months.

points.point: ponerse a + infinitive (start suddenly)
points.explain: Se puso a llover = it started raining.
points.trap: Learners only know empezar a.

example.es: Se puso a llover justo cuando salí.
example.en: It started raining just as I went out.

points.point: andar + gerund (ando buscando chamba)
points.explain: In Mexico andar + gerund is an everyday way to say what you're up to.
points.trap: It doesn't mean wandering around.

example.es: Ando buscando chamba de medio tiempo.
example.en: I'm looking for part-time work.

points.point: dejar de + infinitive (stop doing)
points.explain: Dejar de + infinitive means to stop or quit.
points.trap: *parar fumar.

example.es: Tiene que dejar de fumar.
example.en: You have to stop smoking.

points.point: mandar a + infinitive (me mandaron a hacer unos estudios)
points.explain: Mandar a + infinitive is to send someone to do something.
points.trap: Learners say *me ordenaron estudios.

example.es: El doctor me mandó a hacer unos estudios.
example.en: The doctor sent me for some tests.

points.point: estar a punto de + infinitive; Mexican estar por + infinitive (about to)
points.explain: Both mean 'about to'; estar por is the everyday Mexican one.
points.trap: Estar por can also mean 'be in favour of' elsewhere; here it's time.

example.es: El camión está por llegar.
example.en: The bus is about to arrive.

points.point: debí + infinitive for 'should have' (debí preguntar antes)
points.explain: The preterite of deber + infinitive is the everyday 'should have'.
points.trap: English 'should have asked' tempts *debería tener preguntado.

example.es: Debí preguntar antes de firmar.
example.en: I should have asked before signing.

points.point: seguir + gerund / seguir sin + infinitive (sigue sin funcionar)
points.explain: Seguir + gerund is 'still doing'; seguir sin + infinitive is 'still not'.
points.trap: *sigue no funcionando.

example.es: Me dijeron que esperara 48 horas, pero sigue sin funcionar.
example.en: They told me to wait 48 hours, but it still doesn't work.

points.point: mandar + infinitive for having something done (mandé hacer unas cortinas)
points.explain: Mandar hacer / mandar arreglar = to have something made or fixed.
points.trap: English 'have something done' tempts *tener hecho.

example.es: Mandé hacer unas cortinas y tengo que mandar arreglar el sillón.
example.en: I had some curtains made and I need to have the armchair fixed.

points.point: quedar en + infinitive (agree to)
points.explain: Quedar en means to agree or promise to do something.
points.trap: Quedó en venir ≠ se quedó en casa.

example.es: Quedó en venir el lunes con la cotización.
example.en: He agreed to come on Monday with the quote.

points.point: echarse a + infinitive (burst out: echarse a reír / a llorar)
points.explain: Echarse a + infinitive is a sudden start.
points.trap: It isn't about throwing anything.

example.es: Cuando le conté, se echó a reír.
example.en: When I told her, she burst out laughing.

points.point: dice que + present for passing on a message now
points.explain: To relay a message right away, use dice que and keep the tense.
points.trap: Learners backshift when it isn't needed.

example.es: Dice el casero que mañana viene el plomero.
example.en: The landlord says the plumber's coming tomorrow.

points.point: dijo que + imperfect (backshift)
points.explain: After dijo que, a present becomes an imperfect.
points.trap: Mexicans often keep the present if it's still true; both are fine.

example.es: Me dijo que llegaba a las cinco.
example.en: She said she was arriving at five.

points.point: reported questions with si and question words (me preguntó si quería ir)
points.explain: Yes / no questions are reported with si; others keep the question word.
points.trap: *Me preguntó que si quería ir is common in speech; si alone is standard.

example.es: Me preguntó si quería ir y a qué hora salía.
example.en: She asked me if I wanted to go and what time I was leaving.

points.point: reported requests: dice que + subjunctive (dice que le marques)
points.explain: A request passed on takes the subjunctive.
points.trap: *Dice que le marcas sounds like a statement, not a request.

example.es: Dice tu mamá que le marques.
example.en: Your mum says to call her.

points.point: reported orders in the past: me dijeron que esperara (imperfect subjunctive)
points.explain: A past request moves into the -ra form.
points.trap: *Me dijeron que espere is common, but esperara is the standard.

example.es: Me dijeron que esperara 48 horas.
example.en: They told me to wait 48 hours.

points.point: caminando = on foot (gerund as an adverb)
points.explain: The gerund -ando / -iendo says how you do something: me voy caminando.
points.trap: *a pie is understood, but Mexicans mostly say caminando.

example.es: Está cerca; vamos caminando.
example.en: It's close; let's walk.

points.point: me gusta + infinitive (the infinitive as a noun)
points.explain: An activity after gustar, querer or poder is in the infinitive.
points.trap: English '-ing' tempts *me gusta caminando.

example.es: Me gusta caminar por el parque en la mañana.
example.en: I like walking in the park in the morning.

points.point: the gerund forms: -ando, -iendo, and y in leyendo, oyendo; e > i, o > u in pidiendo, durmiendo
points.explain: -ar verbs take -ando and -er / -ir verbs -iendo; some stems change.
points.trap: *leiendo, *dormiendo.

example.es: Ahorita está durmiendo; te marco al rato.
example.en: He's asleep right now; I'll call you in a bit.

points.point: antes de / después de + infinitive
points.explain: After a preposition, the verb is in the infinitive.
points.trap: English '-ing' tempts *antes de comiendo.

example.es: Antes de venir a México, vivía en Toronto.
example.en: Before coming to Mexico, I lived in Toronto.

points.point: the past participle -ado / -ido
points.explain: Regular participles end in -ado for -ar verbs and -ido for -er / -ir verbs.
points.trap: With haber it never changes: ella ha ido, not *ha ida.

example.es: ¿Has probado el pozole? — Nunca lo he probado.
example.en: Have you tried pozole? — I've never tried it.

points.point: participles as adjectives that agree (está incluido, la luz va aparte, amueblado)
points.explain: With estar or after a noun, the participle agrees like an adjective.
points.trap: *La luz está incluido.

example.es: ¿El depa está amueblado? ¿El agua está incluida?
example.en: Is the flat furnished? Is water included?

points.point: al + infinitive (= when …): al llegar, al salir
points.explain: Al + infinitive means 'on doing' or 'when'.
points.trap: Learners write *en llegar.

example.es: Al salir del metro, me di cuenta de que no traía la cartera.
example.en: When I came out of the metro, I realised I didn't have my wallet.

points.point: participles in descriptions (basada en una historia real, doblada al español)
points.explain: Participles describe films and books, agreeing with the noun.
points.trap: *La película está basado en…

example.es: Es una serie basada en una historia real, doblada al español.
example.en: It's a series based on a true story, dubbed into Spanish.

points.point: the participle and gerund in official writing (una vez recibida la solicitud; anexando copia)
points.explain: Formal documents use absolute participles and gerunds instead of full clauses.
points.trap: Una vez recibida = once (it has been) received; it isn't a mistake.

example.es: Una vez recibida la documentación, se le notificará por correo.
example.en: Once the documents are received, you will be notified by email.

points.point: ahorita: right now, in a moment, or later (context decides)
points.explain: Ahorita in Mexico can mean now, in a bit, or politely 'not now'.
points.trap: Learners take ahorita lo hago as 'immediately'.

example.es: Ahorita vengo.
example.en: I'll be right back.

points.point: aquí / acá, ahí, allá; nomás = only, just
points.explain: Acá and allá are common in Mexico; nomás is neutral for 'just' or 'only'.
points.trap: Nomás isn't slang; it's fine in any shop.

example.es: Nomás quería ver. Los de acá, ¿cuánto cuestan?
example.en: I was just looking. How much are these ones here?

points.point: ya no = no longer; ya = already / now
points.explain: Ya no means something has stopped or run out.
points.trap: *No más for 'no longer'.

example.es: Ya no hay tamales; ya se acabaron.
example.en: There are no tamales left; they've run out.

points.point: bien + adjective = very (bien dulces, bien rico)
points.explain: Bien before an adjective intensifies it, like muy.
points.trap: It isn't 'well': bien caro = very expensive.

example.es: Estos mangos están bien dulces.
example.en: These mangoes are really sweet.

points.point: derecho = straight ahead; place adverbs (cerca, lejos, enfrente, abajo, arriba)
points.explain: Mexicans say derecho for 'straight on'; recto sounds foreign.
points.trap: Derecha = right, derecho = straight on.

example.es: Siga derecho; el cajero está enfrente.
example.en: Go straight on; the cash machine is opposite.

points.point: en la mañana / en la tarde / en la noche (Mexico)
points.explain: Mexicans say en la mañana where Spain says por la mañana.
points.trap: With a clock time it's de: a las diez de la mañana.

example.es: Abren a las diez de la mañana y en la tarde cierran temprano.
example.en: They open at ten in the morning and close early in the afternoon.

points.point: muy vs mucho: muy + adjective / adverb, mucho with verbs and nouns
points.explain: Muy goes before adjectives; mucho goes after verbs or before nouns.
points.trap: *Me gusta muy; *muy calor.

example.es: Me gusta mucho; hace mucho calor, pero está muy bonito.
example.en: I like it a lot; it's very hot, but it's lovely.

points.point: también / tampoco
points.explain: También agrees with a positive, tampoco with a negative.
points.trap: *A mí también no.

example.es: No me gusta el picante. — A mí tampoco.
example.en: I don't like spicy food. — Me neither.

points.point: time words for the past: hoy, ayer, anoche, en la mañana
points.explain: These words fix the time of a finished action.
points.trap: Anoche is one word.

example.es: Anoche cené tacos y hoy desayuné chilaquiles.
example.en: Last night I had tacos for dinner and today I had chilaquiles for breakfast.

points.point: frequency: siempre, seguido, a veces, casi nunca, nunca, una vez a la semana
points.explain: Seguido is the everyday Mexican 'often'.
points.trap: Nunca after the verb needs no: no voy nunca / nunca voy.

example.es: Voy seguido al tianguis, pero casi nunca compro ropa.
example.en: I often go to the street market, but I hardly ever buy clothes.

points.point: antier, la semana pasada, hace + time (= ago)
points.explain: Antier is the Mexican 'the day before yesterday'; hace dos días = two days ago.
points.trap: *dos días hace; and anteayer sounds Spanish.

example.es: Llegué antier; mi hermana vino hace un mes.
example.en: I arrived the day before yesterday; my sister came a month ago.

points.point: tantito and ahorita as softeners (espéreme tantito)
points.explain: Tantito means 'a little bit' and softens a request.
points.trap: It isn't an amount to measure; it's politeness.

example.es: Espéreme tantito, ahorita le paso a la doctora.
example.en: Wait just a moment, I'll put you through to the doctor.

points.point: antes vs ahora; todavía / ya no
points.explain: Antes (before) and ahora (now) frame a contrast.
points.trap: Antes alone doesn't need 'that': antes vivía.

example.es: Antes iba al gimnasio; ahora ya no voy.
example.en: I used to go to the gym; now I don't any more.

points.point: alguna vez, nunca, todavía no, ya
points.explain: These go with the perfect for experience and the preterite for 'yet'.
points.trap: *¿Alguna vez fuiste? is also heard in Mexico; both are fine.

example.es: ¿Alguna vez has comido chapulines? — No, nunca.
example.en: Have you ever eaten grasshoppers? — No, never.

points.point: -mente adverbs from the feminine form (rápidamente, tranquilamente)
points.explain: Add -mente to the feminine adjective; the accent stays.
points.trap: *rapidomente; with two in a row, only the last takes -mente.

example.es: Afortunadamente, llegué rápida y tranquilamente.
example.en: Luckily, I arrived quickly and calmly.

points.point: sí for emphasis (ella sí sabe)
points.explain: Sí before the verb insists on the contrast: she really does know.
points.trap: Without an accent, si means 'if'.

example.es: Yo no sé cocinar, pero mi vecina sí sabe.
example.en: I can't cook, but my neighbour really can.

points.point: cada vez más / menos; últimamente; recién (Mexico)
points.explain: Cada vez más = more and more; recién + verb = just.
points.trap: Recién llegué is everyday in Mexico; recientemente sounds formal.

example.es: Cada vez hay más tráfico; recién abrieron otra plaza.
example.en: There's more and more traffic; they've just opened another mall.

points.point: de for origin and en for where you live
points.explain: Soy de + place, vivo en + place.
points.trap: *Vivo a Coyoacán.

example.es: Soy de Canadá y vivo en Coyoacán.
example.en: I'm from Canada and I live in Coyoacán.

points.point: con / sin (con todo, sin cebolla)
points.explain: Con and sin take a noun with no article.
points.trap: *sin la cebolla.

example.es: Dos de pastor con todo y uno sin cebolla.
example.en: Two al pastor with everything and one without onion.

points.point: a + distance or time (a dos cuadras, a cinco minutos)
points.explain: A says how far: está a dos cuadras.
points.trap: *Está dos cuadras.

example.es: El metro está a cinco minutos, a dos cuadras de aquí.
example.en: The metro is five minutes away, two blocks from here.

points.point: place phrases with de: enfrente de, al lado de, cerca de, lejos de, en la esquina
points.explain: Compound place phrases end in de before the noun.
points.trap: *enfrente el banco.

example.es: La farmacia está enfrente del parque, al lado de un Oxxo.
example.en: The pharmacy is opposite the park, next to an Oxxo.

points.point: a for clock time; de … a … for ranges; para in times (veinte para las ocho)
points.explain: A las cinco = at five; de nueve a seis = from nine to six; Mexicans tell minutes before the hour with para.
points.trap: *En las cinco; and menos is understood but para is Mexican.

example.es: Abren de nueve a seis. Son veinte para las ocho.
example.en: They're open from nine to six. It's twenty to eight.

points.point: hasta = not until (Mexico): abren hasta las diez
points.explain: In Mexico hasta often means the action only starts at that time.
points.trap: Abren hasta las diez means they open at ten, not that they stay open till ten.

example.es: Hoy abren hasta las diez.
example.en: They don't open until ten today.

points.point: en + transport (en camión, en metro); pasar por
points.explain: Travel by vehicle uses en; pasar por = go via.
points.trap: *por camión; and Mexicans say camión for the city bus.

example.es: Voy en metro. ¿Este camión pasa por el centro?
example.en: I'm going by metro. Does this bus go through downtown?

points.point: the personal a before a person object (conocí a tu hermana)
points.explain: A specific person as object takes a.
points.trap: English has nothing here: *conocí tu hermana.

example.es: Ayer conocí a tu hermana y vi a tus papás.
example.en: Yesterday I met your sister and saw your parents.

points.point: ir por = go and get (voy por pan); invitar a
points.explain: Ir por + thing = go and fetch it; invitar a + person or event.
points.trap: *ir para pan.

example.es: Voy por pan. ¿Te invito a cenar?
example.en: I'm going for bread. Can I take you to dinner?

points.point: desde hace + time and desde + date
points.explain: Desde hace counts back from now; desde gives the starting point.
points.trap: *por tres días with something still going on.

example.es: Me duele desde el lunes, o sea desde hace tres días.
example.en: It's hurt since Monday, so for three days.

points.point: por vs para, core uses: para = purpose, recipient, deadline; por = cause, through, exchange, 'for' a time
points.explain: Para points to a goal; por explains a reason or the route.
points.trap: English 'for' covers both.

example.es: Gracias por la ayuda; esto es para usted.
example.en: Thanks for the help; this is for you.

points.point: venir por (come to collect) / venir a (come to do)
points.explain: Vengo por mi credencial = to pick it up; vengo a tramitar = to apply.
points.trap: *Vengo para mi credencial.

example.es: Vengo por mi credencial; la otra vez vine a tramitarla.
example.en: I've come to pick up my ID; last time I came to apply for it.

points.point: dedicarse a
points.explain: ¿A qué te dedicas? asks what someone does for a living.
points.trap: *¿Qué te dedicas?

example.es: ¿A qué se dedica? — Me dedico a la enseñanza.
example.en: What do you do? — I'm a teacher.

points.point: por and para in reports (me robaron por la noche; lo llevaron para el Ministerio Público)
points.explain: Por gives cause, means and time span; para gives direction and purpose.
points.trap: Learners use para for cause: *me asaltaron para el celular.

example.es: Me asaltaron por mi celular cerca de la estación.
example.en: I was mugged for my phone near the station.

points.point: según (according to)
points.explain: Según + source or person; with pronouns it's según yo, según tú.
points.trap: *según a ella.

example.es: Según la leyenda, los mexicas vieron un águila sobre un nopal.
example.en: According to legend, the Mexica saw an eagle on a cactus.

points.point: agradecer a alguien por algo
points.explain: Agradecer takes the person with a and the reason with por.
points.trap: *agradecer por alguien.

example.es: Quiero agradecer a todos por estar aquí.
example.en: I'd like to thank everyone for being here.

points.point: y / pero; y becomes e before i- (español e inglés)
points.explain: Y joins, pero contrasts; y changes to e before an i sound.
points.trap: *español y inglés is common in speech, but e is standard.

example.es: Hablo inglés e italiano, pero poco español.
example.en: I speak English and Italian, but little Spanish.

points.point: o; o becomes u before o- (siete u ocho)
points.explain: O means 'or'; before an o sound it changes to u.
points.trap: Learners forget the u.

example.es: ¿Con salsa verde o roja?
example.en: With green or red salsa?

points.point: porque for reasons; ¿por qué? to ask
points.explain: Porque (one word) answers; ¿por qué? (two words) asks.
points.trap: Mixing them in writing.

example.es: ¿Por qué te gusta? — Porque es muy tranquilo.
example.en: Why do you like it? — Because it's very peaceful.

points.point: es que … for a reason or excuse
points.explain: Es que softens a reason, especially when declining.
points.trap: Learners give a bare reason, which can sound curt.

example.es: Me encantaría, pero es que tengo que trabajar.
example.en: I'd love to, but the thing is I have to work.

points.point: cuando + past (cuando era niño…)
points.explain: Cuando with a past fact takes the indicative.
points.trap: *cuando fuera niño.

example.es: Cuando vivía en Toronto, no comía picante.
example.en: When I lived in Toronto, I didn't eat spicy food.

points.point: story connectors: de repente, entonces, luego, al final, total que
points.explain: These move a story along; total que is Mexican 'so in the end'.
points.trap: Learners chain everything with y.

example.es: Entonces se fue la luz, luego empezó a llover y total que no llegué.
example.en: Then the power went off, then it started raining, and so I never got there.

points.point: pero vs sino; aunque + indicative for known facts
points.explain: Sino corrects a negative (no es caro, sino barato).
points.trap: *no es caro pero barato.

example.es: No es caro, sino justo; aunque está un poco lejos.
example.en: It isn't expensive, it's fair, although it's a bit far.

points.point: para que + subjunctive vs para + infinitive
points.explain: Same subject: para + infinitive; different subject: para que + subjunctive.
points.trap: *para que yo descanso.

example.es: Tome esto para dormir y para que baje la fiebre.
example.en: Take this to sleep and to bring the fever down.

points.point: cuando / en cuanto / hasta que with future meaning take the subjunctive
points.explain: Time links pointing to the future take the subjunctive.
points.trap: *Cuando llegarás.

example.es: No me voy hasta que llegues.
example.en: I'm not leaving until you arrive.

points.point: aunque, antes de que, mientras: subjunctive or indicative by meaning
points.explain: Indicative for facts; subjunctive for the possible or the not-yet.
points.trap: Learners pick by the conjunction, not the meaning.

example.es: Mientras no se arregle la bomba, no hay agua; aunque ya la revisaron.
example.en: Until the pump is fixed, there's no water, even though they've already checked it.

points.point: argument connectors: por un lado / por otro, sin embargo, en cambio, por lo tanto, ya que
points.explain: These structure an argument.
points.trap: En cambio contrasts two things; sin embargo contradicts what came before.

example.es: Por un lado hay más empleo; por otro, las rentas suben. Por lo tanto, hay que regular.
example.en: On the one hand there are more jobs; on the other, rents are rising. So it needs regulating.

points.point: formal connectors: por medio de la presente, en relación con, por lo anterior
points.explain: Fixed connectors for formal letters.
points.trap: Don't use them in speech; they sound stiff.

example.es: En relación con su solicitud, por medio de la presente le informo que fue aprobada.
example.en: With regard to your application, I hereby inform you that it has been approved.

points.point: desde que + preterite (ever since)
points.explain: Desde que + preterite marks when something began.
points.trap: *desde cuando.

example.es: Desde que me caí, me duele la rodilla.
example.en: My knee has hurt ever since I fell.

points.point: siempre y cuando, a menos que, con tal de que (+ subjunctive)
points.explain: These conditional links always take the subjunctive.
points.trap: *a menos que pagas.

example.es: Le hacemos el descuento con tal de que pague de contado.
example.en: We'll give you the discount as long as you pay in cash.

points.point: si bien (although, granted that)
points.explain: Si bien concedes a point in careful argument; it takes the indicative.
points.trap: It isn't 'if well'.

example.es: Si bien el proyecto tiene ventajas, hay que pensar en los vecinos.
example.en: Although the project has advantages, we have to think of the residents.

points.point: reformulators: o sea, es decir, en otras palabras
points.explain: These restate something more clearly when mediating.
points.trap: O sea as filler is for speech; es decir works in writing too.

example.es: Lo que quiso decir es que, en otras palabras, no está de acuerdo.
example.en: What he meant was, in other words, that he doesn't agree.

points.point: ¿Mande? as the polite 'pardon?'
points.explain: ¿Mande? asks someone to repeat; ¿qué? alone can sound rude.
points.trap: Learners say ¿qué? to strangers.

example.es: ¿Mande? No le entendí.
example.en: Pardon? I didn't catch that.

points.point: questions by intonation, and question words with accents (¿cómo?, ¿de dónde?, ¿dónde?, ¿cuánto tiempo?)
points.explain: A statement becomes a question by rising intonation; question words carry an accent.
points.trap: Don't invert or add 'do': *¿Usted vive dónde? is fine, but *¿Hace usted vivir…? isn't Spanish.

example.es: ¿De dónde es? ¿Cuánto tiempo tiene aquí?
example.en: Where are you from? How long have you been here?

points.point: negation: no before the verb
points.explain: No goes before the verb (and before object pronouns).
points.trap: *Yo hablo no.

example.es: No hablo mucho español todavía.
example.en: I don't speak much Spanish yet.

points.point: tags ¿verdad? and ¿no?; ¿a poco? for surprise (understand)
points.explain: Tags check agreement; ¿a poco? means 'really?'.
points.trap: ¿A poco? isn't about smallness.

example.es: Hace calor, ¿verdad? — ¿A poco tú no tienes calor?
example.en: It's hot, isn't it? — You're seriously not hot?

points.point: double negatives (no hay nada, no vino nadie)
points.explain: When nada / nadie / nunca follow the verb, no comes before it.
points.trap: English logic says *hay nada.

example.es: No vino nadie y no hay nada de agua.
example.en: Nobody came and there's no water at all.

points.point: exclamations ¡qué + adjective! / ¡qué + noun! (¡qué padre!, ¡qué susto!)
points.explain: ¡Qué + adjective or noun! reacts with feeling.
points.trap: *¡Cómo bonito!

example.es: ¡Qué padre! ¡Qué susto me diste!
example.en: How cool! What a fright you gave me!

points.point: indirect questions with the accented question word (no sé dónde está)
points.explain: Question words keep their accent inside a sentence.
points.trap: *No sé donde está in writing.

example.es: No sé cuál colonia es mejor ni cuánto cuesta.
example.en: I don't know which neighbourhood is better or how much it costs.

points.point: story openers: fíjate que, ¿qué crees?, ¿a que no sabes…?
points.explain: Mexicans open news or a story with these hooks.
points.trap: They're not real questions; answer ¿qué? and listen.

example.es: ¿Qué crees? Fíjate que ayer me encontré a tu prima.
example.en: Guess what? Yesterday I ran into your cousin.

points.point: agreeing and disagreeing: estoy de acuerdo, tienes razón, para nada, depende
points.explain: Fixed responses for opinions.
points.trap: *Estoy de acuerdo contigo is fine; *soy de acuerdo isn't.

example.es: Tienes razón, pero depende de la colonia. — ¡Para nada!
example.en: You're right, but it depends on the neighbourhood. — Not at all!

points.point: dizque for hearsay (Mexico)
points.explain: Dizque marks something as only what people say, often doubtful.
points.trap: It isn't a typo for dice que.

example.es: Dizque mañana sí viene el plomero.
example.en: Supposedly the plumber is coming tomorrow.

points.point: relative clauses with que, donde and lo que
points.explain: Que links most clauses; donde for places; lo que for 'what' as 'the thing that'.
points.trap: *Lo cual me gusta es…

example.es: Es la colonia donde vivía y lo que más extraño es el mercado.
example.en: It's the neighbourhood where I lived, and what I miss most is the market.

points.point: clefts for focus: lo que … es, fue … el que / quien
points.explain: Clefts put one element in focus.
points.trap: The verb ser matches the tense: fue Juan el que lo dijo.

example.es: Lo que me preocupa es el costo; fue el gobierno el que lo propuso.
example.en: What worries me is the cost; it was the government that proposed it.

points.point: quoted speech in storytelling: me dice …, y yo así de …, ¿cómo que …?
points.explain: Lively stories quote directly with me dice and y yo así de.
points.trap: Learners report everything indirectly, which flattens the story.

example.es: Y me dice: «ya cerramos». Y yo así de: ¿cómo que ya cerraron?
example.en: And she goes, 'we're closed'. And I'm like, what do you mean you're closed?

points.point: complex relatives in critique: preposition + el cual / la cual, lo cual for a whole clause
points.explain: In critical writing, el cual after a preposition and lo cual for the whole previous idea keep long sentences clear.
points.trap: *que after a long preposition (*por que, *sin que) where el cual is needed; lo cual, not *que, for the whole idea.

example.es: Es una novela en la cual nada es lo que parece, lo cual la hace difícil de adaptar.
example.en: It's a novel in which nothing is what it seems, which makes it hard to adapt.

parts_of_speech.name: Register, set phrases and discourse markers

points.point: greetings by time of day; buenas as a short hello
points.explain: Buenos días until about noon, buenas tardes until dark, buenas noches for hello and goodbye.
points.trap: Buenas noches at 7 p.m. as a greeting is normal.

example.es: ¡Buenas tardes! ¿Cómo está?
example.en: Good afternoon! How are you?

points.point: courtesy chunks: con permiso, provecho, disculpe / disculpa
points.explain: Con permiso to pass or leave; provecho to people eating; disculpe to get attention.
points.trap: Perdón for 'excuse me' to pass sounds like an apology.

example.es: Con permiso. — Propio. ¡Provecho!
example.en: Excuse me. — Go ahead. Enjoy your meal!

points.point: addressing people: joven, señorita, señora, don / doña + first name
points.explain: These forms of address are polite and normal for strangers.
points.trap: Joven is used for waiters of any age.

example.es: Joven, ¿me trae la cuenta? Buenos días, doña Lupe.
example.en: Excuse me, could I have the bill? Good morning, Doña Lupe.

points.point: agreeing to a plan: sale, va, órale, está bien
points.explain: Sale and va are Mexico's everyday 'OK'.
points.trap: Spain's vale sounds foreign.

example.es: ¿Nos vemos a las seis? — ¡Sale!
example.en: See you at six? — OK!

points.point: the switch from usted to tú: wait to be offered, or ask (¿nos hablamos de tú?)
points.explain: Move to tú when invited, or ask.
points.trap: Switching on your own can sound too familiar with older people.

example.es: ¿Nos hablamos de tú? — Claro, como quieras.
example.en: Shall we use tú? — Of course, whatever you like.

points.point: phone openers: ¿bueno?, le hablo de parte de …, ¿quién habla?
points.explain: Mexicans answer the phone with ¿bueno?
points.trap: Dígame and ¿sí? sound Spanish.

example.es: ¿Bueno? — Hola, le hablo de parte de la doctora Ruiz.
example.en: Hello? — Hello, I'm calling on behalf of Dr Ruiz.

points.point: si Dios quiere / primero Dios
points.explain: Fixed phrases that hedge plans, used by believers and non-believers.
points.trap: They don't signal religious belief.

example.es: Primero Dios, nos vemos en diciembre.
example.en: God willing, we'll see each other in December.

points.point: offers with ¿gustas …? and the leaving ritual
points.explain: ¿Gustas? offers food; leaving means announcing it, thanking and saying goodbye to each person.
points.trap: Leaving without a round of goodbyes is rude.

example.es: ¿Gustas un tamal? — Gracias. Bueno, ya me voy, muchas gracias por todo.
example.en: Would you like a tamale? — Thanks. Well, I'm off, thank you for everything.

points.point: phone register: le hablo para …, ¿me comunica con …?
points.explain: Hablar = to call; ¿me comunica? asks to be put through.
points.trap: *Llamo para… is understood but le hablo is Mexican.

example.es: Le hablo para reportar una falla. ¿Me comunica con soporte?
example.en: I'm calling to report a fault. Could you put me through to support?

points.point: turn-taking in meetings: si me permiten, perdón que interrumpa, para agregar
points.explain: Phrases to take and hold the floor politely.
points.trap: Cutting in without one sounds aggressive.

example.es: Si me permiten, quisiera agregar algo.
example.en: If I may, I'd like to add something.

points.point: softeners and indirectness: cinco minutitos, un favorcito; se me hace que
points.explain: Diminutives and se me hace que soften requests and opinions.
points.trap: Cinco minutitos may mean much longer.

example.es: ¿Me haces un favorcito? Se me hace que va a llover.
example.en: Could you do me a small favour? I get the feeling it's going to rain.

points.point: formal titles and closings: Lic., Ing., Dr.; Atentamente / Atte.
points.explain: Formal letters use titles and fixed closings.
points.trap: *Sinceramente is a calque.

example.es: Estimado Lic. Pérez: … Atentamente, Ana Torres.
example.en: Dear Mr Pérez, … Yours sincerely, Ana Torres.

points.point: colloquial register and fillers: este, o sea, pues; güey (recognise)
points.explain: Fillers buy time; güey is for close friends only.
points.trap: Using güey with strangers is rude.

example.es: Este… o sea, pues sí, está chido.
example.en: Um… I mean, well yeah, it's cool.

points.point: hedging what you know: tengo entendido que, que yo sepa; hasta donde sé (c1-08)
points.explain: These hedges show that your information may be incomplete.
points.trap: Tengo entendido que takes the indicative; que yo sepa is a fixed subjunctive.

example.es: Tengo entendido que el trámite tarda un mes, pero que yo sepa no hay que ir en persona.
example.en: I understand the process takes a month, but as far as I know you don't have to go in person.

points.point: irony and albures: recognise double meanings, don't attempt them
points.explain: Mexican humour relies on irony and double meaning.
points.trap: Attempting albures as a foreigner usually backfires.

example.es: ¡Qué bonito día para quedarse en el tráfico!
example.en: What a lovely day to be stuck in traffic!

points.point: condolence and toast formulas (mi más sentido pésame; ¡salud!)
points.explain: Fixed formulas for formal occasions.
points.trap: Lo siento alone is too thin at a funeral.

example.es: Mi más sentido pésame; estamos con ustedes.
example.en: My deepest condolences; we're with you.

points.point: proverbs as fixed forms (más vale tarde que nunca)
points.explain: Proverbs are quoted whole; don't change the words.
points.trap: Translating English proverbs word for word.

example.es: Bueno, más vale tarde que nunca.
example.en: Well, better late than never.

points.point: switching register between people when mediating
points.explain: Speak usted to the official and tú to your friend in the same conversation.
points.trap: Learners stay in one register.

example.es: Licenciado, lo que mi amiga quiere decir es… — Tranquila, ya le expliqué.
example.en: Sir, what my friend means is… — Don't worry, I've explained it to him.
